We then prove that every square-integrable martingale in this smaller filtration consequently admits a unique stochastic integral representation with respect to the compensated counting process: the integrand is explicitly characterized as the conditional expectation of the Malliavin derivative, which identifies as the conditional effect of an additional accepted event on the terminal functional. Additionally, we define the mirroring counting process which counts the rejected events in the Poisson embedding procedure and we then provide an orthogonal decomposition of any martingale in the joint filtration of the accepted and rejected counting processes as a sum of a martingale in the counting filtration obtained by Poisson embedding and its mirroring martingale part on the rejected domain. Finally, we apply these results to general Hawkes processes constructed by Poisson embedding, obtaining a martingale representation and an explicit integrand formula in their natural filtration.

papers.title: Handlebodies separate elements of surface groups
papers.abstract: In this note I prove that every non-trivial element of the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface X is non-trivial in the fundamental group of some handlebody with boundary X. This result appears to be folklore. I have uploaded a proof as the result is needed in a joint project with Clement Dupont on mapping class group actions on configuration spaces.

papers.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$
papers.authors: Pawe{\l} Bor\'owka, Paolo Grossi, Anatoli Shatsila
papers.abstract: Bryan, Oberdieck, Pandharipande and Yin predicted the number of hyperelliptic curves on general abelian surfaces under a transversality condition. Some of the numbers have already been confirmed. In this paper we construct singular hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ polarised abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$ confirming a few predicted numbers, namely of (geometric) genus $g=d$ and of geometric genus $k+3$ on $(1,2k)$ and $(1,2k+1)$ polarised surfaces. Moreover, we have found that all genus 7 hyperelliptic curves on general $(1,8)$ polarised surfaces are double coverings of curves locally embedded into $(1,4)$ polarised surfaces. More interestingly, there is a unique genus 9 hyperelliptic curve (up to translation) locally embedded into a general $(1,12)$ polarised surface and it is a Klein covering of a curve locally embedded into a $(1,3)$ polarised surface.

papers.title: Steady conformally K\"{a}hler Ricci solitons with isoparametric potential
papers.abstract: We classify complete, non-compact, simply connected, irreducible four-dimensional steady gradient Ricci solitons that are globally conformally K\"ahler and have an isoparametric potential. The steady Ricci solitons are $U(2)$-invariant nuts on $\mathbb R^4$, including the Bryant and Cao solitons, and bolts on $\mathbb{S}^2 \times \mathbb R^2$ and on $\mathcal O(-m)\to\mathbb{CP}^1$. For each $m\ge3$ there is exactly one non-collapsed bolt. A key step, valid for Ricci solitons of every sign, is that away from the locally conformally flat case, the conformal factor is aligned with the potential function, which yields cohomogeneity-one symmetry.

papers.title: Linear Rank Nonincreasing and Preserving Maps between Matrix Spaces
papers.abstract: We classify linear maps $\phi$ between possibly different rectangular matrix spaces over a field $\mathbb F$ with $|\mathbb F|\ge5$ such that $\operatorname{rank} \phi(A)\le2$ whenever $\operatorname{rank} A\le2$. Every such map has one of six forms. If its image contains a matrix of rank greater than two, then $\phi(A)=MAN$ or $\phi(A)=MA^{\top}N$ for fixed matrices $M,N$. The remaining forms have images consisting entirely of matrices of rank at most two, including an exceptional form arising from $3\times3$ alternating matrices. As a consequence, we characterize linear maps preserving rank exactly two. We also prove that rank-$k$ preservation implies rank-$k$ nonincrease when $|\mathbb F|>k+2$, and that rank-$k$ nonincrease implies rank-$\ell$ nonincrease for every admissible $\ell\ge k$ when $|\mathbb F|>k+1$. The classification uses the fact that the Chow rank of the generic $3\times3$ determinant is five, connecting the rank preserver problem with product decompositions of polynomials.

papers.title: Optimal design problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian at prescribed energy level
papers.abstract: In this work we study two optimal design problems, of hard and soft obstacle type, in fractional Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. We also establish the connection between these problems, and finally we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the quotients $\Lambda_{s,\mu}(\alpha)/\mu$ with respect to the energy level $\mu$ at the endpoints $0$ and $+\infty$.

papers.title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.

papers.title: The Berger conjecture for three dimensional manifolds
papers.abstract: A conjecture of Berger says that on a simply connected manifold all of whose geodesics are closed, all unit speed geodesics have the same shortest period. In this paper we will show that the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow is free. We use symplectic geometry to investigate the topology of the quotient of the unit tangent bundle T^1M/S^1 by the S^1 action that comes from the geodesic flow. We show that this quotient admits the structure of a smooth symplectic manifold and that this symplectic manifold is symplectomorphic to S^2 \times S^2 equipped with a split form. This will enable a computation involving the Euler class of the orbibundle T^1M\rightarrow T^1M/S^1 which will lead to a solution of Berger's conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds.

papers.title: Conformal geodesics and gauged Killing-Yano forms in dimension four
papers.abstract: We study the relation between conformal geodesics and conformal Killing-Yano (CKY) 2-forms on anti-self-dual conformal manifolds of dimension 4. In the flat case, twistor quadrics determine self-dual CKY forms whose zero loci contain conformal geodesics. To extend this construction to curved manifolds, we consider self-dual 2-forms with values in a line bundle and satisfying the gauged CKY equation, coupled to connections with anti-self-dual curvature. In this way we provide a local ambient characterization of non-null conformal geodesics as zero curves of gauged CKY forms, with the curvature vanishing along these curves.

papers.title: The Table Problem for Convex Domains
papers.abstract: We prove a generalized Table Theorem for bounded convex domains in the plane. Then we prove a variation of the Table Problem for compactly supported functions on the plane. Our method is based on relating the table problem on a surface to the square peg problem for a configuration of star-shaped curves in the tangent bundle of the surface.

papers.title: Functorial Analysis of Group-Alphabet Cellular Automata
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $n\in\mathbb N$. We consider one-dimensional cellular automata of length $n$ over the alphabet $G$, with periodic boundary conditions and with local rules $\phi$ given by words. We construct a functor $F$ from $\mathbf{Grp}$, the category of groups (or any similar algebraic structure), to the category of pointed digraphs, and show its faithfulness. We introduce the image category $\mathcal C_{n,\phi}$ of state transition graphs of all such group-alphabet cellular automata, and show $F$ is an equivalence onto this category. Consequently we investigate the translation of categorical structures in $\mathbf{Grp}$ in terms of automata, and give examples of how standard methods of homological algebra may now be applied to automata. Additionally, a graph-theoretical construction of the product in $\mathcal C_{n,\phi}$ is given, together with a formula for cycle lengths and multiplicities in this product. When $G$ is abelian, further structural properties of state transition graphs follow, and we contrast these results with non-abelian counterexamples.

papers.title: Neural Network Methods in the 2BSDE Formalism for Solving the High-Dimensional Black--Scholes Equation with Transaction Costs
papers.abstract: A 2BSDE system is written down for a $(D+1)$-dimensional Black--Scholes partial differential equation (PDE) with the Leland transaction cost model which incorporates the sign of the curvature. The 2BSDE system takes input from the ``speed'' (derivative of the curvature). This system is solved using a single ResNet neural network which learns both the solution to the PDE as well as the degrees of freedom in the curvature matrix. The network is used to learn the price of derivatives such as call options and butterfly spreads on geometric baskets for $D=10,100$ achieving a time-averaged RMSE of less than $0.1$ in each case.

papers.title: CuPIQP: A Batched and Differentiable QP Solver on GPUs for Robot Learning and Control
papers.authors: Fenglong Song, Roland Schwan, Yuwen Chen, Yuning Jiang, Colin N. Jones
papers.abstract: Quadratic programs (QPs) are fundamental building blocks of many robotic tasks such as inverse kinematics, whole-body control, and model predictive control. Extending these methods to large-scale robot learning and control requires solving many QPs concurrently and, for end-to-end learning, differentiating through their solutions. Efficient batched optimization is therefore essential to bringing established model-based methods into GPU-based robotics pipelines. We present \textsc{cuPIQP}, a batched and differentiable QP solver on GPUs based on a proximal interior-point method, with unified support for dense, sparse, and multistage problems. The solver exploits parallelism across independent QPs and their internal structure while preserving per-problem numerical updates and termination decisions. Benchmarks with up to 16384 QPs per batch demonstrate solve-time speedups of up to $18.8\times$ over \textsc{Moreau} and $4.26\times$ over eight-core \textsc{PIQP}. In an end-to-end learning task, \textsc{cuPIQP} accelerates training by $4.6\times$ over \textsc{QPAX} and $7.8\times$ over \textsc{Moreau}. By reducing the computational cost, \textsc{cuPIQP} provides efficient, reusable infrastructure for integrating model-based optimization into large-scale robot learning and control.

papers.title: Erd\H{o}s--Straus Conjecture: Modular Inversion in Mordell Classes
papers.abstract: We examine modular inversion of strict Grid certificates in a ceiling continued-fraction construction for the Erd\H{o}s--Straus equation. The six Mordell classes modulo $840$ form four inversion orbits. Prime-input pattern frequencies in the pairs $121 \leftrightarrow361 $ and $289 \leftrightarrow 529$ have equal asymptotic limits for every fixed cutoff.

papers.title: Rational curves of submaximal quantum index
papers.abstract: On a complex toric surface, oriented real rational curves tangent to the toric boundary at real points are distinguished by their value of quantum index. Using variants of usual Welschinger multiplicities, G. Mikhalkin defined enumerative invariants $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ that are provided by a signed count of oriented real rational curves with given quantum index $\kappa$ and fixed tangency points on the boundary of the positive quadrant (the tangency orders being encoded by $\tilde{\Delta}$). We prove that, for most toric surfaces and tangency orders, the invariant $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ is zero in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$. This is done by enumerating tropical curves with Block--G\"ottsche multiplicities. Additionally, we prove that, in many situations, the lower bound, given by the absolute value $|W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}|$ of $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$, for the number of oriented real rational curves is not sharp close to the tropical limit in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$.

papers.title: Privacy-Constrained Function Computation in Distributed Databases
papers.abstract: Consider distributed databases that contain both sensitive (private) and non-sensitive (public) attributes. A user seeks to compute a function of public attributes and side information by interacting with the databases and downloading their responses. In this paper, we study the trade-offs among download cost, information leakage about the private attributes, and distortion between the computed function and its reconstruction, referred to as the capacity region. Our main contributions are as follows. For a single database, we provide a complete characterization of the capacity region for general discrete sources and characterize the capacity region of two different setups for Gaussian sources when the computed function is defined as the sum of the public attribute and side information. For distributed databases, we establish inner and outer bounds on the capacity region of discrete sources and we characterize the capacity region when the databases and the side information are mutually independent. As a special instance, we study lossless function computation, and results analogous to the lossy case are obtained.

papers.title: Meshless Latent Dynamics Models for Model Order Reduction of time-dependent Partial Differential Equations
papers.authors: Lorenzo Tomada, Federico Pichi, Gianluigi Rozza
papers.abstract:
Latent dynamics learning has emerged as a prominent approach for Model Order Reduction (MOR) of time-dependent, parameterized Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). Traditional autoencoder-based approaches are intrinsically tied to fixed spatial discretizations during both training and inference, motivating the development of meshless methodologies. In this context, conditioning provides a natural mechanism for representing temporal evolution through spatially continuous functions, enabling mesh-agnostic Latent Dynamics Models (LDMs).
  In this work, we introduce a unified mathematical framework for mesh-agnostic LDMs based on conditioning in Neural Fields (NeFs). Leveraging a taxonomy of conditioning mechanisms (weak, strong, and pure), we formulate meshless LDMs as NeFs conditioned on a latent state. We establish a Universal Approximation Theorem (UAT) for this class of models and analyze their stability by deriving Lipschitz bounds for different conditioning mechanisms. Our analysis reveals an expressivity--stability trade-off, providing insight into why more expressive conditioning, despite its higher representational capacity, can potentially degrade performance during temporal extrapolation. Finally, we provide a comprehensive comparison of meshless and mesh-based architectures in the continuous limit of the spatial discretization, showing that meshless models guarantee grid-independent Lipschitz bounds, unlike mesh-based counterparts.
  Our experiments across Burgers' equation, Navier--Stokes flow past a cylinder, and linear advection show that meshless LDMs can achieve predictive accuracy comparable to or better than their mesh-based counterparts while using only 2% of the trainable parameters and exhibiting nearly constant error across spatial discretizations.

papers.title: On kinetic alignment models with rough communication kernel
papers.abstract: We prove the weak maximum principle and the Cucker-Smale flocking theorem for a general class of kinetic alignment models with rough communication kernels. This includes the classical Cucker-Smale and Motsch-Tadmor systems with defining kernel $\phi$ assumed to be merely continuous or even $\phi\in L^\infty$ for solutions in the Lebesgue class $f\in L^1$. For such models the characteristic flow-map is not well-defined and therefore the classical approaches of Cucker-Smale \cite{CS2007a,CS2007b} or Ha-Liu-Tadmor \cite{HL2009,HT2008} break down. We develop a new method adopted to rough settings based on Ambrossio's probabilistic representation of solutions and construction of dynamic barriers. All proofs are performed in the framework of so called bounded communication protocols, a non-smooth variant of regular protocols introduced in \cite{Shv-CPAM, Shv-EA} and representing a broad range of models of collective dynamics.

papers.title: Box-Cone Representations of Bound-Factor RLT Constraints in Semidefinite Relaxations
papers.authors: Katherine Charbonneau, Hao Hu, Renata Sotirov
papers.abstract: Linear inequalities can generate large constraint systems in semidefinite relaxations of binary quadratic programs, making the quadratic subproblems of splitting methods expensive to solve. We develop a box-cone representation of bound-factor reformulation-linearization technique (RLT) constraints in semidefinite relaxations of binary quadratic programs. These constraints arise by multiplying each original linear inequality by every binary variable and its complement and linearizing the resulting products. Our key observation is that all products generated by one inequality share a common slack and admit an exact representation in the standard cone over the unit box. This box-cone representation processes the inequalities through independent explicit projections, without introducing a separate nonnegative slack for each scalar RLT inequality. We illustrate the computational use of the representation within standard two-block alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). The resulting subproblems require linear solves with a reusable factorization and explicit cone projections, without enlarging the semidefinite matrix. Experiments on 257 binary quadratic programs compare this implementation with SDPNAL+. A second application groups Max-Cut triangle inequalities into box cones and uses the resulting bounds within an existing branch-and-bound framework. Tests on 220 graphs show competitive performance with MADAM using only triangle cuts. Together, these applications illustrate the representation's usefulness as a building block for first-order methods.

papers.title: An explicit bound on the extremal function for complete graph minors
papers.abstract: Kostochka and Thomason independently proved that every graph with density at least $\beta\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor, for some constant $\beta$. Thomason later proved that the least such density is $(0.319\ldots+o(1))\,t\sqrt{\log t}$. However, the $o(1)$ term in this formula is not explicit, so the formula gives no bound for any specific value of $t$. The goal of this paper is a bound of the form $\beta\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ that holds for every $t$, with $\beta$ small. We prove that, for every integer $t\geqslant2$, every graph with density at least $4.5\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor.

papers.title: String-averaging bargaining in solidarity cooperative games
papers.abstract: We consider the situation that the grand set of all players, in a cooperative game in characteristic function form with a nonempty core, consists of recognizable subsets of players. The underlying assumption is that the players of each subset have something in common between themselves which is not shared by the players of other subsets. For example, the members of these subsets are distinguishable by their nationalities or by their geographic locations or by some other market-related economic or social property. In addition to the agreement of all players to play the game to reach a point in the core, the members of each subset want to steer the iterative orbit of the bargaining process to a point in the core that will reflect the strength of their solidarity within their subset. This is why we call such subsets solidarity sets. The solidarity means that players of a solidarity set are willing to participate in coalitions that include only members of their solidarity set and are not willing to participate in coalitions of other solidarity sets. The question is how can such a game be played? Is there an iterative bargaining scheme that will generate a sequence of payoffs that converges to a point in the core which reflects the solidarity of the members of the solidarity sets? We propose bargaining schemes that allow the members of each solidarity set to perform, independently from other solidarity sets and, therefore, simultaneously in time, a full but finite sweep of intercoalitional collaboration. Then the end-points of all these sweeps are combined into a single payoff vector via a convex combination wherein the coefficients of the convex combination may reflect some a priori knowledge about the relative strengths of the different solidarity sets. These bargaining schemes are applied to a new type of cooperative game that we call solidarity cooperative game (SCG).

papers.title: The complexity of tilting
papers.abstract: Many explicit constructions in algebra are not first-order definable in classical finitary logic, but are, however, definable in infinitary logic. The aim of this paper is to show how infinitary logic can be used to lift model-theoretic results in arithmetic to a quantifier-sensitive form. We apply this idea to a deep result of Jahnke and Kartas on the model theory of perfectoid fields. Our main result is that a first-order sentence $\phi$ holds in the tilt $k^{\flat}$ of a perfectoid field $k$ if and only if a certain sentence $\phi^{\natural}$ holds in a non-principal ultrapower of $k$, where $\phi^{\natural}$ does not depend on $k$ and is only slightly more complicated than $\phi$ itself. In particular, tilting preserves the L\'evy hierarchy in a precise sense. To this end, we prove that the Standard Decomposition of a valued field at a constant $t$ is infinitarily interpretable by formulas of rank at most 1.

papers.title: Stochastic Linesearch Methods for Stochastic Variational Inequality Problems: Parameter-Free Schemes and Non-Monotone Variants
papers.authors: Zhuoyu Xiao, Uday V. Shanbhag, Yue Xie
papers.abstract: Much of the existing convergence guarantees and rate statements for stochastic variational inequality (SVI) problems are limited to stochastic approximation schemes that employ constant or diminishing steplength sequences bounded by some reciprocal of the Lipschitz constant $L$ of the map. This requires both knowing such constants and may lead to debilitatingly small steplengths, afflicting the scheme with potentially poor performance. We propose a parameter-free stochastic extragradient method with periodically restarted linesearch (\textbf{SEG-LS}) for solving pseudomonotone and monotone SVI problems. The resulting stepsize sequence is neither monotone nor requires prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant $L$. We show that the iteration and sample complexities for computing a point whose residual has norm at most $\epsilon$ in expectation are $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4})$, respectively. These results improve to $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-1})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ in the monotone setting. In addition, we propose a periodically restarted biased stochastic linesearch method (\textbf{B-SLAM}) for solving non-monotone SVIs under strict copositivity. The resulting iteration and sample complexities are $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4})$, respectively. Preliminary numerics support these findings and display promise.

papers.title: Initial Subcategories via Free Presentations of the Constant Functor
papers.authors: Thomas Br\"ustle, Justin Desrochers, Samuel Leblanc
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category. We characterize the full initial subcategories of $\mathcal{C}$ as precisely those whose representables give a free presentation of the constant functor $\Delta_{\mathcal{C}}\mathbb{K}:\mathcal{C}\to\mathrm{Vect}$. Such a presentation yields a formula for the limit of any functor $\mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}$ as the kernel of a morphism between products of evaluations.
  When the linearized endomorphism ring of every object is local, we show that a minimal free presentation, whenever one exists, determines the unique minimal full initial subcategory, up to equivalence. Bass's characterization of perfect rings gives a sufficient condition for the existence of such presentations. In particular, every finite category with no nonidentity endomorphisms, such as a finite poset, contains a unique minimal initial full subcategory. In the poset case, our results recover the minimal initial subposet constructed in [BDL27] and [DL26]. When $\mathcal{C}$ is the free category on a finite quiver, we give an explicit construction of its minimal initial full subcategories, show that every such subcategory arises from this construction, and provide algorithms with time-complexity bounds.

papers.title: Stochastic and Noisy Oracles in Smooth Continuous Optimization
papers.authors: Albert S. Berahas, Liyuan Cao, Katya Scheinberg
papers.abstract: We review models of inexact computational oracles in smooth continuous optimization and their implications for the convergence, computational complexity, and attainable accuracy of optimization algorithms. We adopt a framework in which zeroth-,first-, and second-order oracles are characterized by quantitative error bounds and may accept additional control parameters that influence both their accuracy and computational cost. We introduce deterministic and stochastic oracle models and illustrate their properties through a variety of examples, including finite-difference approximations, stochastic gradients, and randomized derivative estimators. Particular attention is given to the distinction between absolute and relative errors, bias and variance, and stochastic function evaluations with independent or coupled randomness. A central theme of the review is the use of common analytical tools to recover and compare convergence and complexity guarantees under different oracle models. For deterministic and stochastic first-order methods, we show how a general descent inequality leads to complexity bounds under various assumptions on the objective function and all proposed oracle models. In the stochastic setting, we develop bounds on expected stopping times and the accuracy that can be guaranteed under different oracle conditions. We also examine the total computational complexity of algorithms relying on specific oracle constructions and briefly review models of inexact second- order information and their use in optimization algorithms.

papers.title: Robust edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz preconditioner for high-frequency Helmholtz problems
papers.authors: Shubin Fu, Shihua Gong, Guanglian Li, Yulei Liao
papers.abstract: We develop a novel hybrid Schwarz method, termed the robust edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz method (REMs-HS), for the efficient solution of high-frequency Helmholtz problems. The method combines a one-level restricted additive Schwarz preconditioner with impedance transmission conditions (RAS-imp) and an edge multiscale (EMs) coarse solver in a multiplicative way. A key ingredient of our construction is a modified impedance boundary condition (mIBC), which is imposed both on the subdomain problems and on the local problems that generate the EMs coarse space. Compared with the original impedance boundary condition, the mIBC makes the proposed method both stable and inexpensive theoretically. We prove that the resulting REMs-HS preconditioner gives rise to a uniform convergent fixed-point iteration for large wavenumbers. Moreover, the required resolution conditions are substantially relaxed. Only a mild condition on the level parameter $\ell$ of the hierarchical coarse basis $\ell>\frac{1}{2}\log_2 k$ is needed, which is markedly weaker than the conditions in previous analyses. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method for Helmholtz problems with large wavenumbers.

papers.title: Unavoidable flats in matroids excluding a uniform minor
papers.abstract: We extend a theorem of Geelen, Kroeker, and Nelson on unavoidable flats in $\operatorname{GF}(q)$-representable matroids. For all integers $1\le a\le b$ and $n\ge1$, we prove that every simple matroid of sufficiently large rank with no $U_{a,b}$-minor has a rank-$n$ flat whose restriction is free or isomorphic to a projective or affine geometry over a finite field.

papers.title: Variance Bounds and Strict Log-Concavity for Forest Coronas
papers.abstract: We prove that the size of a random independent set in every nonempty forest has variance strictly smaller than its mean at common activity $0<t\le1$. A rooted quadratic reserve gives quantitative forms of this inequality. Mean matching transfers the bounds to fixed-weight canonical completion laws, and exact binomial moments prove strict log-concavity for every forest corona and every well-covered forest. The stronger factorial normalization $((m-j)!i_j)_{j=0}^m$ is strictly log-concave; we give explicit coefficient margins, terminal sharpness, one-less smoothing, and the exact universal three-index binomial ULC prefix. An exact attachment argument doubles the rooted reserve for every nontrivial unweighted tree. For a single marked root, a square reserve holds through $\Theta=\tfrac12e^{3-2W(1/e)}$ and for every positive mark at roots of degree at most four. A stronger reserve holds through mark $15/14$. These estimates yield marked clique, adjacent-pair, and repulsive two-piece variance bounds with fixed-weight canonical transfer. Finally, arbitrary positive site activities in $[3t/4,t]$ satisfy a uniform rooted reserve on every forest. This proves strict log-concavity for weighted forest coronas with compatible base marks. An explicit weighted-star obstruction shows why an unrestricted heterogeneous extension is impossible. Complete proofs are included, together with the required classical graph characterization and variance comparison.

papers.title: Defect TQFTs, the Generalized Cobordism Hypothesis, and Algebraic $K$-Theory
papers.abstract:
By constructing a fully dualizable category $\mathrm{Bord}^{\mathcal{C}}_n$ as the left adjoint of the forgetful functor, we state a generalized cobordism hypothesis. As a corollary, we establish a generalized Pontryagin-Thom isomorphism that gives a geometric interpretation of higher algebraic $K$-theory using cobordism classes of framed manifolds and stratified spaces decorated by categorical string diagrams, which we call lasagnas. For finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, these decorations are branched local systems.
  We also examine low-dimensional representatives, including $K_1$, Steinberg-group presentations of $K_2$, and fillings related to the Steinberg relation, providing a more explicit construction of Ghys' manifold.

papers.title: Long-Time Behavior towards Generic Riemann Solutions for Radiative Euler Equations
papers.abstract:
We study the time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for the one-dimensional radiative Euler equations, where the Riemann pattern consists of a $1$-rarefaction wave, a $2$-contact discontinuity, and a $3$-shock wave. We prove that, for sufficiently small wave strengths and initial perturbations, the Cauchy problem admits a unique global solution, which converges uniformly as $t\to \infty$ to a composite wave of the $1$-rarefaction wave, $2$-viscous contact wave, and $3$-radiative shock profile with a time-dependent shift. As a key ingredient, we establish a comprehensive set of quantitative estimates for weak radiative shock profiles.
  Our proof is based on the method of $a$-contraction with shifts. In all previous applications of the $a$-contraction method to the study of long-time behavior, the proof has relied essentially on the parabolic structure provided by either viscosity or heat conduction. In this work, we extend the method to a hyperbolic-elliptic system without parabolic structure.

papers.title: Deck Reconstruction for Restricted Word Classes
papers.authors: Krishna Angal, Ruben Ascoli, Simon X. He, Xiaoyu He, Logan Post, Arker Oke Soe, Olga Zhukova
papers.abstract:
For a binary word $x\in \{0,1\}^+$, the $k$-deck of $x$ is the multiset of all length-$k$ subsequences counted with multiplicity. The deck reconstruction problem asks for the minimum $k$ such that every word of a fixed length is uniquely determined by its $k$-deck. In this paper, we study deck reconstruction for several restricted classes of binary words, including words with exactly $s$ ones, words with at most $\ell$ runs of ones, and words where the indices of ones are given by a monotone polynomial of degree $d$. We prove that for these classes of words, their reconstruction thresholds are bounded by a function of the structural complexity of the class.
  We also study weak deck reconstruction, in which subwords may contain "wildcard" symbols that map to either 0 or 1. By generalizing a "template lemma" of Dud\'ik and Schulman, we improve the upper bound in an open question about weak reconstruction from Dud\'ik and Schulman. Finally, for the class of periodic words with period $d$, we prove that its in-class reconstruction threshold is equal to the general reconstruction threshold for words of length $d$, and give a general template construction producing further classes with the same threshold-preservation phenomenon.

papers.title: Clusters of primes revisited
papers.abstract: We revisit the generalized Rayleigh quotient optimization problem related to the Maynard-Tao sieve with the goal of finding a more efficient function basis. We demonstrate that a family based on products of reciprocals, previously used in asymptotic estimates for $H_m = \liminf_{n \to \infty}(p_{n+m}-p_n)$, provides results that are close to the theoretical limits of the sieve across many regimes. In particular, we establish $H_2 \leq 31 \, 140$, $H_3 \leq 2 \, 560 \, 022$, $H_4 \leq 193 \, 672 \, 056$, and $H_5 \leq 13 \, 659 \, 045 \, 840$. We also show that, as $k \to \infty$, the related variational quantity $M_k$, introduced by Maynard, satisfies the lower bound $M_k \geq \log k - 0.273572 + o(1)$.

papers.title: A spectral theory of zeta functions of function fields
papers.abstract: We study Hilbert spaces constructed from the Weil quadratic form associated with the zeta function of a curve over a finite field, together with self-adjoint extensions of the differentiation operator on these spaces. For a distinguished family of these extensions, we prove that the eigenvalues converge to the ordinates of the zeros of the zeta function and that the corresponding entire spectral functions, after normalization, converge locally uniformly to an infinite product determined by these zeros. These limits occur as the interval parameter approaches a finite endpoint, rather than infinity as in the setting of the Riemann zeta function. We also realize the global Hilbert space through the Rosati trace pairing and show that translation by $\log q$ is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by normalized Frobenius. This provides a geometric model for the analogous analytic constructions associated with the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: Derived products and top-degree inverse limits
papers.abstract: We compute top derived products and inverse limits on products of affine lines with doubled origin over $B[s]$, for any nonzero commutative ring $B$. For every $B$-module $M$, the two top obstruction modules fit into an explicit exact sequence and contain $M^{\mathbb N}/M^{(\mathbb N)}$as a natural $B$-module direct summand.This gives exact product dimensions, sharp vanishing bounds for inverse sequences, and faithfulness in the coefficient module. For a Grothendieck category of finite product dimension, we also obtain degree shifts under adjoining commuting locally nilpotent endomorphisms and prove that this construction preserves top-degree vanishing for epimorphic inverse sequences. A fixed Gabriel--Popescu presentation then describes the general top obstruction through actual Ext sequences and separates two module-theoretic terms.

papers.title: Circular regular dessins with underlying graphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$: the metacyclic case
papers.abstract: A dessin is a 2-cell embedding of a connected bipartite graph into an orientable closed surface. It is regular if the colour- and orientation-preserving automorphism group acts regularly on edges, and circular if every face boundary is a simple cycle. We classify and enumerate circular regular dessins of the complete bipartite multigraph ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$ ($e\ge f\ge 2$, $d\ge 1$) whose automorphism group is {\it metacyclic}. This extends the work of Fan (circular, metacyclic) and Cai--Hu (regular, metacyclic) from simple graphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}$ to multigraphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$. Such dessins correspond to non-exact bicyclic factorisations $G=\l a\r\l b\r\cong\ZZ_{2^{e+d}}\ZZ_{2^{f+d}}$, where $\l a\r\cap\l b\r\cong\ZZ_{2^d}$ and $\l ba\r\cap \l a\r=\l ba\r\cap \l b\r=1$. In general, a group admitting such a factorisation need not be metacyclic; in this paper we impose the additional condition that $G$ is a metacyclic 2-group. Under this assumption, we obtain explicit enumeration formulas for the number of such dessins up to isomorphism. Together with the known classifications for simple graphs (the case $d=0$), this completes the enumeration of the metacyclic case for 2-power complete bipartite multigraphs.

papers.title: Bounds for lattice points in terms of volume and successive minima
papers.abstract: We prove, in every dimension, the upper bound conjectured by Betke, Henk and Wills for the lattice-point enumerator in terms of volume and successive minima. For every convex body $K\subset R^n$ and full-rank lattice $\Lambda$, we establish $$ \#(K\cap\Lambda)\le\frac{\mathrm{vol}_n(K)}{\det\Lambda}\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1+\frac{i\lambda_i}{2}\right), $$ where $\lambda_i$ are the successive minima of $(K-K)/2$ with respect to $\Lambda$. Equality holds precisely for lattice translates of positive integral dilates of unimodular simplices. We also prove $$ \#(\mathrm{int}K\cap\Lambda)\ge\frac{\mathrm{vol}_n(K)}{\det\Lambda} \left(1-\frac{n}{4}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\lambda_i-\frac{n}{2}\lambda_n\right), $$ which implies the lower estimate with factor $1-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n i\lambda_i$. In dimension two we prove the lower bound with factor $(1-\lambda_1/2)(1-\lambda_2)$ when $\lambda_2\le1$. We also observe that a conjectured product lower bound for origin-symmetric bodies fails in dimension three. The proofs combine geometric compression, lattice-cell counts in coordinate sections, and an elementary coefficient comparison.

papers.title: Strong solvability and its failure for critical SDEs
papers.abstract:
We revisit the construction of strong solutions to singular SDEs by compactness on Wiener space. For spatially varying diffusion coefficients, assuming sufficiently small form bounds on the drift and diffusion gradient, we use basic energy estimates and an extended compactness criterion for Wiener functionals to construct an approximation-independent stochastic flow of homeomorphisms. Both forward and inverse maps have local Sobolev moment bounds, and the resulting strong solutions are pathwise unique in a class of solutions satisfying a Krylov estimate.
  We also show that the endpoint critical condition $b\in L^\infty_tL^d_x$, together with $\mathrm{div } b=0$ does not guarantee the existence of a strong solution. For every $d\geq2$, we construct a SDE with a divergence-free drift in this class and an additive Brownian noise, started from the origin, has a weak solution unique in law, but no strong solution. The proof uses logarithmic rescaling to characterize strong solvability by whether the sample measures of an associated stationary diffusion are Dirac masses. Positivity of the top Lyapunov exponent, combined with random SRB theory, rules out this concentration and hence strong solvability.

papers.title: Weil Operators and Remainders of Anderson Generating Functions over a Punctured Projective Line
papers.authors: Chuangqiang Hu, Xiao-Min Huang, Guorui Ma
papers.abstract: Let $A_\rho$ be the coordinate ring of the projective line over $\Fq$ with a closed point of degree $N$ removed. We give finite formulas for higher Weil operators in a basis of Riemann--Roch spaces, which recover the formulas of Hu--Ou--Yang when $N=1$. We identifythese operators with representatives of the residue Casimir tensors and obtain a determinant formula for the Weil pairing, relative to a chosen determinant realization. For a normalized rank-one Drinfeld module, we compute the remainder of its Anderson generating function modulo any nonconstant $p\in A_\rho$. The formula includes multiple zeros and a zero at the ordinary point at infinity. Its last coefficient is a nonzero scalar multiple of an exponential division value. When $(p)$ is a finite principal prime, a value of the associated special function at one zero of $p$ generates the torsion field after adjoining that zero. We give an explicit $q$-linear formula recovering a torsion generator from this value. We also specialize the evaluation theorem of Gazda--Maurischat and compute the different as the principal ideal $(\partial_xp)$.

papers.title: Nonexistence of Stable Solutions to the Liouville Equation on Graphs with Polynomial Volume Growth
papers.abstract: We study stable solutions of the discrete Liouville equation \[ -\Delta u=e^u \] on infinite, locally finite graphs with polynomial volume growth. We prove that no stable solution exists whenever the order $d$ of polynomial volume growth satisfies $d<10$.

papers.title: Turnpike Properties for Exploratory Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Indefinite Cost Functionals
papers.authors: Yaohua Hu, Zhaoqing Li, Hanxiao Wang, Jie Xiong
papers.abstract: Continuous-time exploratory stochastic control provides a stochastic control framework for the exploration--exploitation trade-off in reinforcement learning. In this paper, we study the long-time behavior of finite-horizon exploratory stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) optimal control problems as the time horizon $T\to\infty$, and establish so-called turnpike properties for such problems. In the finite-horizon setting, we derive a feedback representation of the exploratory stochastic LQ problem and analyze its long-time structure. We formulate an exploratory static distribution optimization problem analogous to the classical static optimization problem and identify the corresponding static reference object. We prove a turnpike property for the optimal state process relative to a stochastic reference process, as well as a Wasserstein turnpike property for the optimal control distribution. In addition to the exploratory control formulation, another key feature of our results is that, by introducing a joint coercivity condition, we allow the cost functional to be indefinite and the controlled state system to be merely stabilizable. Consequently, the derived turnpike property is novel even within the classical stochastic LQ control framework.

papers.title: Koopman--Lyapunov and Koopman--Riccati Controller Synthesis
papers.abstract: While the Koopman operator-based lifted representations of nonlinear autonomous and controlled systems have been well covered in the literature, the direct controller synthesis problem largely remains open. As the controlled system is generally a bilinear (instead of fully linear) Koopman model, controller synthesis appears to lose the linear--quadratic structures of the classical Lyapunov and Riccati methods for finite-dimensional linear systems. However, in infinite dimensions, bilinearity in the feature map should be merely artifactual and hence reducible to linearity in principle. In this work, by considering the operator semigroups in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space with a linear--Sobolev kernel and utilizing the Yosida approximation of their generators, the synthesis problems of a stabilizing controller and an input-unconstrained optimal controller can be formulated as an operator Lyapunov inequality and an operator Riccati equation, respectively. These formulations recover the desirable linear--quadratic structures, and hence, with sample data, they are solvable efficiently in analogous ways to usual linear systems by semidefinite programming solvers and Kleinman iterations, respectively. In addition to proving control performance bounds dependent on the sampling denseness and Yosida regularization, through numerical comparison to linearized LQR, bilinear EDMD-based synthesis, nonlinear MPC, and Koopman MPC methods on numerical models and process control examples, this work demonstrates the proposed Koopman--Riccati synthesis as a computationally efficient approach to obtain a near-optimal state-feedback control law.

papers.title: On the Communication-Sensing Tradeoff in DMT-Optimal Space-time-Coded ISAC Systems
papers.authors: Wei-Chen Chen, Yu-Chih Huang, Ming-Chun Lee
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) has been extensively studied from the perspective of communication-sensing performance tradeoffs. In MIMO communication systems, the diversity-multiplexing tradeoff (DMT) fundamentally characterizes the tradeoff between communication reliability and multiplexing gain, and DMT-optimal space-time codes achieve this optimal tradeoff without instantaneous channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT), making them particularly attractive for ISAC scenarios where accurate CSIT is difficult to acquire or maintain. In this work, we propose an analytical framework for characterizing the sensing behavior and communication-sensing gain tradeoff of DMT-optimal space-time codes in ISAC systems. Under a single-target detection model, we propose the sensing diversity order as the high-SNR sensing reliability metric. We further show that a class of DMT-optimal space-time codes, exemplified by Perfect codes, eliminates sensing blind spots for all nonzero codewords, thereby achieving joint DMT-sensing-diversity (DMTS) optimality. Furthermore, using the Perfect code as a representative DMT-optimal construction, we show that its isotropic average transmit covariance limits the achievable sensing gain when the target angular region is narrow. We therefore develop a full-rank spatial precoding framework and a low-complexity surrogate precoder that preserve joint DMTS optimality while shaping the transmit beampattern. Simulation results show that, for a target angular region of $\theta\in[-\pi/10,\pi/10]$, the proposed design achieves approximately 3 dB sensing-gain improvement over the unprecoded Perfect code.

papers.title: Critical Optimizers for the Finite-Rank Fractional Lieb--Thirring Inequality
papers.abstract: We study optimal potentials for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring problem at the eigenvalue-counting endpoint, for \(0<s<1\) and \(d>2s\). Using the zero-energy Birman--Schwinger formulation, we prove a profile decomposition of normalized optimizing sequences with exact splitting of rank and potential mass, and strong approximation in \(L^{d/(2s)}\). Strict subadditivity yields existence and compactness modulo translations and dilations. At rank two, the optimal constant equals the rank-one constant, the supremum is not attained, and every normalized optimizing sequence splits into two Sobolev potentials. We also prove strict increase of the minimal potential masses and a uniform spectral gap for optimizing sequences. For each optimizer, we derive an Euler--Lagrange system and establish boundedness, local H\"older regularity and \(V(x)=|x|^{-4s}(c_\infty+o(1))\) as \(|x|\to\infty\), with \(c_\infty\geq0\). The conformal orbit of every optimizer contains a representative with a strictly positive asymptotic coefficient.

papers.title: Smith Algebra from $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Tensor Product Branching via the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko Algebra
papers.authors: Kohei Hasegawa, Takuya Matsumoto, Akito Takashima
papers.abstract: Let $L_n$ be the finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $n$. We study the space of highest-weight vectors in $L_n\otimes L_m$ for the diagonal $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action. The extremal projector constructs these singular vectors and gives operators connecting the highest-weight lines in the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition. We interpret these operators in the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko algebra of the diagonal pair $(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2, \mathfrak{sl}_2^{\mathrm{diag}})$. A rescaling of their quadratic relation yields the cubic Smith relation $[E,F]=2(H^3-cH)$. This cubic algebra is also known as a Higgs algebra in the physics literature. We express both the central parameter $c$ and the Smith Casimir in terms of the quadratic $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Casimir elements of the two tensor factors. The singular subspace becomes an irreducible Smith module of dimension $\min\{n,m\}+1$, with explicit formulas for the actions of the raising and lowering operators $E$ and $F$. Finally, comparison with finite-dimensional simple Smith modules gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a module to arise from this tensor-product construction.

papers.title: Solyanik Estimates for Ergodic Flows
papers.abstract: Let $\{T_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a measure-preserving flow on a probability space $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$ and let $T^*$ be the associated one-sided ergodic maximal operator. We show that the sharp Tauberian constant $C(\alpha)=\sup_{\mu(E)>0}\frac{\mu(\{T^*\chi_E>\alpha\})}{\mu(E)}$,$0<\alpha<1$, equals $1/\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$, unless every measurable set is invariant modulo null sets, in which case $C(\alpha)=1$ for every $\alpha$. In particular the Solyanik estimate $\lim_{\alpha\to1^-}C(\alpha)=1$ holds for every measure-preserving flow, and for ergodic flows on nonatomic spaces the estimate $C(\alpha)-1\le 1/\alpha-1$ holds with equality. This answers the one-parameter case of a question of Hagelstein and Parissis. The main point is the lower bound, which is obtained from a lacunary cross-section built out of the upcrossings of a probe function along the orbits of the flow.

papers.title: Dilation systems with two generators and the optimal Riesz bounds of a basis of ReLU networks
papers.authors: Jorge Antezana, Daniel Carando, Tom\'as Fern\'andez Vidal, Melisa Scotti
papers.abstract: For two $1$-periodic functions $\psi_1,\psi_2\in L^2(0,1)$ with mean zero we characterize when $\{1\}\cup\{\psi_1(\alpha\cdot x),\psi_2(\alpha\cdot x)\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}^d,\,\alpha\succ0}$ is a Riesz basis of $L^2([0,1]^d)$, in terms of a $2\times2$ matrix of Dirichlet series, and we compute its optimal bounds. The tool is a $2\times2$ matrix version of the theorem of Hedenmalm, Lindqvist and Seip for systems of dilations with two generators, proved through the reproducing kernel of the Hardy space of the infinite polydisk. In particular, we get the optimal bounds $2/3$ and $3/2$ for $\psi_1,\psi_2$ the triangle waves considered by Daubechies, DeVore, Foucart, Hanin and Petrova in $L^2(0,1)$, and the extended version in $L^2([0,1]^d)$ defined by Schneider and Vyb\'iral.

papers.title: Changing parameters in Hall-Littlewood functions
papers.authors: Aritra Bhattacharya, Ziyi Dai, Qilin Hou, Edward Tong
papers.abstract: We study the transition coefficients $b_{\lambda,\mu}(q,t)$ of the Hall--Littlewood $P$-functions $P_\lambda(t)$ expanded in the basis $P_\mu(q)$. We find a tableaux formula when $\lambda$ is a hook shape which generalizes term-by-term Lascoux-Schutzenberger's charge formula as well as Macdonald's monomial expansion formula for Hall-Littlewood functions. We conjecture that $b_{\lambda,\mu}(t+1,t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ and prove it when $\lambda$ is a hook shape, when $\lambda$ has two-columns and some more simple cases. We prove that $b_{\lambda,\mu}(t+n,n)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$, extending work of Alexandersson, and we record a stability property and some reduction principles.

papers.title: Sharp Solyanik Estimates for Discrete and Ergodic Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operators
papers.abstract: Let $U_1,\dots,U_n$ be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of a probability space, and let $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)$ denote the sharp Tauberian constant of the associated ergodic uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator. Hagelstein and Parissis showed that $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)-1\lesssim_n(1/\alpha-1)^{1/(n(n+1))}$ as $\alpha\to1^-$ and asked whether this exponent is sharp. We prove that $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)-1\lesssim_n(1/\alpha-1)^{1/n}$ for all such transformations, and that this is sharp: equality of the ergodic and discrete Tauberian constants holds for every action admitting arbitrarily large Rokhlin towers (in particular for every free action, ergodic or not), and the discrete constant satisfies $\widetilde{C}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)-1\asymp_n(1/\alpha-1)^{1/n}$. For $n\ge2$ the sharp ergodic exponent $1/n$ is strictly smaller than the sharp Euclidean exponent $2/(n+1)$ recently obtained by Mukherjee; the discrepancy is caused by a lattice ``first layer'' effect. We also show that the discrete Tauberian constants of the Hardy--Littlewood and strong maximal operators dominate their Euclidean counterparts; for the strong maximal operator this yields $C^{*}_{\mathrm{S}}=C_{\mathrm{S}}$ for every free action.

papers.title: An atomic approach to Shokurov's conic-bundle conjecture
papers.authors: Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, Ludmil Katzarkov, Daniel Pomerleano, Zhijia Zhang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply a weaker version of Hodge atoms to show that a standard conic bundle over a smooth complex projective rational surface $S$ is irrational if $|2K_S+\Delta|\ne\emptyset$, where $\Delta$ is the discriminant divisor. This proves Shokurov's conjecture on rationality of conic bundle threefolds. As an application, we deduce precisely which nodal quartic double solids are rational.

papers.title: Only constant mean curvature surfaces in $E(\kappa,\tau)$, $\tau\ne0$, have a holomorphic original Abresch-Rosenberg differential
papers.abstract:
For immersed surfaces in the homogeneous spaces $E(\kappa,	au)$ with $	au
e0$, we prove that the original Abresch--Rosenberg differential $[2(H+i	au)p-(\kappa-4	au^2)A^2]\,d\zeta^2$ is holomorphic if and only if the mean curvature $H$ is constant; here $p\,d\zeta^2$ is the Hopf differential and $A=\langle\xi,\partial_\zetaangle$. The result is local: no completeness, compactness or analyticity is assumed, and there are no exceptional surfaces. Where $dH

e0$, where the statement fails, we show that a non-CMC surface with holomorphic original differential has nowhere vanishing $dH$ and constant angle function, and belongs to an explicit family; in particular, closed surfaces with holomorphic original differential are CMC there. We also show that the Hopf-cylinder alternative in a theorem of Dorfmeister, Inoguchi and Kobayashi contains no non-CMC surface.

papers.title: Filtration theorems, Hilbert functions, and generic freeness
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a finitely generated module over a ring $R$ that is a finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring $A$ by $r$ elements. We prove that there are finitely many primes $P_1, \ldots, P_k$ of $A$ such that $M$ has a countable ascending filtration by finitely generated $A$-modules with the property that every factor $F_n$ has a filtration by cyclic modules of the form $A/P_i$, $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that the number of copies $H_i(n)$ of $A/P_i$ that occur in the filtration of $F_n$ is an eventually polynomial function of $n$. We prove a number of bounds on the degrees of these eventually polynomial functions: $r-1$ is always a bound, and the dimension of $\dim(M_P)-1$ is a bound under mild hypotheses. One application is an immediate proof Grothedieck's classic theorem on generic freeness. Several other applications are given.

papers.title: Algebraic Vector Fields of Connected Semi-simple Matrix Groups are 3-generated
papers.abstract: We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields for any connected, semi-simple matrix group over $\mathbb{F}$, for $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}$, can be generated by three $\mathbb{F}$-complete algebraic vector fields.

papers.title: Rainbow Hamiltonian paths in graph collections under edge-size conditions
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{n-1}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct graphs of order $n$ on the same vertex set $V$. A path $P$ with $V(P)\subseteq V$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $\phi\colon E(P)\to [n-1]$ such that $e\in E(G_{\phi(e)})$ for each $e\in E(P)$. In this paper, we show that if $n\ge3$, $e(G_i)> \binom{n-2}{2}+2$ for each $i\in[n-1]$ and $G_j$ is connected for some $j\in[n-1]$, then there exists a rainbow Hamiltonian path in $\mathbf{G}$ unless $n=6$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{5}\cong K_2\vee 4K_1$, or $n=8$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{7}\cong K_3\vee 5K_1$. This corrects Theorem 6 in [Graphs Combin., \textbf{41}(6)(2025), 119] and relaxes its hypothesis from requiring all $G_i$ to be connected to only requiring that at least one $G_i$ is connected, where $i\in[n-1]$. Moreover, we show that if $n\ge2$ and $e(G_i)\ge \binom{n-1}{2}$ for each $i\in[n-1]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ contains a rainbow Hamiltonian path unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{n-1}\cong K_{n-1}\cup K_1$, or $n=4$ with $G_1=G_2=G_3\cong K_{1,3}$. As a consequence, Theorem 2 of [Discrete Math., \textbf{347}(2024), 114128] follows immediately.

papers.title: On hot spots of the torsion function and the ground state of the Laplacian
papers.authors: Jiaxin He, Qinfeng Li, Shangfeng Wu, Shuangquan Xie
papers.abstract:
We compare the maximum points \(P_\Omega\) and \(Q_\Omega\) of the
  torsion function and the positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction. We begin with a systematic analytic description of both
  hot spots over the full range of opening angles of circular sectors: uniqueness,
  strict monotonicity with respect to the angle, distinct
  small-angle asymptotics, and explicit limiting equations in the
  slit-disk limit. We also prove the existence of a coincidence angle and establish arithmetic
  properties of the limiting coordinates. We then consider bounded convex planar domains with a line of symmetry, and we prove the sharp diameter-normalized identity
  \[
  \sup_\Omega
  \frac{|P_\Omega-Q_\Omega|}{\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)}=\frac12.
  \]
  Its upper-bound argument uses standard localization in the heart and
  an elementary geometric enclosure. Sharpness follows from thin convex
  domains with a vanishing relative width perturbation peaking near one
  endpoint: the torsion hot spot approaches that endpoint, whereas the
  ground-state hot spot approaches the midpoint.

papers.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of Schr\"{o}dinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
papers.abstract: We establish improved local smoothing estimates for the Schr\"odinger equation on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

papers.title: DistFlow and Its Conic Relaxation: Regularity, Monotonicity, and Hybrid Exactness via Graph Decomposition
papers.abstract: Classical exactness conditions for conic relaxations of the DistFlow model rely, among other assumptions, either on all nodal injections being adjustable or on a network-wide path condition. In practice, these conditions may not hold uniformly across a feeder: controllable distributed energy resources (DERs) sit at some buses and fixed loads at others, while reverse flows from DER-rich regions can violate the path condition. This paper certifies exactness region by region and composes the regional certificates, accounting for perturbations that propagate downstream through voltages. We first introduce a subtree voltage stability region, in which the network and all compatible subtrees remain regular. Within it, two endpoint sign conditions, one relaxing the nonnegative-flow assumption and one implied by the classical path condition, yield monotone responses of voltages, currents, and losses to root voltages. Using duality, the implicit function theorem, and sign properties of inverse sensitivity matrices, we recast both classical arguments as individual sign certificates on branch multipliers. This turns exactness into a branchwise property that can be certified region by region. A partition rule then splits the network into dispatchable and passive subtrees, and a hybrid certificate combines their local conditions into exactness of the full-network relaxation, under additional operating-limit and objective conditions. In particular, placing controllable DERs at both ends of a branch with large reverse flow exempts that branch from the passive sign conditions.

papers.title: Positive Values of Inhomogeneous Quadratic Forms of Type (1, 4): The Constant \Gamma_{1,4} = 8
papers.abstract: Let Q be a real indefinite quadratic form of type (1, 4) with determinant D \neq 0. We prove that for every c \in \mathbb{R}^5 there exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^5 such that 0 < Q(x + c) \le (8|D|)^{1/5}, and that the constant 8 is optimal. This establishes a conjecture of Bambah, Dumir and Hans-Gill and, together with earlier work, completes the determination of the sharp constants \Gamma_{r,s} for positive inhomogeneous values of nondegenerate indefinite quadratic forms. The proof combines classical reduction and gap theorems with uniform bounds for circular gaps of quadratic residues. A central step identifies the exceptional parameters in certain resonant reduced families: an explicit ladder of integer witnesses resolves their punctured neighbourhoods, leaving only three rational parameter points, subject to stated coefficient conditions. These are treated by retaining the coupling in a preceding, less reduced form. The remaining covering statements are verified by finite certificates in exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Orientations for skein-valued curve counting
papers.abstract:
Ekholm and Shende's skeins-on-branes formalism provides invariant counts of holomorphic curves with boundary on a Maslov zero Lagrangian within a Calabi-Yau 3-fold. This paper proves the orientation relations required for worldsheet skein relations to cancel codimension-one boundary strata. However, standard Cauchy-Riemann Fredholm orientations reveal an unexpected sign puzzle: the orientation relation at a curve with a hyperbolic boundary crossing depends on whether the crossing lies on distinct boundary components or the same component. This domain-dependent sign contradicts the uniform crossing relations of the HOMFLYPT skein algebra. We show that this discrepancy is resolved by passing to an anti-holomorphic orientation convention.
  We establish all required orientation comparisons in the general setting of an oriented Lagrangian submanifold of a 6-dimensional symplectic manifold.

papers.title: Efficient Importance Sampling of Brownian Motion Avoiding Poissonian Obstacles for Long Time
papers.authors: Jose Blanchet, Paul Dupuis, Hao Liu
papers.abstract: We design and analyze an efficient importance sampling estimator of the probability that, over a long time horizon, a Brownian particle avoids obstacles of a fixed radius placed according to an independent Poisson random field. Donsker and Varadhan identify the exponential decay rate of this probability as the optimal balance between the volume cleared of obstacles and the spectral cost of confinement, and the confinement results of Sznitman and Povel show that the particle survives by localizing its path in a ball of (roughly) deterministic radius but with a random center. This strategy makes direct Monte Carlo exponentially ineffective over long horizons, and makes a practical yet asymptotically optimal sampler non-trivial to design, since the sampler must track the random region swept out by the path. For every fixed dimension \(d\ge2\) and every fixed obstacle radius, we construct a sequential importance sampler that is unbiased and asymptotically optimal. The full algorithm has finite expected total work at every fixed horizon, and both its expected work and the coefficient of variation grow at most subexponentially with the time horizon. The method avoids repeatedly solving eigenvalue problems on the evolving explored regions and suits parallel implementation. Numerical experiments illustrate the efficiency of the method.

papers.title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
papers.abstract:
Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$.
  The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $\iota_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincar\'e duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.

papers.title: A Good-Vorticity Low-Regularity Integrator for the Inviscid Oldroyd--B System with Stress Diffusion
papers.authors: Xinyu Cheng, Zhaonan Luo, Zhaojie Yang, Cheng Yuan
papers.abstract: We establish sharp convergence results for a sequential semi-implicit good-vorticity integrator for the two-dimensional inviscid Oldroyd--B system with stress diffusion on the torus. For exact solutions satisfying $u\in C_tB^{1+\alpha}_{\infty,1}$ and $\tau\in C_tB^\alpha_{\infty,1}\cap L^1_tB^{2+\alpha}_{\infty,1}$, $0\le\alpha\le2$, we prove convergence in the critical norms $B^1_{\infty,1}\times B^0_{\infty,1}$, uniformly over the time nodes on every finite interval where these regularity assumptions hold, including the critical endpoint $\alpha=0$. For $0<\alpha\le2$, we obtain the rate $O(h^{\alpha/2})$ without any additional time H\"older assumption, reaching first order at $\alpha=2$. These algebraic exponents are optimal for this Eulerian scheme over the stated solution classes, as shown by fixed-data lower bounds in the case $a=b=0$ with nonzero velocity mean. For a fixed shear solution at critical regularity, we establish matching logarithmic upper and lower bounds on the numerical error, ruling out every positive algebraic convergence rate. We also prove that the gain of one stress derivative at the time nodes is optimal when the velocity is controlled in $B^1_{\infty,1}$, even for smooth initial stress.

papers.title: Stochastic Mirror Descent under Dependent Observations
papers.authors: Gersende Fort, Anatoli Juditsky, Jiaming Liang
papers.abstract: We study the non-asymptotic convergence of Stochastic Mirror Descent (SMD) algorithm when the noisy first-order oracle is driven by dependent observations. Departing from the classical i.i.d. assumption underlying most existing guarantees, we introduce a flexible ``forgetting" condition that accommodates geometrically or polynomially dependent sequences. Under this condition we derive explicit finite-sample accuracy bounds for the averaged SMD iterates, recovering the classical $O(1/T)$ and $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ rates in the large- and small-initial-error regimes. We instantiate the general framework on two applications: high-dimensional linear regression with dependent regressors and nonparametric estimation of the drift function of a functional autoregressive model.

papers.title: POST-MIMO: Partition-Oriented Semantic Transmission for MIMO Point Cloud Delivery
papers.authors: Hang Yue, Junlin Chang, Tianqing Zhao, Yulin Zhao, Rongke Liu
papers.abstract: Point clouds have become a fundamental data format for emerging three dimensional (3D) applications, while their wireless delivery remains challenging due to the large data volume and irregular geometric structure. Existing semantic point cloud transmission methods are mainly developed for single-input single-output systems, making them difficult to apply directly to multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To address this issue, we propose a partition-oriented semantic transmission framework for MIMO (POST-MIMO) point cloud delivery. POST-MIMO partitions the input point cloud into spatially coherent blocks and aligns them with parallel MIMO streams. Based on this block-aligned representation, the transmitter employs a hierarchical encoder to capture both intra-block local geometry and inter-block global dependency, while the auxiliary side information is transmitted jointly to assist reconstruction. At the receiver, a progressive decoder reconstructs the block geometry in a progressive manner and restores the final point cloud with block-aware adjustment. Experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction quality and lower computational resource consumption than representative reference schemes under the considered MIMO setting.

papers.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 3: expectation under a general distribution
papers.abstract: For multinomial counts $X\sim\operatorname{Mult}(N;\mathbf p)$ on $n$ ordered bins and a reference law $\mathbf r$ we study the expectation of the reference-centered discrete total variation $d_{\mathbf r}(X)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|(X_{j+1}-Nr_{j+1})-(X_j-Nr_j)|$, the natural extension of the comb-test statistic to a non-uniform null. For a non-uniform null the raw total variation of the counts carries a deterministic staircase of order $N$ that no centering of the statistic removes; the counts are therefore centered at the reference law, and under the null ($\mathbf p=\mathbf r$) the statistic is the matched $d_{\mathbf p}$. Exact finite-sample expectations are obtained by conditioning on the total mass in each adjacent pair, which reduces every edge to a translated binomial absolute-deviation problem. For fixed $n\ge3$ and a sampling law bounded away from the boundary of the simplex, the matched statistic admits a three-term asymptotic expansion in powers of $1/N$ whose coefficients are explicit continuous periodic functions of $N(p_{j+1}-p_j)$ (a generalized, non-Poincar\'e asymptotic expansion), obtained by a weighted local Edgeworth estimate and a corner Euler--Maclaurin summation; all half-integer orders vanish by parity. Each correction separates into a smooth Edgeworth part and an oscillatory lattice part, the latter an Edgeworth perturbation of one formal Euler--Maclaurin series of a Gaussian lattice sum. Under a sampling law $\mathbf p\neq\mathbf r$ the leading expectation is the folded-normal profile implied by the central limit theorem; under local alternatives we identify the $O(1)$ correction (a skewness term, plus a variance-gradient term for Pitman alternatives), and fixed alternatives give a law-of-large-numbers limit, the $\ell_1$ distance between the adjacent-gradient profiles of $\mathbf p$ and $\mathbf r$, on which threshold tests are consistent.

papers.title: A note on decompositions into 3-chromatic graphs
papers.authors: Bertille Granet, Daniel Horsley, Jeffrey N. Santrio
papers.abstract: Delcourt and Postle recently introduced the `discharging in the dual' proof technique, leading to a breakthrough proof of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions. Independently, and almost simultaneously, the first and second authors built on the `condensation' method of Bryant, Dukes, Horsley, Maenhaut and Montgomery to determine the decomposition threshold of all odd cycles of length at least $73$. In this note, we explain how the `discharging in the dual' and `condensation' methods can be combined to determine the decomposition threshold of cycles of any odd length, as well as the approximate decomposition threshold of a range of other $3$-chromatic graphs.

papers.title: Dimension Changes the Scale-Signal Channel in Nearest-Neighbor Two-Sample Testing
papers.abstract: Nearest-neighbor two-sample tests are often analyzed with dimension fixed. We study the power of the generalized edge-count test on a directed 1-nearest-neighbor graph. This statistic combines a weighted sum and a difference of the two within-sample edge counts. For balanced isotropic Gaussian samples with $d/\log N\to\gamma>0$, we derive the connection probabilities under local location and scale alternatives. Under location alternatives, the two counts have equal mean shifts, which cancel in their difference. Under scale alternatives, the two counts instead have mean shifts of opposite signs. We also derive the growth rate of the null expectation $\mathbb{E}_0C_3$, where $C_3$ counts pairs of directed edges sharing exactly one vertex. On an explicit range of $\gamma$, we establish local-power limits strictly above the test level for scale alternatives in the difference component at the scale $|\varepsilon_N|\asymp (\mathbb{E}_0C_3)^{1/2}/(Nd)$. Here $\mathbb{E}_0C_3$ gives the variance order of the difference count under these local alternatives. At this scale, the standardized drift of the weighted sum vanishes. When $d=1$, the weighted component instead detects local Gaussian scale alternatives while the difference component has no limiting drift. Thus dimension changes both the magnitude of a detectable scale difference and the component of the test that detects it.

papers.title: On the Tur\'an number for the Cartesian product of an odd cycle and a tree
papers.authors: Ya-Hong Chen, Yong Lu, Quan Sun, Qi Wu, Long-Tu Yuan
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a fixed tree on at least two vertices. We determine the Tur\'an number and all extremal graphs for the Cartesian product of an odd cycle $C_{2m+1}$ and $T$, for every fixed integer $m\ge1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, in terms of its decomposition family. Every extremal graph is the join of an independent set and an extremal graph for that family. The proof combines the Erd\H{o}s--S\'os theorem with weak stability and progressive induction.

papers.title: Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials
papers.abstract: We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(\mu)$ associated to a partition $\mu=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ \kappa_\mu:=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety. In genus $g=6$ the same conclusion holds for \[ (10),\ (9,1),\ (8,2),\ (8,1,1),\ (7,3),\ (6,4),\ (5,5). \]

papers.title: Rigidity in sharp eigenvalue estimates for differential forms
papers.authors: Tsz-Kiu Aaron Chow, James Koh, Sen Yuk Wu
papers.abstract: For $1\leq p\leq n/2$, we derive sharp eigenvalue estimates for the Hodge Laplacian on differential $p$-forms under the curvature condition introduced by Petersen and Wink, and study their equality cases. Equality recovers the stronger curvature operator lower bound and, in the closed case, leaves only round or Sasakian metrics on the universal cover. For manifolds with boundary, weak $p$-convexity of the boundary makes the unit hemisphere the only equality case for the absolute boundary problem.

papers.title: Vector Valued Katok-Sarnak Formulas
papers.abstract: We introduce a version of the Katok-Sarnak formula linking twisted traces of scalar valued Maass cusp forms for $\Gamma_0(N)$ with $N$ square-free to Fourier coefficients of vector valued Maass cusp forms for the metaplectic group $\operatorname{Mp}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and the Weil representation associated to a lattice of signature $(2,1)$. We prove this by computing the Fourier coefficients of the vector valued Siegel and Millson theta lift of a scalar valued newform by two different methods and comparing the results.

papers.title: Stochastic dynamics generation of directed percolation using a two-channel convolutional neural network
papers.authors: Feng Gao, Jianmin Shen, Wei Li
papers.abstract: Neural networks provide a promising approach to learning and generating the stochastic dynamics of nonequilibrium systems. In this study, we propose a stochastic dynamics generative method based on a two-channel convolutional neural network, using the (1+1)-dimensional directed bond percolation model to investigate its ability to learn local stochastic transition rules and reproduce stochastic dynamics across different system sizes. The proposed method takes the current particle configuration and the control parameter as inputs, learns the conditional activation probabilities at the next time step through local convolutions, and generates stochastic temporal evolution through iterative Bernoulli sampling. The results show that the network-generated dynamics agree well with Monte Carlo simulations across different control parameters. Furthermore, applying the trained network to a substantially larger system with $L=10000$ yields an estimated critical probability of $p_c=0.643$ and an effective density decay exponent of $\delta\approx0.1592$, close to the established theoretical values. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method can reproduce the stochastic dynamics of directed percolation and capture its macroscopic dynamical and statistical properties across different spatial sizes.

papers.title: Scaled-Gradient Hard Thresholding Algorithms for Sparse Signal Recovery
papers.abstract: Thresholding methods provide a simple iterative framework for sparse signal recovery by combining a search direction with a thresholding operation. Gradient-based search directions are computationally efficient because they require only first-order information for the error metric. We incorporate componentwise gradient scaling into this framework by preserving large-magnitude components and attenuating the remaining components of the gradient of error metric.
