papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra (VOA), not necessarily rational or $C_2$-cofinite, such that the category $\mathcal C_1(V)$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is semisimple and contains the generalized Verma modules associated to finite-dimensional modules over the Zhu algebra $A(V)$. Such VOAs include affine VOAs at admissible and generic levels. We prove that the bottom degree of Huang-Lepowsky's $P(w)$-tensor product module $M^1\boxtimes_{P(w)}M^2$ is isomorphic to the left $A(V)$-module $M^1\odot_{w,0}M^2$ arising from the restricted conformal blocks on $(\P^1,\infty,w,0)$. By shifting the marked points and using the parallel transport of the restricted conformal blocks, we construct an explicit braiding isomorphism on the category of finite-dimensional $A(V)$-modules, which is the restriction of the braiding isomorphism of Huang-Lepowsky-Zhang to the bottom degrees. For the affine VOA $L_k(\mathfrak g)$ at a positive integral level, it is given by the Casimir tensor of $\mathfrak g$ on certain quotients of tensor products of finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules, and at generic levels it recovers Drinfeld's commutativity isomorphism.

papers.title: An energy-constrained implicit step-and-truncate algorithm and its robust error estimates
papers.abstract: Deriving mesh-robust error bounds is an open problem for low-rank methods, including dynamical low-rank (DLR) and step-and-truncate (SAT) approaches, as highlighted in a recent review. Existing bounds can depend on Lipschitz constants that grow with inverse mesh size, making them impractical, particularly for kinetic equations, a major application of low-rank methods. We develop a unified framework for implicit SAT that provides a discrete counterpart of energy-localization analysis for nonlinear partial differential equations. By restricting numerical solutions to energy-localized regions, we obtain one-sided Lipschitz stability with constants independent of spatial resolution. The resulting error estimates and time-step restrictions are mesh robust, answering this open problem for the class of implicit SAT schemes covered by our assumptions. We emphasize that energy localization provides a general mechanism for mesh-independent robust error estimates in low-rank approximation, extending beyond the SAT methods considered here. Analogous results for DLR methods will be presented in subsequent work. Returning to implicit SAT, we demonstrate the broad applicability of the framework through error estimates for different classes of equations. Specifically, for semilinear parabolic and Vlasov--Poisson equations, we establish robust first-order error bounds for backward-Euler SAT under suitable regularity assumptions. Energy localization also has practical implications. We design an energy-constrained implicit SAT algorithm. Implicit SAT methods without energy constraints can select incorrect solution branches even when their algebraic residuals are small. Moreover, time-step reduction can be essential for continuation into larger energy regions. Numerical experiments support these conclusions.

papers.title: Quasi-projective dimensions over homological ring epimorphisms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study quasi-projective dimensions of modules over rings connected by homological ring epimorphisms. We establish several inequalities relating the quasi-projective dimensions over the source and target rings. As applications, we investigate the quasi-global dimension of triangular matrix rings and provide examples showing that the class of modules with finite quasi-projective dimension does not satisfy the 2-out-of-3 property in general.

papers.title: Distributed Zeroth-Order Composite Finite-Sum Optimization via Incremental Variance Reduction
papers.abstract: We study decentralized composite finite-sum optimization over a fixed connected undirected network, where agents access local component functions through function evaluations and share a possibly nonsmooth convex regularizer. In this setting, standard two-point gradient estimators can retain nonvanishing variance at a solution, complicating their integration with gradient tracking. We propose Distributed Zeroth-Order Incremental Variance Reduction (Distributed ZIVR), which combines incrementally updated component-gradient estimates with a proximal gradient-tracking scheme. The method admits an implementation using a constant number of function evaluations per agent at every iteration, without intermittent full-component or full-coordinate refreshes. For convex smooth component functions and strongly convex local averages, we establish linear convergence up to a controllable finite-difference error. With the finite-difference radius chosen for the target accuracy, Chebyshev-accelerated mixing yields a per-agent oracle complexity of $\widetilde{O}(d(m+\kappa)\log(1/\epsilon))$ for expected squared solution error $\epsilon$, where $d$ is the dimension, $m$ is the number of components per agent, and $\kappa$ is the condition number. This matches the centralized ZIVR oracle bound, while the communication bound has only an inverse square-root dependence on the network spectral gap. Experiments on logistic and robust regression demonstrate rapid reduction of solution and consensus errors.

papers.title: A Gaussian Process Regression-Enhanced Two-Sweep Parameterized Power Method for Computing Extreme Eigenpairs
papers.authors: Tiantian Sun, Xiaofei Peng, Juan Zhang, Seakweng Vong
papers.abstract: For computing the dominant eigenvalue and the corresponding eigenvector of a real and symmetric matrix, inspired by the parameterized power method and multistep iteration, we propose a two-sweep parameterized power method, and establish its convergence theory. To further improve the convergence speed of the new method, we use Gaussian process regression (GPR) to predict the quasi-optimal parameter and give a version of the proposed method based on GPR. Numerical experiments show that the two-sweep parameterized power method with quasi-optimal parameters outperforms some existing methods in terms of computing efficiency.

papers.title: Push forwards of smooth measures on the unitary group in odd characteristic under the Chevalley map are almost bounded
papers.authors: Avraham Aizenbud, Nir Avni, Dmitry Gourevitch, David Kazhdan, Eitan Sayag
papers.abstract:
In this paper we study analytic properties of the Chevalley map $p:\mathfrak{u} \to \mathfrak{c}$ where $\mathfrak{u}$ is the Lie algebra of a unitary group over a local field of odd characteristics. This map essentially sends a matrix to its characteristic polynomial.
  Our main result is that smooth compactly supported measures on $\mathfrak{u}$ are pushed by the Chevalley map to measures on $\mathfrak{c}$ with density functions in $L^q(\mathfrak{c})$ for all $q < \infty$. We also provide similar results for the Chevalley map attached to the unitary group.
  An important consequence is an odd characteristic analogue to results of Harish-Chandra stating the local integrability of the orbital integrals on the unitary group and its Lie algebra. Further possible applications to local integrability of characters of admissible representations of unitary groups over local fields of odd characteristic are also discussed.

papers.title: Numerical Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for rank-three matroids
papers.abstract: We prove the numerical Kawamata--Viehweg conjecture for every matroid of rank three: the Euler characteristic of the inverse of an integral big and nef line bundle class is nonnegative. The proof reduces the conjecture to an inequality for a stone game.

papers.title: Boundary stabilization of a moving interface in a 2 x 2 weakly hyperbolic system of balance laws: application to continuous sedimentation
papers.authors: Mohand Ouidir Amirat (LAGEPP), Vincent Andrieu (LAGEPP, CNRS), Mathieu Bajodek (LAGEPP, CPE), Claire Valentin (LAGEPP)
papers.abstract: We design a boundary feedback for the level of the sediment bed of a continuous settler and prove that it exponentially stabilizes the linearized closed loop under a small-gain condition. The unit is modeled by a 2 x 2 system of balance laws in which the bed surface, the interface, is not a smooth part of the solution but a moving shock between a weakly hyperbolic free-settling zone and a strictly hyperbolic compression zone. We describe it by the Rankine-Hugoniot relations and map the problem onto a fixed domain. Moreover, we prove local well-posedness with a continuation criterion given by a single margin function. Then we linearize the system near an equilibrium. The linearization couples a dissipative distributed layer to one scalar, the interface position, whose equation does not contain the control. We solve this by infinitedimensional forwarding: a Sylvester kernel cancels the interface trace and isolates the interface pole, and a proportional feedback then sets its decay rate. Every hypothesis is verified on an illustrative example, a laboratory-scale continuous settler containing a bed of compact polystyrene beads.

papers.title: Global existence and uniqueness of Lions' weak solutions for the 2D inhomogeneous Navier-Stokes equations in bounded domains
papers.abstract: The global well-posedness for Lions' weak solutions to the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in two-dimensional bounded domains is concerned. When the initial density $0\leq \rho_0\in L^\infty(\Om)$ (allowing for vacuum) and initial velocity $u_0\in L^2_\sigma(\Omega)$, the global existence, regularity, and exponential decay-in-time rates of weak solutions are established via a priori estimates, which rely crucially on the duality of BMO and Hardy space for the pressure term, and the classical Sobolev extension theorem. In particular, for the non-vacuous case where $0< \rho_0\in L^\infty(\Om)$ is bounded away from zero, we further prove the uniqueness of weak solutions in the sense of approximation by strong solutions, based on the key estimate \(t^{1/2}\nabla u\in L^2(0,T;L^\infty(\Omega))\), which essentially follows from a delicate localized point-wise bound for \(\nabla u\) near the boundary. The latter bound is derived by the Green functions estimate for the nonhomogeneous Dirichlet Stokes problem, and the uniform \(C^1\) boundary estimate on the remaining homogeneous Stokes problem, through a Stokes decomposition on suitably constructed local \(C^2\) domains.

papers.title: Spectral theory for transmission problems and resonances for transparent balls
papers.abstract: We construct generalized eigenfunctions and a spectral calculus for the transmission problem on Lipschitz domains. Then, focusing on the specific example of the ball, we prove a high-frequency resonance dichotomy for Maxwell's equations for a ball with positive, piecewise constant permittivity and permeability. If the product of these coefficients is no larger inside the ball than outside, the cutoff resolvent extends holomorphically to a strip of fixed width below the real axis, including the case of equal products. If the interior product is larger, we construct whispering-gallery resonances exponentially close to the real axis. The proofs use estimates for the transverse electric and transverse magnetic determinants that are uniform in angular momentum and complex frequency, together with a quasimode construction and Rouch\'e's theorem. Explicit generalized eigenfunctions identify these determinants with the scattering poles and give the spectral resolution and the normalization relating the scattering amplitude to the Mie T-matrix.

papers.title: P-generalized determinant over quaternions and its applications
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the ${\rm P}$-generalized determinant, a more general class of quaternion determinants. It unifies several classical quaternion determinants proposed between 1922 and 2008, including the Moore determinant, the Xie determinant, the Chen determinant, and the Kyrchei row--column determinants, thereby revealing the essential nature of quaternion determinants as multivariate polynomial-type functions with a fixed ordering of products. We provide equivalent characterizations of the expansion of the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant along a given row or column, and establish conversion relations between the $\mathrm{P}_{l}$- and $\mathrm{P}_{r}$-generalized determinants. We prove that the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant of a quaternion Hermitian matrix is a real number independent of the choice of cycle representation rule. We further investigate the behavior of the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant under elementary row and column operations on quaternion Hermitian matrices, as well as its linearity in rows and columns. Finally, using the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant, we derive determinantal representations of the inverse of an invertible quaternion Hermitian matrix and of the unique solution to the quaternion matrix equation $AXB=C$. In particular, this yields Cramer's rule for the left and right linear systems $Ax=b$ and $xA=b$.

papers.title: Secure Deterministic Identification with Feedback and Sensing over State-Dependent Wiretap Channels
papers.authors: Vida Gholamian, Yaning Zhao, Christian Deppe, Holger Boche, Rafael F. Schaefer
papers.abstract:
Identification differs from classical transmission in that the receiver determines whether a particular identity was sent rather than recovering a message. We study secure deterministic identification over state-dependent discrete memoryless wiretap channels with private noiseless feedback and a sensing distortion constraint. The encoder has no local randomness and uses only the identity and past feedback. A symbol-wise input restriction guarantees the sensing constraint.
  We show that the secure deterministic identification capacity equals its non-secure feedback counterpart when the admissible main channel has positive ordinary transmission capacity and H(Y|Z,X=x)>0 for some fixed admissible input x. This equality does not require positive classical wiretap secrecy capacity. For achievability, noiseless feedback generates common randomness for identification and enables secret-key extraction by privacy amplification. The extracted key one-time-pad encrypts a short identification tag, whose reliable transmission requires only a sublinear number of additional channel uses. We also present an alternative construction in which feedback-generated randomness replaces the local randomization of a stochastic wiretap encoder.
  We further prove that secure identification capacity vanishes whenever non-secure identification capacity is zero. We also identify a class of channels with input-independent wiretapper observations that achieves full non-secure identification capacity even when the private conditional feedback entropy is zero, illustrated by a binary state-dependent wiretap channel. Thus, feedback can support both identification and secrecy without local encoder randomization while satisfying sensing constraints.

papers.title: Genetic weight of a mutant in a biparental Moran model with infinite selection
papers.authors: Camille Coron (MIA Paris-Saclay, INRAE), Olivier H\'enard
papers.abstract: We study, after Coron Le Jan (2024), the genetic contribution of a single strongly advantageous mutant in a biparental Moran model under infinite selection. We prove a functional limit theorem for the entire beneficial mutation spreading period: after normalization by \(\sqrt N\), the contributions carried by the advantaged and disadvantaged subpopulations converge jointly in law to a non-degenerate random multiple of an explicit deterministic profile. Randomness is generated during the initial microscopic growth of the mutant lineage and subsequently propagated through the population along a deterministic macroscopic trajectory. At the heart of this phenomenon is an eigenmode martingale that measures the imbalance between the mean genetic weight of the founding ancestor within the two classes; its limiting value provides precisely the random amplitude of the macroscopic profile and is characterized by a smoothing equation.

papers.title: Mathematical foundations of second quantization: an introduction through spin-boson models
papers.abstract: These lecture notes originate from a one-semester course on the mathematical foundations of second quantization, first given at the Department of Physics of the Friedrich-Alexander-Universit\"at Erlangen-N\"urnberg in the Winter Semester 2025/26 to a mixed audience of physics and mathematics students. Their guiding thread is a class of physical models: spin-boson models, describing a two-level system coupled to a boson field. After summarizing the necessary background on unbounded operators, up to the Kato-Rellich and KLMN theorems, and developing direct sums and tensor products of Hilbert spaces and of unbounded operators, we treat single-mode boson fields, constructing the ladder and number operators and characterizing their domains, before moving to Fock spaces, second quantization, bosonic and fermionic annihilation and creation operators, and the canonical (anti)commutation relations. Throughout, spin-boson models provide both the motivation and the test bench for the formalism: we rigorously establish their self-adjointness, solve the pure dephasing and Jaynes-Cummings models explicitly, deriving their spectra and the qubit channels they induce, show how their multimode counterparts display irreversible decoherence and decay, and, in an appendix, prove the rotating-wave approximation for the quantum Rabi model with an explicit error bound. Finally, we use the KLMN theorem to construct spin-boson models with non-normalizable form factors, and briefly discuss stronger ultraviolet divergences and the need for renormalization. Exercises with full solutions are included.

papers.title: Estimates of Lucas series and expansions in non-integer bases
papers.abstract: Special Fibonacci and Lucas type expansions proved useful to ``correct'' some theorems on the number of expansions in non-integer bases \cite{BaiKomLor2021, KomLorPed2024, KomLorPed2025}. The proof of a key lemma was non-constructive. It was made constructive in the Fibonacci case by giving a precise estimate of the growth of the partial sums of the series of the inverses of the Fibonacci numbers \cite{KomPed2025}. In this paper we extend this result to the general case.

papers.title: Reduction numbers under flat extensions
papers.abstract:
The reduction number of the maximal ideal of a localization (or even faithfully flat extension) need not
  increase under specialization. Nevertheless, for
  each fixed local ring the reduction numbers of the maximal
  ideals of all its localization have a finite common bound.

papers.title: Elliptic Fekete points: separation, Riesz energies, and polynomial conditioning
papers.abstract: Elliptic Fekete configurations minimize logarithmic energy on the sphere. They also provide a natural source of complex polynomials with controlled Shub--Smale condition number. The link between these two problems is the product of the distances from each point to all the other points: logarithmic energy controls the geometric mean of these products, whereas local conditioning depends on each product separately. This paper studies the passage from global information to uniform estimates at individual nodes, exploring its connections with quantitative equidistribution, Riesz energies, and polynomial conditioning. We improve separation bounds for elliptic Fekete configurations and obtain quantitative Riesz-energy estimates for both these configurations and spherical roots of polynomials with optimal-order global conditioning. For $0<s<2$, these estimates also improve explicit upper bounds for the minimal Riesz $s$-energy.

papers.title: Bridging rough stochastic differential equations and rough semimartingales
papers.authors: Jannis R. Dause, Peter K. Friz, Jost Pieper
papers.abstract: We bridge the gap between the mixed-moment theory of c\`adl\`ag rough stochastic differential equations (short:RSDEs), introduced by Friz, Hocquet and L\^e (2021) and extended to the c\`adl\`ag setting by Allan and Pieper (2026), and the theory of rough semimartingales (short:RSMs), introduced by Friz and Zorin-Kranich (2023), by investigating the intersection of these two theories for the first time. By introducing the concept of good solutions to RSDEs, solutions which are simultaneously both mixed-moment solutions and RSMs, we develop a solution concept, which allows for good control on both moment-based and pathwise properties of solutions. The well-posedness of good solutions is proven using a fixed point argument on the space of $L^{2}$-martingales by suitably leveraging previously known mixed-moment estimates. Based on these insights we further characterize a large class of good solutions of semi-linear RSDEs through a novel rough stochastic Duhamel's principle.

papers.title: Proper conflict-free degree-choosability of graphs with maximum average degree less than $8/3$
papers.abstract: A proper coloring $\varphi$ of a graph $G$ is called proper conflict-free if, for every non-isolated vertex $v$, some color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood $N_G(v)$. For a nonnegative integer $k$, a graph $G$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable if, for every list assignment $L$ satisfying $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)+k$ for each $v\in V(G)$, there exists a proper conflict-free coloring $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(v)\in L(v)$ for each $v\in V(G)$. We prove that every connected graph other than the $5$-cycle $C_5$ with maximum average degree less than $8/3$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable. This improves the maximum average degree bound $18/7$ of Kashima, \v{S}krekovski and Xu, and removes the assumption $g(G)\ge7$ from the $8/3$ theorem of Qi, Song and Cao. As an immediate consequence, our theorem also yields that every planar graph of girth at least $8$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable.

papers.title: Inviscid limit for the hyperbolic Keller--Segel equations in $B_{\infty,1}^{1}$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the inviscid limit for the hyperbolic Keller--Segel equations with logistic sensitivity $1-u$. We establish a common existence time and a priori estimates uniform with respect to the diffusion coefficient in the critical Besov spaces $B_{p,1}^{1+d/p}(R^d)$ with $1\le p\le\infty$. For $1<p<\infty$, we obtain explicit convergence rates in $B_{p,1}^{0}$, and we also give estimates for the case $p=1$. For initial data in $B_{\infty,1}^{1}$, we prove convergence at rate $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ in $L^\infty$, a bound of order $O(\varepsilon^{1/2}\log(e/\varepsilon))$ in $B_{\infty,1}^{0}$, and strong convergence in $L^\infty(0,T;B_{\infty,1}^{1})$. Additional regularity of the initial data yields improved convergence rates. We construct a fixed initial datum showing that the exponent $1/2$ in $L^\infty$ is optimal.

papers.title: A Preconditioned Quantum Linear Solver for Periodic Two-Phase Heat Conduction with Mesh-Independent Condition Number
papers.abstract:
We consider here computational homogenization of a periodic two-phase conduction problem. Quantum linear-system algorithms for its finite element discretization are limited by the condition number of the stiffness matrix. This condition number grows quadratically with the number of elements per side. Classically, preconditioning by the homogeneous (single-phase) operator bounds the condition number by the conductivity contrast, for every mesh size. On a quantum computer, however, a preconditioner encoded as a separate factor multiplies the subnormalizations, and the quadratic dependency returns.
  In this paper, we absorb the closed-form inverse square root of the homogeneous operator into the finite element factors. The preconditioned operator then becomes the product of a norm-preserving gradient operator $\mat{V}$, a diagonal matrix of scaled conductivities, and $\mat{V}^T$. Each factor has norm at most one. The block encoding therefore has subnormalization one, and its condition number is bounded by just the conductivity contrast, for every mesh size and in every dimension. The operator $\mat{V}$ is applied as a quantum Fourier transform, a small rotation at each wavenumber, and an inverse transform. Quantum singular value transformation then block-encodes the inverse of the preconditioned operator.
  We test the method numerically on three periodic cells with up to $10^6$ unknowns. The results confirm that the condition number does not depend on the mesh, and the energy-norm error of the inverse is below the polynomial tolerance at every mesh. On meshes of $4 \times 4$ and $8 \times 8$ elements, we also build the entire inverse as one Qiskit circuit and simulate it by state vector, with the rotation at each wavenumber built from uniformly controlled rotations. The output state agrees with the finite element solution to within the polynomial tolerance.

papers.title: Shaping and Finite-Blocklength Analysis of Quaternionic Alamouti-Type Codes
papers.authors: Juliana G. F. Souza, Yu-Chih Huang
papers.abstract: We study finite $2\times2$ Alamouti-type space--time codes associated with classical maximal orders in definite quaternion algebras over $\mathbb Q$. For the family indexed by primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, we prove that the Eisenstein case $q=3$ uniquely minimises the finite quotient-alphabet energy at fixed minimum lattice distance and alphabet size. This ordering holds for every integer $p\geq2$, including when the representatives and their common translation are jointly optimised, with an explicit positive gap for every $q>3$. For uniform finite inputs, we derive a controlled high-SNR expansion of the information variance and determine its limiting ratio to the mutual information deficit. The mutual information expansion specialises arbitrary input fading results and gives an explicit remainder. Standard random-coding and second-order achievability tools relate these quantities to reliability over independently faded Alamouti blocks. All alphabets preserve symbol-wise maximum-likelihood detection at the Alamouti level. Numerical energy, mutual information, and error-rate comparisons support the analysis. Centred comparisons with classical Alamouti, Golden, and Silver codes illustrate the trade-off between reliability, symbol rate, and decoding effort.

papers.title: Exchange graphs and $g$-vectors of surface rigid algebras
papers.abstract: We classify the connected components of support $\tau$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected if and only if the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules, and has Cartan rank one. In this case, it has exactly two connected components. For every nonzero $\tau$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra, the graph of $\tau$-tilting completions is connected. More generally, we classify the completion components for an arbitrary surface rigid algebra and a fixed $\tau$-rigid pair. For partial tagged triangulations with all endpoints at punctures, we express the Cartan matrix and $g$-vectors by signed endpoint data. We prove that $\tau$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates. Trees give type A, and a criterion on the original partial tagged triangulation distinguishes types D and C in the unicyclic case.

papers.title: First and second order firing statistics of large neuronal networks with community structure
papers.authors: Thiago H. N. Coelho, Daniel Figueiredo, Giulio Iacobelli, Guilherme Ost, Conrado C. Pinto
papers.abstract: We study a discrete-time stochastic model for the spiking activity of a network of $n$ interacting neurons partitioned into $k$ communities. The interaction network is a random directed weighted graph generated by a Stochastic Block Model with $k+1$ edge types ($k$ intra-community, $1$ inter-community). Each edge is present independently with a probability that depends only on its type. When present, an edge carries a type-dependent deterministic weight scaled by $n^{-1}$, which is excitatory or inhibitory depending on an independent random sign. Given the interaction network, the spiking process is a stationary Markov chain. Our results describe how the network's community structure manifests itself in the first- and second-order statistics of this chain, as $n \to \infty$ with $k$ fixed. Representing these statistics as explicit functions of the random interaction network, we prove that, with high probability: (i) the vectors of mean firing activity and firing variances are approximated in supremum norm by deterministic vectors that are constant within each community, with an error of order $\sqrt{\log(n)/n}$; (ii) the off-diagonal part of the $0$-lagged firing covariance matrix is approximated in max norm, with an error of order $\sqrt{\log(n)/n^3}$, by a deterministic community-block matrix (constant on each block defined by a pair of communities), with block values determined by the unique solution to a $k \times k$ Stein matrix equation; (iii) in contrast, the $t$-lagged covariance matrix, for every lag $t \ge 1$, is approximated in max norm, again with an error of order $\sqrt{\log(n)/n^3}$, by a random matrix built from two components: a random matrix capturing the interaction network and a deterministic community-block matrix. Finally, we discuss conditions on the model parameters under which these limiting statistics enable the identifiability of the community structure.

papers.title: Numerical analysis of linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze the standard and the mass-lumped linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem. For the standard method, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of the discrete ground state up to sign for sufficiently small mesh sizes, which only requires the $H^1$-convergence of the discrete ground states. For both methods, we establish optimal convergence rates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-norms for $1 \le p < \infty$. Under additional regularity assumptions on the potential, we further obtain an optimal convergence rate in the $W^{1,\infty}$-norm and an almost optimal convergence rate, up to a logarithmic factor, in the $L^\infty$-norm. Moreover, we prove that the discrete ground states superconverge to the Ritz projection of the exact ground state in the $W^{1,p}$-seminorm. The analysis is based on a perturbation argument. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

papers.title: CRCs in four-dimensional lattice graphs
papers.abstract: We obtain series of new completely regular codes in Cayley graphs of the groups $Z_q^n$ with the Lee metric. Combined with binary linear programming methods, the constructions lead to enumeration of all completely regular codes in such graphs for the groups $Z_q^4$, $q\leq 7$ up to parameter matrices.

papers.title: Effective threshold dynamics for the cubic nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation in three dimensions
papers.abstract: We consider the focussing cubic Klein-Gordon equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$ in the radial setting. Foundational work by Nakanishi-Schlag gives a complete qualitative characterisation of the dynamics near the ground state $Q$, in particular revealing a threshold phenomenon, whereby a co-dimension one Lipschitz manifold separates finite time blow up from scattering solutions in forward time. Our aim in this paper is to derive an effective bound for the scattering norm $\|u\|_{L_t^3([0,\infty);L_x^6(\mathbb{R}^3))}$, for scattering energy class solutions $u$ with data sufficiently near $Q$ and close to the threshold manifold. This requires the development of an induction on energy strategy in a setting where an alternative to the usual Morawetz approach appears necessary.

papers.title: Relative Du Bois complexes over higher dimensional bases
papers.abstract: We extend the notion of the right relative Du Bois complex to a smooth base of arbitrary dimension. We further show that this complex satisfies base change in the sense of Kov\'acs--Taji, for flat families with strict higher Du Bois fibers, extending the result by Ning over a smooth curve.

papers.title: Deformations of Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms
papers.abstract:
Recent work of Brantner and Taelman shows that derived deformation theory and period maps can recover strong mixed-characteristic lifting results. In this paper, we develop a prismatic version of this method for Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms, constructing compatible deformations over $A/I^n$ for every $n$ under suitable hypotheses.
  We also apply our method to $F$-split Calabi--Yau varieties over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. In particular, we consider an $F$-split smooth proper variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$, with $H^{d-1}(X,O_X)=0$ and trivial canonical bundle. We show that $X$ admits a lift to $W_3(k)$.

papers.title: Maximum edge overlap between independent random regular graphs
papers.abstract: Optimising the vertex correspondence can substantially increase the number of edges shared by two independent realisations of the same random graph. We quantify this phenomenon for uniformly random $d$-regular graphs and derive corresponding results for their edge-based graph edit distance. For every fixed $d\geq 3$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n+\Theta_{\mathbb P}(n/\log n)$, where the leading term $n$ arises from Hamiltonicity, while the surplus captures the optimal order of the excess beyond it. We establish explicit upper and lower bounds on the surplus. The upper bound is obtained by counting common cores of minimum degree at least two, while the lower bound is established using spanning factors consisting of cycles of the same logarithmic length. For the special case $d=2$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n-(1+o_{\mathbb P}(1))\log n$. The additional overlap achievable is also studied by rotating aligned Hamilton cycles, using a contiguity argument. As a by-product, we determine the asymptotic maximum overlap between unions of independent random perfect matchings under cyclic shifts.

papers.title: $K$-tropical curves, Riemann-Roch and Serre duality
papers.abstract: We endow a tropical curve with the structure of a ringed space and establish analogues of Riemann-Roch and Serre duality for these ringed spaces. As a corollary, we give a cohomological proof of the tropical Riemann-Roch theorem.

papers.title: A note on rational wavefront sets for finite special orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: We study rational wavefront sets of irreducible representations of finite special orthogonal groups over $\mathbb F_q$. We assume that $q$ is odd and that both $q$ and its characteristic are sufficiently large. Using {the second author's} results for full orthogonal groups, we determine the maximal rational wavefront sets and the dimensions of the corresponding generalized Whittaker models. We show that each rational wavefront set is the rational closure of its maximal elements. For unipotent representations, we describe the maximal rational wavefront sets in terms of Lusztig's canonical quotient and their behavior under Alvis--Curtis duality.

papers.title: On unitary representations of $p$-adic $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}$ and $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ of purely bad parity
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$ or split $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$ over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We classify the irreducible unitary representations of $G$ of purely bad parity: such a representation is unitary if and only if it is of Arthur type, except for one additional family when $G=\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$. In particular, we confirm the remaining case of Ciubotaru's conjecture for $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$, namely that every unitary unipotent representation with integral infinitesimal parameter is of Arthur type.

papers.title: Feasibility of Common-Stream-Only Sensing in ZF-RSMA with Imperfect CSIT
papers.abstract: Reusing the Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) common stream for sensing eliminates dedicated probing signals in Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC), but creates a feasibility bottleneck: the common-power fraction must simultaneously support common decoding, private decoding, and target detection. This paper investigates this tradeoff in downlink zero-forcing RSMA with imperfect channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT) and imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). With the common beam fixed over a sensing dwell through sensing geometry, the common-power fraction becomes the sole design variable. We prove that the communication-feasible set is either a closed interval or empty. Analytical outage expressions localize these endpoints, revealing a high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) floor-ceiling effect: common decoding dictates a common-power floor, while imperfect CSIT and SIC impose a private-decoding ceiling. For sensing, the conditional detection constraint is affine, preserving the interval structure. A geometry-matched common beam ensures monotonic detection improvement, reducing joint-feasibility check to the communication-feasible upper endpoint. Simulations validate our analysis, identifying regimes where common-stream-only sensing is viable.

papers.title: A solution to Haagerup's Problem on decomposable maps
papers.abstract: We prove that a von Neumann algebra $N$ is injective if and only if $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$ for every linear map $T:\ell^\infty_3to N$, answering a problem of Haagerup (1985).

papers.title: $W^{1,p}$ error estimates of an IPDG and a class of HDG methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) method, a hybrid mixed DG method, and two representative hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains. For any fixed $\epsilon\in (0,\frac{1}{2})$, we first derive optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates for $2\leq p<\frac{1}{\epsilon}$ by combining the interface Green's functions developed in \cite{lq2026} with the Fubini-type weighted estimates established in this paper. These error estimates lead to discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability for $2\leq q<\frac{1}{\epsilon}$, where $q$ is the conjugate number of $p$ such that $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. Using this stability result and a suitably constructed dual problem, we extend the optimal error estimates to $\frac{1}{1-\epsilon}<p<2$ and subsequently establish the corresponding inf-sup stability for $\frac{1}{1-\epsilon}< q<2$. Thus, both optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates and discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability hold throughout the range $\frac{1}{1-\epsilon}<p<\frac{1}{\epsilon}$, with $q=p/(p-1)$. Note that all of the aforementioned results are free of logarithmic factors and also hold on polyhedral meshes (except for the hybrid mixed DG method). Compared with the conforming finite element method (FEM), establishing such error estimates and inf-sup stability results for DG methods on convex polyhedral domains is more delicate because their analysis involves mesh-dependent norms. Consequently, the operator interpolation theory employed for conforming FEMs cannot be directly applied to DG methods. Finally, a numerical example is presented to illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Hereditary Approximation under Hilbertian Extension
papers.authors: Gang Cai, Qingjin Cheng, Longfa Sun, Yinghua Sun
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that if a Banach space $X$ has the hereditary approximation property, then $X\oplus_2 H$ has the hereditary approximation property for every Hilbert space $H$. This answers a question of Johnson and Szankowski. In addition, if $X$ is also reflexive, then every closed subspace of $X\oplus_2H$ has the metric approximation property. The proof uses Grothendieck's characterization of the approximation property, a factorization of nuclear operators through quotients of $X$, and a nuclear perturbation of the coordinate projection on a closed graph.

papers.title: Derived tame monomial algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite-dimensional connected monomial algebra over an algebraically closed field is derived tame if and only if every finite connected convex subcategory of its universal cover has non-negative Euler form. Derived tameness is also equivalent to tameness of its repetitive category and trivial extension. For one-cycle algebras, this condition is equivalent to the non-negativity on $\mathbb R$ of $|Q_0|$ explicitly computable polynomials in $\mathbb Q[t]$. This gives a finite algorithm for deciding derived tameness. We also construct an infinite family of derived-tame one-cycle string algebras with minimal cubic relations, no two of which are derived equivalent.

papers.title: Morse theory and topological degree for resonant mean field equations on Riemann surfaces with boundary
papers.authors: Mohameden Ahmedou, Zhengni Hu, Heming Wang, Lei Zhang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish Morse theory for the Neumann mean field equation on a compact Riemann surface at $\rho=4\pi m$, $m\in\mathbb N$. To address the loss of compactness associated with bubbling, we use Bahri's theory of critical points at infinity. Assume that the reduced functionals are Morse and that the leading scale coefficient does not vanish at their critical points. We classify the critical points at infinity arising from interior, boundary, and mixed concentration, compute their Morse indices and local relative homology, and establish deformation lemmas at resonance. We prove that, for $m\geq 2$, every sufficiently negative sublevel is homotopy equivalent to the boundary-weighted barycenter space of order $m-1$. The Euler--Poincar\'e identity gives the Leray--Schauder degree at resonance without assuming nondegeneracy of the solutions. If all solutions are nondegenerate, we further obtain strong Morse inequalities with explicit Betti numbers over $\mathbb Z_2$. As a consequence, we obtain existence and multiplicity results, as well as criteria for solutions with prescribed Morse index.

papers.title: On the modularity of residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2
papers.abstract: We use a new version of the Taylor--Wiles method, based on a tame analogue of the techniques introduced by Skinner--Wiles, to prove new modularity theorems for residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2 over totally real fields.

papers.title: On the generic case of Jiang's conjecture
papers.abstract: Jiang's conjecture predicts that if $\pi$ is a generic representation of a quasi-split $p$-adic group, then the $L$-parameter of the Aubert-Zelevinsky involution of $\pi$ must be trivial on $\mathrm{SL}_2$. In this paper, we prove this statement for a general quasi-split group under certain assumptions on the conjectural local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: An odd version of the Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra and the odd Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
papers.abstract: We study an ``odd'' version of the Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra that is obtained by replacing free Lie algebras in even generators by free graded Lie algebras in odd generators in the classical definition. These odd variants are related to the ``odd'' Kontsevich graph complex in the same way as the classical Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller group is related to the even Kontsevich graph complex. We show an odd analog of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, namely that the odd Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra is isomorphic to a free graded Lie algebra in one odd generator of weight 3. Thus we in particular compute the odd graph cohomology in the bottom cohomological degree, showing that it is mostly zero.

papers.title: Bounds on the maximum denominator of fractional chromatic numbers
papers.abstract: For a positive rational number $x=p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are coprime positive integers, let $\operatorname{den}(x)=q$. For a positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{sd}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{den}(\chi_f(G)): |V(G)|=n\}$. Let $D(n)=2^{-n}(n+1)^{(n+1)/2}$. It was proved by Alon, Tuza and Voigt that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)$. In this paper, we prove that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)n^{-\frac12\log_2 n+\frac14\log_2\log_2 n+O(1)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For the lower bound on $\operatorname{sd}(n)$, it was recently proved by Bonamy, Hylasov\'a, Kaiser and Sereni that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge\sqrt{2}$. We prove that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge 3^{1/3}>\sqrt{2}$.

papers.title: Coring morphisms presenting nonaffine noncommutative fibre bundles
papers.abstract: We consider noncommutative analogues of associated fibre bundles where the total space, base space and even the fiber may be nonaffine, that is, not represented by a single algebra, and where the structure group is replaced by a Hopf algebra $H$. We choose to describe gluing of affine pieces by corings. In the role of a principal bundle we take an internal $E$-coring $M$ in the monoidal category of right $H$-comodules where $E$ is a faithfully flat right Hopf-Galois extension. In a role of a fibre we either take a left $H$-comodule algebra $F$, or more generally an internal $F$-coring $N$ in the monoidal category of left $H$-comodules. Cotensor products combining these data is used to obtain an ordinary coring representing the total space of an associated bundle. If the fiber coring $N$ is equipped with a choice of an $H$-coinvariant grouplike element, then we exhibit a canonical morphisms of corings from the $H$-coinvariant coring of $M$ to the associated bundle coring which is viewed as a dual to the projection of an associated bundle.

papers.title: Characterizations and MacWilliams-Like Identities of Weakly Regular Bent Partitions
papers.authors: Jiaxin Wang, Yadi Wei, Fang-Wei Fu, Jin Li, Fulin Li
papers.abstract: Bent partitions play a significant role in the theory of bent functions. In this paper, we study weakly regular bent partitions, that is, all generated bent functions are weakly regular (called in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$). Let $\Gamma=\{A_{i}, i \in V_{m}\}$ be a bent partition of $V_{n}$ in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$, where $V_{n}$ denotes an $n$-dimensional vector space over the prime field $\mathbb{F}_{p}$, $n$ is even, $m \leq \frac{n}{2}$, and $m \geq 2$ if $p=2$. We first characterize bent partition $\Gamma$ in terms of the duals of component functions of vectorial bent functions. In particular, we prove that if $p \neq 3$, then all bent functions generated by $\Gamma$ are regular. Building on the above result, we give characterizations of bent partition $\Gamma$ in terms of two classes of linear codes. When $n \geq 4$ and $m=\frac{n}{2}$, except for the case where $(p, n)=(2, 4)$ and $|A_{i_{0}}|=1$ for some $i_{0}$, we show that $\Gamma$ is obtained from a spread (after a shift). Particularly, any normal bent partition of $V_{n}$ of depth $p^{\frac{n}{2}}$ in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$ must be obtained from a spread (after a shift), where $n \geq 4$. We establish the Macwilliams-like identities for bent partitions in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$. Furthermore, if $p$ is odd, we present some nonexistence results on bent partitions in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$.

papers.title: Critical fluctuations in the edge--triangle exponential random graph models
papers.authors: Song-Hao Liu, Qi-Man Shao, Hao Shi, Jing-Yu Xu
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative limit theorems for the edge density $Q$ in the dense edge--triangle exponential random graph model at criticality and under parameter perturbations of order $n^{-1}$. At the fixed critical parameters $(\alpha_c,h_c),$ the centered fluctuations satisfy $n^{2/3}(Q-\mathbb{E} Q)\Rightarrow \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_0^2)$, with explicit variance $\sigma_0^2>0$. This disproves the quartic fluctuation conjecture of Bianchi, Collet and Magnanini (2024). Gaussian limits also hold $(\alpha_c+ \lambda/n,h_c + \gamma/n)$, except when the coefficients satisfy $-\frac{11}{16}+\frac{2}{9}(\gamma+\frac49\lambda)=0$. Under this linearity condition, the limiting laws of $\sqrt n(Q-2/3)$ have densities proportional to $\exp\{-81z^4/64+9\theta z^2/8\}$, where $\theta=-57/16+8\lambda/27$. We obtain a sharp $n^{-1/3}$ rate in $1$-Wasserstein distance for the Gaussian limits and an $O(n^{-1/2})$ bound for the quartic limits. The proofs combine Stein's method for exchangeable pairs with conditional row estimates and a local Dobrushin contraction.

papers.title: Ore-degree conditions for hypergraph matchings
papers.authors: Mingyang Guo, Tianhong Kan, Hongliang Lu, Feihong Yuan
papers.abstract:
Let $\sigma_k(H)$ be the minimum sum of the vertex degrees over all non-edges of an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$. For every $k\ge3$, $n\geq ks$ and sufficiently large $n$, we establish a sharp Ore-type degree condition that forces a matching of size $s$ in $H$. Specifically, we prove that if \[
  \sigma_k(H)>\max\left\{
  k\left(\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-s}{k-1}\right),
  (k-c)\binom{ks-2}{k-1}\right\}, \] then $H$ has a matching of size $s$, where $c=n-ks+1$. In particular, this proves a conjecture of Balogh, Palmer and Raeisi for $k\geq 3$ and sufficiently large $n$.

papers.title: A note on surjective endomorphisms of Smale spaces
papers.abstract: We give conditions that are all equivalent to surjectivity for endomorphisms of irreducible Smale spaces. This extends results previously obtained by Hedlund~\cite{hedlund-endomorphisms} for full shifts, by Coven and Paul and by Lind and Marcus for irreducible subshifts of finite type.

papers.title: Bethe Hessian Recovery through the Kesten-Stigum Regime
papers.abstract:
We show that outlier eigenvectors of the Bethe Hessian achieve weak recovery in the stochastic block model down to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, for every fixed common expected degree $d>1$. This extends previous recovery guarantees, which required $d$ to be sufficiently large. This threshold is information-theoretically optimal for the symmetric two-community model and is conjectured to mark the limit of efficient recovery in broader symmetric models. Our result matches the recovery guarantees of non-backtracking spectral methods while using Hermitian $n\times n$ matrices.
  To do this, we identify recursive formulas for the negative outlier eigenvalues and show that their eigenspaces have nonvanishing overlap with the corresponding planted eigenspaces. The proof constructs approximate eigenvectors from the planted labels on the limiting Poisson tree, with weights given by its Green's function, and transfers these approximations to the finite graph.

papers.title: Critical curl extremals and the hyperbolic plane
papers.abstract: We study the critical Sobolev-curl quotient on $\mathbb{R}^3$ at the conformally invariant exponent $p=3/2$. Its sharp constant and optimizers were posed as open problems in the literature. We identify the toroidal and poloidal extremals. Two structural facts are used. First, the critical curl--curl equation is self-dual: the map $u\mapsto|\nabla\times u|^{-1/2}\nabla\times u$ is an involution on finite-energy solutions. It is the self-dual case of a duality between the exponents $p$ and $3p/(4p-3)$, which exchanges toroidal and poloidal fields and relates the sharp constants. Second, the toroidal minimization problem reduces exactly to a subcritical $3/2$-Laplace problem on the hyperbolic plane. Combined with symmetry and shooting results, these facts show that the two restricted sharp constants coincide. They also classify the gauge-minimal extremals: these are unique up to scaling and the Euclidean transformations realizing hyperbolic isometries, semi-explicit, and dual to each other. For nonzero one-signed profiles radial about a fixed hyperbolic centre, a gauge-canonical inverse of the duality yields an iteration by one-dimensional quadratures: the quotients are nonincreasing and converge to the restricted sharp constant, while the normalized iterates converge to the extremal pair. The first step from an explicit competitor gives the new upper bound $96\sqrt{15}\pi/(5\sqrt{4455\pi-13568})\approx11.2948$ for the restricted constants. The unrestricted sharp constant remains open. As an application, bounded axisymmetric poloidal potentials admit no $L^2$ zero mode of the Weyl-Dirac operator. An explicit conformal transformation extends this exclusion to both extremals at every real coupling.

papers.title: Coxeter Rigidity and ADE Classification of Fibonacci-Generated Tensor Categories
papers.abstract: We propose a program to classify tensor categories generated by prescribed seed tensor categories. We carry out this program for finitely many marked copies of the positive Fibonacci category with pairwise nonisomorphic generating simple objects, in the setting of split locally finite semisimple rigid $\CC$-linear tensor categories with simple unit. We show that the Fibonacci fusion relation forces the fusion rules to be those of a specialized Coxeter--Hecke ring. The systems admitting categorification have Coxeter exponents $2,3,\infty$. For every such system we construct a tensor category and prove uniqueness up to marked tensor equivalence. Its simple objects are indexed by the Coxeter group, which may be infinite. Finite rank occurs precisely for disjoint unions of finite ADE diagrams, giving the ADE classification of Fibonacci-generated fusion categories. These categories are unitarizable, with no unitary structure assumed on the candidate. In finite ADE type, allowing Yang--Lee seeds gives one independent tensor-branch choice on each connected component.

papers.title: Fractional Differential Equations in Chemical Modeling: From Memory and Anomalous Transport to Mathematically Justified Models
papers.authors: Ravshan Ashurov, Nigora Qutlimurotova, Ilyoskhuja Sulaymonov
papers.abstract:
Fractional differential equations are increasingly used to model memory and anomalous transport in chemistry and related fields. However, the formal replacement of an integer-order derivative by a fractional one does not by itself justify fractional dynamics. The essential issue is whether nonlocality can be derived from a physical, stochastic, geometric, or reduction mechanism and whether it leads to experimentally testable consequences.
  This review, written primarily for mathematicians and specialists in fractional analysis, discusses representative applications in electrochemistry, adsorption and sorption, reaction--subdiffusion, chemical and enzyme kinetics, polymer relaxation, and atmospheric chemistry. Particular attention is paid to distinguishing mechanism-based fractional models from phenomenological fractionalizations.
  Mathematical questions of well-posedness, nonnegativity, conservation laws, dimensional consistency, parameter identifiability, and numerical convergence are emphasized. Experimental electrochemical examples illustrate the need to distinguish genuine fractional effects from model mismatch or non-identifiability. Several open problems connecting fractional analysis with experimentally grounded chemical modeling are formulated.

papers.title: The Alon-Tarsi number of 4-regular circulant graphs
papers.abstract: This paper studies the Alon-Tarsi number of connected $4$-regular circulant graphs $C_n(s,t)$, where $1\le s<t<n/2$. We prove that if $n=\ell p^r$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $r\ge 1$, and $t\equiv\pm s\pmod{\ell}$, then $\operatorname{AT}(C_n(s,t))=3$ if $\ell$ is even, or if $\ell\ge 3$ is odd and $p\nmid 2^\ell-2$. We also prove that $\operatorname{AT}(C_{6m}(2,3))=3$ for $m\ge 2$, and $\operatorname{AT}(C_n(1,3))=3$ for $n\ge 8$.

papers.title: Holomorphic functions and hulls of Matsuki-dual orbits of $SU(p,q)$ in complex Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Let $G_0$ be a real form of a complex semisimple group acting on a flag manifold $Z$, with maximal compact subgroup $K_0$ and its complexification $K$. Matsuki duality pairs each $G_0$-orbit $\gamma$ with a $K$-orbit $\kappa$, and $M=\kappa\cap\gamma$ is a compact $K_0$-orbit. For lower-dimensional $\gamma$, $M$ is a compact CR manifold, and we ask which functions are holomorphic near $M$ and what its holomorphic hull is. In general, we show that $K_0$-finite holomorphic functions near $M$ are regular functions on $K$-orbits, and that $M$ carries non-constant holomorphic germs if some $K$-stable prime divisor of $Z$ misses $\kappa$, and, under a connectedness hypothesis, only constants otherwise. For $G_0=SU(p,q)$ acting on any Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_k(\mathbb{C}^{p+q})$ we give a complete answer. Holomorphic functions near $M$ are constant unless $M$ is of holomorphic type: $k\in\{p,q\}$ and $M$ lies in the Harish-Chandra chart of the bounded symmetric domain $\mathcal{D}$. Then $M$ is the manifold of rank-$c$ partial isometries, and a holomorphic hull of $M$ is $\overline{\mathcal{D}}\cap\{\mathrm{rank}\le c\}$. This agrees with the polynomial hull of Kaup and Zaitsev except in one totally real case, where it is strictly smaller because $\det^{-1}$ is holomorphic near $U(p)$. The same dichotomy decides when global CR functions on $M$ are constant and when holomorphic sections of line bundles near $M$ are global; its exceptions differ from the Gindikin-Matsuki exceptions for cycle spaces, except at the base point of $\mathcal{D}$. This settles the descent question left open in earlier work with K. Shabbir on rank-one orbits. We also determine which $K$-orbits carry non-constant regular functions, prove constancy via chains of rational curves for small $c$, and compute Levi forms in examples.

papers.title: Decomposing super unitary representations using Berezin integration
papers.abstract: I introduce the notion of a family of super unitary representations depending upon odd parameters as well as the notion of a direct Berezin integral of such representations. I use this to decompose the (left-)regular representation of the super Heisenberg group and of a super Heisenberg-like group into smaller (irreducible) subrepresentations. I compare the obtained subrepresentations to the representations obtained by applying (super) geometric quantization of the coadjoint orbits of the corresponding groups. It turns out that for the super Heisenberg group we need coadjoint orbits with an odd symplectic form in order to describe all subrepresentations found in the decomposition and for the Heisenberg-like super group we even need orbits with a non-homogeneous symplectic form.

papers.title: Revisiting the directed pathwidth of h-semicomplete digraphs
papers.authors: Guilherme C. M. Gomes, Raul Lopes, Matthias Mnich
papers.abstract: A digraph is $h$-semicomplete if every vertex has at most $h$ non-neighbors. In semicomplete digraphs, $k$-triples are obstructions to bounded directed pathwidth with many algorithmic applications: Fradkin and Seymour [JCTB 2013] showed that a large triple contains a subdivision of every small digraph, and triples were used for irrelevant vertex arguments in routing problems by Fomin and Pilipczuk [JCTB 2019] and Gomes, Lopes, and Sau [ICALP 2025]. Fradkin and Seymour also showed that there is a function $f(k)$ such that every semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth at least $f(k)$ contains a $k$-triple, and their proof gives $f(k)$ triply exponential in $k$. For $h$-semicomplete digraphs, a result of Kitsunai et al. [ESA 2015] also yields a $k$-triple, but only existentially, and finding one in fixed-parameter time remained open. We improve the bound on $f(k)$ to a single exponential and extend the result to $h$-semicomplete digraphs: we show that every $h$-semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth greater than $(h+1) \cdot k \cdot 2^{27k+9}$ contains a $k$-triple, which we find in polynomial time, and no bound subexponential in $k$ or sublinear in $h$ is possible. We also extend the approximation algorithm for directed pathwidth of Fomin and Pilipczuk to $h$-semicomplete digraphs, so its certificates of large directed pathwidth remain valid. Our proof is much shorter than the analysis of Kitsunai et al., and while their algorithm is exact, ours runs in polynomial time. As an application, we show that Arc-Disjoint Paths on $h$-semicomplete digraphs is fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of paths and $h$, generalizing the semicomplete case. Finally, unlike in semicomplete digraphs, directed pathwidth does not bound directed cliquewidth: for every $k$, some acyclic $1$-semicomplete digraph, so of directed pathwidth zero, has directed cliquewidth at least $k$.

papers.title: A conjecture on Galois groups and large fields
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a field such that $p$ is prime to the absolute Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$, in the sense that $p$ does not divide the degree of any finite Galois extension of $K$. We conjecture that $K$ is large in the sense of Pop: any smooth algebraic curve $C$ over $K$ with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points. This conjecture would have some consequences in mathematical logic. For instance, it would imply the expected classification of stable fields of positive characteristic. We give some weak evidence for this conjecture. Specifically, suppose that $K$ is a perfect field and $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$ is prime to $p$. Then every abelian variety $A$ over $K$ has Zariski dense $K$-rational points, and if $C$ is a smooth curve of genus less than $7-p$ with at least one $K$-rational point, then $C$ has infinitely many $K$-rational points.

papers.title: Area laws for free fermions in ergodic field: spectral criteria and localisation-based methods
papers.abstract: We review rigorous results concerning the Area Law for the entanglement entropy of free fermions whose one-body Hamiltonian is an ergodic Schr\"odinger operator with a strongly localised pure point spectrum. Particular attention is paid to operators with deterministic potentials (quasi-periodic ones and those generated by subshifts of finite type). Our approach relies on reducing the problem to obtaining exponential estimates for the eigenfunction correlator. This provides an effective route from localisation to the Area Law and allows for the identification of additional spectral estimates that need to be proven for various classes of ergodic operators. We realise this approach by using various localisation techniques, including dynamical localisation and the uniformly localised eigenfunction property for bounded and unbounded ergodic operators (e.g. the Maryland model), as well as a new method for obtaining the corresponding exponential bounds for Schr\"odinger operators generated by subshifts of finite type.

papers.title: Improved estimation of differential entropy of a multivariate Gaussian distribution
papers.abstract: We consider estimation of entropy of a multivariate variate normal distribution with unknown mean vector and unknown covariance matrix. Using a decision-theoretic approach, we study the problem under a general location-invariant loss function that is strictly convex and minimized at zero. We first characterize the class of affine equivariant estimators and obtain the best affine equivariant estimator. We further show that the best affine equivariant estimator is inadmissible under the general loss. Exploiting information in the sample mean, we derive Stein-type improved estimators, including an extension to the case of a mean matrix. Under the linex loss, we obtain a smooth Brewster--Zidek-type estimator that dominates the best affine equivariant estimator, and we show that this estimator is generalized Bayes under a suitable non-informative prior.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of the dual solution for obstacle problems in the space BV
papers.abstract: We consider the variational problem of minimizing the multiple integral $\int_\Omega f(\nabla u) \, dx$ with a convex density $f$ being of linear growth among functions $u$: $\Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the Dirichlet boundary condition $u = u_0$ on $\partial\Omega$ and for which $u \ge \Psi$ holds throughout the domain $\Omega$. We prove that the dual problem has a unique solution. This result is extended to the case of interior obstacle problems, where the validity of $u \ge \Psi$ is only required on a subset $E$ of $\Omega$. Moreover, we discuss the vectorial setting, i.e. the case of functions $u$: $\Omega \to \mathbb{R}^N$, $N > 1$, combined with the additional condition $u(\Omega) \subset A$ for a closed convex set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^N$, again showing the existence and the uniqueness of the associated dual solution.

papers.title: Channel dichotomies
papers.abstract: We study channel interconversion under non-signalling superchannels, where the asymptotic conversion rate is given by the ratio of the channel capacities. Our main result determines the second-order expansion of the optimal target length. Namely, when each channel has a single capacity-achieving dispersion, the coefficient is given by the inverse sesquinormal distribution, with parameters determined by the capacities and dispersions. The result extends state-dichotomy theory to channels: one superchannel approximates the target uniformly over inputs and maps every reference channel whose output is independent of its input to another such channel. As in state dichotomies, there are finite-error resonances where the second-order term vanishes, leaving an $O(\log n)$ remainder. Crucially, our new characterization cannot be obtained by concatenating channel coding and simulation protocols [Cao {\it et al.}~IEEE Trans.~Inf.~Theory (2024)]. Instead, the proof combines comparisons of binary hypothesis testing experiments with uniform Gaussian estimates and a construction that uses symmetry within type classes to satisfy the non-signalling constraints. Shared randomness assistance already suffices at first order, but we show that its second-order behaviour can differ strictly from the non-signalling case.

papers.title: Batch Universal Prediction via Conditional Additive Smoothing
papers.abstract: Modern language models motivate renewed interest in universal prediction problems in which a predictor can exploit previously observed data before predicting a fresh sequence. We study an idealized version of this setting by introducing \emph{batch regret}: a conditional analogue of classical average regret in which a predictor observes a batch of $n$ training sequences and is then evaluated on an independent test sequence generated by the same unknown source. Additive smoothing estimators, which add a bias to the observed token frequencies before predicting the next token, played a fundamental role as a simple prediction strategy with almost-optimal average regret for memoryless and Markov sources. Their equivalent under batch regret are the conditional additive smoothing estimators, which estimate the conditional distribution of the test sequence given the training batch. In this work, we study their asymptotical batch regret for binary memoryless and first-order Markov sources. For binary memoryless sources, we show how the optimal bias of the estimator, and consequently the corresponding batch regret, change as a function of the training batch size $n$, by extending the Poisson-based analysis of Krichevsky. For binary Markov sources with positive transitions, we characterize the leading coefficient of batch regret and its dependence on whether the initial law is known, free, or stationary. Finally, we introduce a R\'{e}nyi analogue of batch regret and identify the corresponding optimal predictors as conditional $\alpha$-NML estimators, thereby giving an operational interpretation to a conditional version of Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information.

papers.title: Rates and Nearly-Lossless State over a Multi-Access Channel with Causal State Information
papers.abstract: The problem of transmitting both data and state over a memoryless state-dependent multi-access channel with causal state information is addressed. The state comprises three independent components: a common component, which is revealed to both en- coders, and two private components, each of which is revealed to a different encoder. The data are to be recovered with arbitrarily-small probability of error, and the state sequence with arbitrarily-small symbol-error rate. Under the assumption that the capacity region in the absence of a state recon- struction constraint is nonempty, the capacity region is derived and is shown to be achievable using a Block-Markov coding scheme employing binning and superposition coding.

papers.title: Loose Inductive Set Theories
papers.abstract: We prove that KP, with Full Set Induction, is neither solid nor tight. More generally, every consistent theory obtained from KPC by adding a quantifier bounded set of sentences has a model with a parameter-free definable class surjection from its natural numbers onto its universe. Using such enumerations to define generic extensions by relative interpretations, we show that theories with the stable definable ground property are not tight. Ground definability over MOST and continuum coding over ZFC^{\Pi_3} yield applications to weak inductive set theories with large cardinals and forcing axioms. Finally, solidity for quantifier bounded extensions of MOST with Full Set Induction implies a Ground Axiom formulated using a fixed finite level of genericity; under the same solidity hypothesis, the corresponding extension of full ZFC proves the ordinary Ground Axiom.

papers.title: The twistor construction of toric gravitational instantons
papers.authors: Maciej Dunajski, Lionel Mason, Paul Tod
papers.abstract: We give an explicit construction of all ALF and ALE toric gravitational instantons in terms of certain rational matrix functions of one complex variable on the Riemann sphere; these provide patching matrices for their corresponding twistor holomorphic vector bundles. The reconstruction of the instantons arises from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert splitting problem and we show how this can be solved via linear algebra, resembling but not equivalent to the Belinski--Zakharov ansatz. This construction gives a complete classification together with an explicit form for all toric gravitational instantons up to the resolutions of conical and orbifold singularities. We illustrate the formalism by computer--assisted numerical construction of two new ALF (but not AF) gravitational instantons with five nodes.

papers.title: A four-dimensional residue calculus for quaternionic slice regular functions
papers.abstract: We develop a 4-dimensional residue calculus for quaternionic slice semiregular functions. Its local singularities are isolated real poles and 2-dimensional spheres. For the latter, we introduce a spherical residue and characterize it as a spherical Laurent coefficient, as the sum of two classical residues on any full complex slice, and by a finite differential procedure involving alternating spherical and slice derivatives. The residue theorem expresses a weighted boundary flux on a circular domain as the sum of the real and spherical residues it contains. Beyond this formula, polynomially weighted flux moments recover every coefficient of every finite principal part, including the companion coefficient at a spherical pole, invisible to ordinary residue summation. Once the polar components and order bounds are fixed, the quotient of the real polynomial ring by the global pole polynomial is the finite-dimensional algebra of weights. We prove that the residue pairing is well defined and nondegenerate, and identifies formal principal parts with the full quaternion-valued real dual of this algebra. Hermite interpolation and the Chinese remainder theorem provide global weights selecting each local coefficient. We separate the regularity domain of the function from the geometry of integration: for a smooth noncircular integration domain compactly contained in a circular ambient domain, away from the reals and with boundary disjoint from the polar set, we establish an exact residue formula with an explicit volume correction governed by the Cauchy-Fueter operator. The theory includes higher-order poles, exceptional points, product domains, and zero divisors. Applications give formulas for rational and oscillatory integrals on the imaginary hyperplane and characterize the rational data on the 3-dimensional imaginary subspace of the quaternions admitting a canonical slice regular extension.

papers.title: A Finite-Range, Translation-Invariant Counterexample to Weak Gibbsianity
papers.abstract: We construct a finite-range, translation-invariant counterexample to the Weak Gibbsianity property for quantum spin systems on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. The proof relies on showing how a local potential can induce macroscopically large deviations from an equilibrium configuration after a perturbation is introduced at the boundary of the lattice.

papers.title: On the Geroch conjecture for toric gravitational instantons
papers.authors: Lars Andersson, Mattias Dahl, Gustav Nilsson
papers.abstract: Geroch conjectured that the local solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations with two commuting Killing fields and vanishing twist constants are generated from flat space by an infinite-dimensional group of transformations, and Hauser and Ernst proved this for stationary axisymmetric spacetimes near the axis. The solutions generated from flat space by the transformations with finitely many poles in the spectral parameter are the solitons of Belinski and Zakharov. We prove a solitonic form of the conjecture in Riemannian signature, for toric gravitational instantons. The proof combines Weinstein's uniqueness argument, a closed formula for the soliton metrics in Hankel determinants and a degree argument. It also applies to the toric Ricci-flat metrics with conical singularities constructed by Li and Sun.

papers.title: Taylor-type joint spectrum and essential spectrum of row-bounded sequences of commuting operators
papers.authors: Penghui Wang, Fan Zhang, Ruoyu Zhang, Zeyou Zhu
papers.abstract: As the cornerstone of multivariable operator theory, (essential) Taylor's joint spectrum plays crucial roles in many areas. The present paper is devoted to developing the theory of (essential) Taylor-type joint spectrum of row-bounded sequences of commuting operators on Hilbert spaces and to establishing the associated Fredholm index theory. Furthermore, the holomorphic functional calculus for row-bounded sequences is established. At last, we obtain a Gleason-Richter-Sundberg type index theorem in the infinite-variable setting, which connects the Fredholm index, the asymptotic Arveson's curvature invariant and fibre dimensions.

papers.title: Finite Composites of the Fibonacci Category with Pointed Fusion Categories
papers.abstract: We classify finite composites of the positive Fibonacci category with arbitrary pointed fusion categories, retaining the entire source functor and making no unitarity assumption on the target. Formal codegrees, dimension fields, and algebraic integrality exclude all dihedral Fibonacci rings $R_n$ with $n\ge4$ from categorification. Together with an independent graphical uniqueness argument, this gives the finite two-Fibonacci classification. For several marked Fibonacci generators, a geometric height-and-polygon argument identifies the based ring with a standard-basis Coxeter--Hecke ring. Transitive conjugation by the pointed image forces the noncommutation graph to be empty or a perfect matching. We then obtain a crossed-product classification in terms of a quotient group, a stabilizer, labelled Fibonacci or rank-six $\TT$ blocks, and compatible cocycle and categorical action data. This includes the Fibonacci--$\Z/3\Z$ composite problem without target unitarity. We also establish the corresponding forms and marked descent statements over characteristic-zero fields admitting the chosen Fibonacci-type input.

papers.title: On approximate support versions of Donoho--Stark uncertainty principles for $k$-Hadamard operators
papers.abstract: In this paper we present results related to Donoho--Stark type uncertainty principles that were proved in the article "The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme" by Wigderson and Wigderson for $k$-Hadamard operators in the finite-dimensional setting. Namely, the authors showed that Donoho-Stark principles can be generalized to versions for approximate supports with respect to norms $\ell^{p}$ for $p=1$ and $p=2$. In the second case they assumed the so-called speciality condition, namely that a suitable matrix satisfies $A^{*}A = kI$. First we show that such theorems cannot be generalized to $p>1$ if matrices are not special $k$-Hadamard. Next we prove Donoho-Stark type principle for special $k$-Hadamard operators for $\ell^{p}$ norms within the range $1\leq p\leq 2$. Finally, we show that such theorems are false for $p>2$ even in the presence of the speciality condition.

papers.title: Lax-idempotent monads in homotopy theory
papers.abstract: We extend the theory of lax-idempotent monads to the setting of $(\infty,2)$-categories. In particular, we prove an analogue of Kock and Z\"oberlein's characterization of the category of algebras over a lax-idempotent monad. We then apply this theory to many examples that arise naturally in homotopy theory. For example, we show that $(\infty,1)$-toposes are monadic over presentable $(\infty,1)$-categories, with left adjoint given by the symmetric $(\infty,1)$-topos. We also show that $\infty$-operads are comonadic over symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories through the monoidal envelope construction, obtaining along the way a new proof of Barkan-Steinebrunner's result that the envelope functor is a faithful inclusion. We furthermore use this theory to simplify Ramzi's proof that dualizable stable $(\infty,1)$-categories are comonadic over $\aleph_1$-compactly generated stable $(\infty,1)$-categories.

papers.title: Localisation and delocalisation of the integer-valued membrane model
papers.authors: Alessandra Cipriani, Biltu Dan, Rajat Subhra Hazra
papers.abstract: We study the integer-valued membrane model on boxes $[-L,L]^d\cap\mathbb{Z}^d$ with zero boundary conditions. We show that in dimension two the model is delocalised at sufficiently high temperature. More precisely, the variance at the origin is of order $L^2/\beta$, where $\beta$ is the inverse temperature. More generally, for every $\epsilon>0$ and all sufficiently small $\beta>0$, the logarithm of each Laplace transform lies between $(1+\epsilon)^{-1}$ and $1$ times its Gaussian counterpart. The temperature threshold is independent of $L$ and the test function. In dimensions three and four, we prove that the variance at the origin is bounded uniformly in the box size at every positive inverse temperature. Thus the integer constraint changes the order of fluctuations in these dimensions. The proofs use a modification of the Fr\"ohlich--Spencer argument in dimension two and a comparison with integer-valued Gaussian free fields in higher dimensions.
