For fixed $\varepsilon > 0$, we prove that DRO still achieves the minimax rate if the problem has bounded residual effective rank. On the other hand, we identify significant failure modes where DRO is provably suboptimal by dimension-dependent factors. Fortunately, we prove that two alternative procedures, minimax regret optimization (MRO) and spectral-norm regularization (SNR), attain the minimax rate. We derive an exact convex reformulation of MRO and an accelerated proximal algorithm for SNR, along with high-probability finite-sample guarantees. We support these theoretical results with numerical experiments separating the performance of MRO and SNR from DRO.

papers.title: Functional Tensor Trains for High-Order Greeks and Exposure Tails of Multi-Asset Structured Products
papers.authors: Javier Lopez-Piqueres, Atithi Acharya, Yue Sun, Niraj Kumar
papers.abstract: Risk management of worst-of autocallables needs price sensitivities (Greeks) up to third order and the potential future exposure, a tail quantile of the note's future value. In Monte Carlo, each order of differentiation multiplies the sampling noise by a factor that grows with the observation frequency, and nested simulation turns the noise of its inner paths into a bias of the quantile. We instead solve the backward pricing recursion, storing the continuation value as an $hp$ functional tensor train (hp-FTT) whose piecewise-polynomial cores are split at the barriers, so that worst-of barrier events act exactly, with rank one. For Gaussian transitions we show that the polynomial degree sufficient for an error $\varepsilon$ grows only as $\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}$. One solve then gives every Greek at any spot without sampling noise, by integrating the likelihood-ratio weight against the stored value, and the values it stores at future dates replace inner simulation. Against the strongest Monte Carlo estimators we could build or find published, on worst-of autocallables observed monthly on three to five assets, the order of the Greek and the accuracy decide which method is cheaper. At $1\%$ accuracy Monte Carlo is more than an order of magnitude cheaper for deltas, second-order Greeks go either way, and hp-FTT is cheaper for every third-order Greek, by up to two orders of magnitude. At $0.1\%$ hp-FTT is cheaper for every Greek we could check, under geometric Brownian motion and local volatility alike. For the exposure alone Monte Carlo is cheaper at $1\%$ and hp-FTT at $0.1\%$, and a solve run for the Greeks yields it for little more than scenario sampling. Sampling pays in variance for each derivative and hp-FTT in rank for each asset, so Monte Carlo keeps low-order Greeks at percent accuracy, rarely observed contracts and many assets.

papers.title: Time-optimal quantum dynamics under fixed-norm generators
papers.abstract: We investigate the dynamics of quantum systems whose evolution is governed by linear generators of fixed unitarily invariant norm. For this broad class of evolutions, we derive a universal time-optimal generator of the dynamics converting one given state into another. It provides a time-optimal non-Hermitian Hamiltonian for pure state conversion. We then use this general result to derive quantum speed limits for mixed-state evolutions governed by Lindbladians and non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. Our findings follow from the geometric properties of the group $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, in particular the geodesic distance. The derived bounds hold for an arbitrary system size $n$, depend only on the norms of the evolution generator and the initial and final states, and do not require performing any time-averaging.

papers.title: Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger
papers.abstract: Instance-dependent limits for bandit regret, sequential tests, best-arm identification and Markov decision processes are proved by one chain. It runs from a divergence decomposition through data processing to a statistic, a testing step that turns a class guarantee into a requirement on the history, and optimization over alternatives and allocations. Only the first step is an identity. This work writes the chain as an exact ledger. By the chain rule, data processing loses exactly a conditional divergence, which vanishes for arms in natural exponential families at the per-arm counts and reward sums. A one-parameter family of martingale identities extends the decomposition to every tilt between two instances. The classical limits follow by relaxations with named defects. All defects but the asymptotic step's can be computed from an algorithm's own runs, the uniform quantification's only when the class guarantee is a number. On seven published sources, from movie ratings to engine replacement, the ledger locates the difference between standard algorithms and the classical limits. For identification among trained models and for Wald's test the largest term is usually the uniform quantification's.

papers.title: Site Percolation on Multi-dimensional Lattice
papers.abstract: Sites in an infinite d-dimensional lattice, open with probability greater or equal to 1/d, form an infinite open path.

papers.title: On kernel Mengerian orientations of line multigraphs
papers.abstract: A kernel of a digraph is an independent set $K$ such that every vertex outside $K$ has an arc to a vertex in $K$. We present a polyhedral description of kernels in clique-acyclic orientations of line multigraphs. Given a digraph $D$, let $FK(D)$ denote its fractional kernel polytope, and let $\sigma(D)$ denote the linear system defining $FK(D)$. A digraph $D$ is called kernel perfect if every induced subdigraph has a kernel, called kernel ideal if the fractional kernel polytope of every induced subdigraph is integral, and called kernel Mengerian if the defining system of every induced subdigraph is totally dual integral. We show that a clique-acyclic orientation of a line multigraph is kernel ideal if and only if it is kernel Mengerian. These equivalent properties hold precisely when the orientation is kernel perfect and has no even-cycle obstruction.

papers.title: The gauge fixing theorem with applications to the Yang-Mills flow over Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: In 1982, Uhlenbeck \cite {U2} established the well-known gauge fixing theorem, which has played a fundamental role for Yang-Mills theory. In this paper, we apply the idea of Uhlenbeck to establish a parabolic type of gauge fixing theorems for the Yang-Mills flow and prove existence of a weak solution of the Yang-Mills flow on a compact $n$-dimensional manifold with initial value $A_0$ in $W^{1,n/2}(M)$. When $n=4$, we improve a key lemma of Uhlenbeck (Lemma 2.7 of \cite {U2}) to prove uniqueness of weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow on a four dimensional manifold.

papers.title: Geometrization of almost extremal representations in $\text{PSL}_2\Bbb R$
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a closed surface of genus $g$. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between hyperbolic cone-structure on $S$ and representations of the fundamental group into $\text{PSL}_2\Bbb R$. We consider surfaces of genus greater than $g$ and we show that, under suitable conditions, every representation $\rho:\pi_1 S\longrightarrow \text{PSL}_2\Bbb R$ with Euler number $\mathcal{E}(\rho)=\pm\big(\chi(S)+1\big)$ arises as holonomy of a hyperbolic cone-structure $\sigma$ on $S$ with a single cone point of angle $4\pi$. From this result, we derive that for surfaces of genus $2$ every representation with $\mathcal{E}(\rho)=\pm1$ arises as the holonomy of some hyperbolic cone-structure.

papers.title: Asymptotics of principal evaluations of Schubert polynomials for layered permutations
papers.authors: Alejandro H. Morales, Igor Pak, Greta Panova
papers.abstract: Denote by $u(n)$ the largest principal specialization of the Schubert polynomial: $ u(n) := \max_{w \in S_n} \mathfrak{S}_w(1,\ldots,1) $ Stanley conjectured in [arXiv:1704.00851] that there is a limit $\lim_{n\to \infty} \, \frac{1}{n^2} \log u(n), $ and asked for a limiting description of permutations achieving the maximum $u(n)$. Merzon and Smirnov conjectured in [arXiv:1410.6857] that this maximum is achieved on layered permutations. We resolve both Stanley's problems restricted to layered permutations.

papers.title: Infinite periodic groups of even exponents
papers.abstract: We give a new proof that free Burnside groups of sufficiently large even exponents are infinite. The method is very flexible and can also be used to study (partially) periodic quotients of any group which admits an action on a hyperbolic space satisfying a weak form of acylindricity.

papers.title: Hecke Algebra-valued Poincar\'e Series and Geometric Factorization of Affine Weyl Groups
papers.abstract: This paper studies affine Weyl groups through the geometry of geodesic tubes and their hyperbolic stabilizers. We introduce a geometric framework relating affine Weyl group factorizations to Hecke-algebra-valued Poincar\'e series and zeta functions on quotient complexes. Using this framework, we prove a conjecture describing the connection between geodesic tubes and factorizations of Poincar\'e series for affine Weyl groups. We also establish partial results toward a Hecke-algebra-valued zeta identity for simply connected groups, including the cases of types $\widetilde{A}_{n-1}$ and $\widetilde{C}_n$. These results highlight the interaction between affine Weyl group geometry, Hecke algebras, and zeta functions arising from Bruhat--Tits buildings.

papers.title: On the Mourre estimates for three-body Floquet Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: In this paper,we consider the Floquet Hamiltonian $K$ associated with a three-body Schr\"odinger operator with time-periodic pair potentials $H(t)$. By introducing a conjugate operator $A$ for $K$ in the standard Mourre theory, we prove the Mourre estimate for $K$. As by-products of the Mourre estimate for $K$, the minimal velocity estimates for the physical propagator $U(t,0)$ generated by $H(t)$ as well as the propagator $e^{-i\sigma K}$ generated by $K$ can be obtained.

papers.title: Small measure expansion in connected noncompact groups
papers.authors: Jinpeng An, Yifan Jing, Chieu-Minh Tran, Ruixiang Zhang
papers.abstract:
Assuming $G$ is unimodular and $K>1$, and that $\mu(A^2) < K \mu(A)$. We show that this is a continuous surjective group homomorphism $\chi: G \to L$ with a compact kernel, where $L$ is a Lie group satisfying $$\dim(L) \leq \lfloor\log K\rfloor(\lfloor\log K\rfloor+1)/2.$$ This dimension bound is sharp, We also establish the relationship between $A$ and its image under the quotient map, and obtain a more general version of this result for the product set $AB$ without assuming unimodularity.
  We present two applications:
  (1) An inverse Kemperman theorem in noncompact groups. Let $G$ be a connected, noncompact, locally compact group with a left Haar measure $\mu$, and let $A$ and $B$ be nonempty, compact subsets of $G$. We classify all cases where $G$, $A$, and $B$ exhibit nearly minimal expansion properties (in the unimodular case, this means $\mu(AB)$ is close to $\mu(A) + \mu(B)$). This result completes the noncompact cases of the Kemperman inverse problem and resolves a question posed by Griesmer and Tao.
  (2) An effective generalized Margulis lemma for discrete subgroups of almost-connected locally compact groups acting properly by isometries. If $B(x,4r)$ can be covered by $K$ translates of $B(x,r)$ at one point and one scale, it gives a small radius $r/2M$, and the group generated at this radius has a subgroup of index at most $M \exp((\log K)^4)$ which is nilpotent modulo a finite normal subgroup. The nilpotency step is bounded by $(\log K)^2$, and \[ M\leq K^{\exp(C(\log K)^4\log\log K)} \] and $C$ is an absolute constant.

papers.title: Distinction and quadratic base change for regular supercuspidal representations
papers.abstract: In this article, we study Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations based on the machinery developed by Hakim and Murnaghan to study distinguished representations, and the fundamental work of Kaletha on parameterization of regular supercuspidal representations. For regular supercuspidal representations, we give some new interpretations of the numerical quantities appearing in Prasad's formula, and reduce the proof to the case of tori. The proof of Prasad's conjecture then reduces to a comparison of various quadratic characters appearing naturally in the above process. We also have some new observations on these characters and study the relation between them in detail. For some particular examples, we show the coincidence of these characters, which gives a new purely local proof of Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of these groups. We also prove Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of G(E), when E/F is unramified and G is a general tamely ramified quasi-split reductive group.

papers.title: A proof of Ryser's circulant Hadamard conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that an $n\times n$ circulant Hadamard matrix must satisfy a family of congruence equations that have solutions only when $n \leq 4$, proving Ryser's 1963 conjecture that no such matrices exist for $n>4$.

papers.title: The Fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra over nontrivially valued fields and the radius of convergence of nonarchimedean differential equations
papers.abstract: We prove a fundamental theorem for tropical partial differential equations, analogous to the fundamental theorem of tropical geometry in this context. We extend results from Aroca et al., Falkensteiner et al. and from Fink and Toghani for the case of trivial valuation as introduced by Grigoriev to differential equations with power series coefficients over any valued field. Crucial ingredients are the framework for tropical partial differential equations introduced by Giansiracusa and Mereta and a result on infinite intersections of projections of fibers of tropicalizations, which we prove using Hrushovski and Loeser's model-theoretic interpretation of Berkovich analytification. As a corollary of the fundamental theorem, we show that the radius of convergence of solutions of an ordinary differential equation over a nontrivially valued field can be computed tropically.

papers.title: Full-Duplex-Enabled Integrated Sensing and Communications: Opportunities and Challenges
papers.authors: Chandan Kumar Sheemar, George C. Alexandropoulos, Sourabh Solanki, Eva Lagunas, Jorge Querol, Symeon Chatzinotas
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) is one of the six usage scenarios of IMT-2030, with in-band full duplex (IBFD) being the most direct way to realize it. In this paradigm, a base station that transmits and receives on the same time-frequency resources can sense continuously with its own downlink waveform while serving uplink traffic. This article revisits full-duplex-enabled ISAC (FD-ISAC) in light of the technologies lately shaping sixth-generation (6G) radio design, such as extremely large multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems operating in the near field, holographic and dynamic metasurface apertures, fluid and movable antennas, beyond-diagonal reconfigucable intelligent surfaces (BS-RISs) and wave-domain processing with stacked intelligent metasurfaces. We present a holistic FD-ISAC architecture built around a multi-stage, echo-preserving self-interference cancellation chain, and map each 6G technological enabler to the gains it brings and the risks it introduces. A case study with a $28$~GHz full-duplex XL-MIMO base station showcases that near-field-aware beamforming combined with wave-domain, analog, and digital cancellation delivers more than twice the throughput of half-duplex and 3GPP sub-band full-duplex baselines at the same localization-accuracy bound. It is also demonstrated that incorporating a group-connected BD-RIS recovers most of the fully-connected gain at a small fraction of its circuit complexity. The article concludes discussing emerging use cases and open challenges.

papers.title: Characteristic polynomials and eigenvalues of tensors
papers.authors: Francesco Galuppi, Fulvio Gesmundo, Ettore Teixeira Turatti, Lorenzo Venturello
papers.abstract: We lay the geometric foundations for the study of the characteristic polynomial of tensors. For symmetric tensors of order $d \geq 3$ and dimension $2$, and symmetric tensors of order $3$ and dimension $3$, we prove that only finitely many tensors share any given characteristic polynomial, unlike the case of symmetric matrices and the case of non-symmetric tensors. We propose precise conjectures for the dimension of the variety of tensors sharing the same characteristic polynomial, in the symmetric and non-symmetric settings.

papers.title: Periodic Tunnel Systems: Reeb Graph Representations and Circular Max-Flow
papers.abstract: Inspired by the study of transport properties in materials science, we investigate the Reeb graph of a map \(f:X\to\Ss\), interpreting \(X\) as a periodic tunnel system in which transport takes place. The map \(f\) encodes a chosen periodic direction and induces a directed structure on the graph. Under constructibility, we establish a lifting result for directed paths that makes precise how the graph represents tunnel segments in \(X\). To turn this representation into a numerical transport descriptor, we equip the graph with cross-sectional capacities defined, in a Riemannian setting, by weighted Hausdorff-measure integrals. Under boundary regularity and Morse assumptions in dimension \(d\ge2\), we establish continuity over regular Reeb values and continuity of the total capacity across fibers. Taking edgewise infima gives the bottleneck capacities for a circular max-flow formulation, which measures flow through fibers of the map to the circle without choosing an arbitrary inlet or outlet. The resulting descriptor is computable by linear optimization and is related to minimum-cost circulations. For nonnegative real capacities, we prove that the max-flow value is invariant under periodic unrolling: the same descriptor is obtained whether the medium is modeled by a toroidal cell or by its periodic replication along the chosen direction. Simulations on periodic point clouds illustrate the construction and the effects of imposing source--target cuts.

papers.title: Maximal Inequalities for Empirical Processes under General Mixing Conditions
papers.abstract: This paper provides a bound for the supremum of sample averages over a class of functions for a general class of mixing stochastic processes with arbitrary mixing rates. Regardless of the speed of mixing, the bound is comprised of a concentration rate and a novel measure of complexity. The speed of mixing, however, affects the former quantity implying a phase transition. Fast mixing leads to the standard root-n concentration rate, while slow mixing leads to a slower concentration rate whose speed depends on the mixing structure. Our findings are applied to obtain new Glivenko-Cantelli type results.

papers.title: Birational geometry of log Calabi-Yau pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3, D)$ of coregularity 2
papers.abstract: This paper aims to study the birational geometry of log Calabi-Yau pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3, D)$ of coregularity 2, where in this case $D$ is an irreducible normal quartic surface with canonical singularities. We completely classify which toric weighted blowups of a point will initiate a volume preserving Sarkisov link starting with this pair. Depending on the type of singularity, our results point out that some of these weights do not work generically for a general member of the corresponding coarse moduli space of quartics.

papers.title: Turning non-smooth points into rational points
papers.abstract: In a recent paper, the author and St\"ohr established a bound on the number of iterated Frobenius pullbacks needed to transform a non-smooth purely inseparable point on a regular geometrically integral curve into a rational point. In this paper we improve this result, by establishing a new bound that is sharp in every characteristic $p>0$.

papers.title: Asymptotic geometry of non-abelian Hodge theory and Riemann--Hilbert correspondence, rank three $\widetilde{E}_6$ case
papers.abstract: We prove the Geometric P=W conjecture in rank 3 on the three-punctured sphere. We describe the topology at infinity of the related character variety. We use asymptotic abelianization of harmonic bundles away from the ramification divisor and an equivariant approach near the branch points to find the WKB (also known as Liouville--Green or phase-integral) expansion of the involved maps. We analyze the Stokes phenomenon governing their behavior.

papers.title: Learning Maximal Regions of Attraction on Compact Sets using Taylor Lyapunov Networks
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of learning maximal Lyapunov functions to compute the maximal region of attraction of nonlinear dynamical systems using neural networks. Two obstacles limit existing neural-network approaches: 1) finite-width approximations can fail to preserve the strict Lyapunov inequalities near the equilibrium, where they become arbitrarily weak, and 2) training is necessarily performed on a bounded computational domain for which the classical Lyapunov and Zubov theorems do not directly apply. To address these issues, first we derive Lyapunov and Zubov theorems directly on a prescribed compact computational domain, characterizing the maximal region of attraction within that domain as the solution of a boundary-value PDE. Second, we introduce the Taylor Lyapunov network, an architecture that prescribes the quadratic leading-order term via the system's linearization and represents the higher-order remainder through a structured cubic factorization, guaranteeing that any network in this class is a valid local Lyapunov function by construction. Finally, we prove that Taylor Lyapunov networks are universal approximators of maximal Lyapunov functions on compact domains, and combine these results into an unsupervised, physics-informed training procedure. Numerical experiments on systems of varying dimensions and stability types show that the proposed architecture is efficient at estimating the maximum region of attraction.

papers.title: Algebraic tori in the complement of quartic surfaces
papers.authors: Eduardo Alves da Silva, Fernando Figueroa, Joaqu\'in Moraga
papers.abstract: Let $B\subset \mathbb{P}^3$ be an slc quartic surface. The existence of an embedding $\mathbb{G}_m^3\hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^3\setminus B$ implies that $B$ has coregularity zero. In this article, we initiate the classification of coregularity zero slc quartic surfaces $B\subset \mathbb{P}^3$ for which $\mathbb{P}^3\setminus B$ contains an algebraic torus $\mathbb{G}_m^3$, and equivalently, the classification of cluster type pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3,B)$. Along the way, we give criteria for a log Calabi--Yau pair $(X,B)$ over a toric variety $T$ to be of cluster type.

papers.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Local and Global Solutions for a Partial Differential-Algebraic Equation of Index One
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use the theory of nonlinear semigroups to establish the existence and uniqueness of both local and global solutions for a partial differential-algebraic equation (PDAE) of index one. This method is applied to a reaction-diffusion system coupled with an elliptic equation in one dimension by transforming the PDAE into a system of linear evolution equations with a Lipschitz-continuous perturbation

papers.title: Curved $\infty$-Local Systems And Projectively Flat Riemann-Hilbert Correspondence
papers.abstract: We generalize the higher Riemann-Hilbert correspondence in the presence of scalar curvature for a (possibly non-compact) smooth manifold $M$. We show that the dg-category of curved $\infty$-local systems, the dg-category of graded vector bundles with projectively flat $\mathbb Z$-graded connections and the dg-category of curved representations of the singular simplicial set of the based loop space of $M$ are all $A_\infty$-quasi equivalent. They provide dg-enhancements of the subcategory of the bounded derived category of twisted sheaves whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant and have finite-dimensional fibers. In the ungraded case, we reduce to an equivalence between projectively flat vector bundles and a subcategory of projective representations of $\pi_1(M; x_0)$. As an application of our general framework, we also prove that the category of cohesive modules over the curved Dolbeault algebra of a complex manifold $X$ is equivalent to a subcategory of the bounded derived category of twisted sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules which generalizes a theorem due to Block to possibly non-compact complex manifolds.

papers.title: Relatively-Secure LLM-Based Steganography via Constrained Markov Decision Processes for High-Efficiency Embedding
papers.authors: Yu-Shin Huang, Chao Tian, Krishna Narayanan, Lizhong Zheng
papers.abstract: Linguistic steganography aims to conceal information within natural language text without being detected. An effective steganography approach should encode the secret message bits into a minimal number of language tokens while preserving the natural appearance and fluency of the stego-texts. We present a new framework to enhance the embedding efficiency by framing the steganographic embedding procedure as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP), which takes into consideration the long-term dependencies instead of merely the immediate effects. We constrain the solution space such that the discounted expected cumulative total variation between the selected conditional probability distribution and the original one given by the LLM is below a threshold. To find the optimal policy, we first show that the functional optimization problem can be simplified to a convex problem with a finite number of variables. For the binary-state model, we give a full characterization of the optimal policy, including closed-form expressions in several regimes, and show that it displays water-filling-like behavior in certain cases. The solution indicates that states with highly deterministic transition distributions are preferable for adjustment in the binary-state case. For larger state spaces, the optimal solution is more complex and explicit solutions are difficult to obtain, but the optimal policies show similar structural behaviors.

papers.title: Quadratic obstructions to Small-Time Local Controllability for the multi-input bilinear Schr\"odinger equation
papers.abstract: We investigate the small-time local controllability (STLC) near the ground state of a bilinear Schr\"odinger equation when the linearized system is not controllable. It is well known that, for single-input systems, quadratic terms in the state expansion can then lead to obstructions to the STLC of the nonlinear system. In this work, we extend this phenomenon to the multi-input setting, presenting the first example of multi-input quadratic obstructions for PDEs. Our results build upon our previous study of such obstructions for ODEs and provide a functional framework for analyzing them in the bilinear Schr\"odinger equation.

papers.title: On the surjectivity of Galois representations attached to Drinfeld $A$-modules of rank $2$
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, where $q$ is a prime power and let $A:= \mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$ and $F:= \mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. By~\cite{PR09}, the adelic image of the Galois representation attached to a generic Drinfeld $A$-module $\varphi$ of rank $2$ over $F$ satisfying $\mathrm{End}_{\bar{F }}(\varphi)=\varphi(A)$ is open, and determining when it is surjective remains a subtle problem. To resolve this question, in this article, we study the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic surjectivity of the Galois representations attached to $\varphi$, where $\mathfrak{p} \in \Omega_A:= \mathrm{Spec}(A) \setminus \{ (0) \}$. There are two directions to investigate this problem: one by fixing the prime $\mathfrak{p}$, and the other by fixing $\varphi$.
  In the horizontal direction, for a fixed $\mathfrak{p} \in \Omega_A$, we give explicit and easily verifiable conditions on Drinfeld $A$-modules $\varphi$ of rank $2$ over $F$ which ensure the surjectivity of the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic Galois representation $\rho_{\varphi,\mathfrak{p}}$. This work extends~\cite{Ray24} to arbitrary $\mathfrak{p}$, and, for $\mathfrak{p}=(T)$, recovers the results of~\textit{loc. cit.} under weaker hypotheses.
  In the vertical direction, we show that for a fixed Drinfeld $A$-module $\varphi$ of rank $2$ over $F$, whose coefficients satisfy certain congruence and valuation conditions, the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic Galois representation $\rho_{\varphi,\mathfrak{p}}$ is surjective for all $\mathfrak{p} \in \Omega_A$. This recovers the example of \cite{Zyw11} and yields new examples beyond those considered in \cite{Zyw25}. As a consequence, we obtain the surjectivity of the associated adelic Galois representation.

papers.title: NumPSLA -- An experimental research tool for pseudoline arrangements and order types
papers.abstract: We present a program for enumerating all pseudoline arrangements with a small number of pseudolines and abstract order types of small point sets. This program supports computer experiments with these structures, and it complements the order-type database of Aichholzer, Aurenhammer, and Krasser. This system makes it practical to explore the abstract order types for 12 points, and the pseudoline arrangements of 11 pseudolines.

papers.title: Transition in the asymptotics of the joint degree distribution of uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic joint degree distribution of uniformly chosen vertices in uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs, a natural generalization of random recursive trees. Here, a graph is built by adding vertices one-by-one and connecting each new vertex to $m\in\mathbb{N}$ uniformly selected vertices already present. Using a representation based on Kingman's coalescent, we establish a transition in the joint degree distribution at the threshold $(m+1)\log n$, arising from the interplay between geometric degree asymptotics and fluctuations in the coalescent construction. Our results extend previously known asymptotics toward this threshold and provide a unified description of the transition, including mixed regimes where prescribed degrees lie on different scales.

papers.title: Quantum Velocity Averaging (or Not...) in the Semiclassical Regime
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the possibility of applying the velocity averaging theorems in [F. Golse, P.-L. Lions, B. Perthame, R. Sentis: J. Funct. Anal. 76(1):110--125, 1988] to the Wigner equation governing the quantum evolution of the Wigner transform of quantum density operators. Our first main results address the case of the Wigner function of a special class of density operators associated to mixed states, whose Hilbert-Schmidt norm is of order $\hbar^{d/2}$, where $d$ is the space dimension and $\hbar$ the reduced Planck constant. In space dimension $d=1$, we prove that the density function belongs to the Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb R)$ for some $s>0$. In the case of pure states, we first obtain a characterization of the Wigner transform of rank-one quantum density operators, and apply this characterization (1) to analyze a rather general setting in which velocity averaging cannot apply to the Wigner functions of a family of rank-one density operators whose evolution is governed by the von Neumann equation, and (2) to obtain a quick derivation of Madelung's system of quantum hydrodynamic equations. This derivation provides a physical explanation of one key assumption used in the proof of the negative result (1) described above.

papers.title: On almost Gallai colourings in complete graphs
papers.authors: Alexandr Grebennikov, Let\'icia Mattos, Tibor Szab\'o
papers.abstract: We investigate a rainbow analogue of the Ruzsa--Szemer\'edi problem. For $t \in \mathbb{N}$, we say that a colouring of $E(K_n)$ is almost $t$-Gallai if no two rainbow $t$-cliques share an edge. Motivated by a lemma of Berkowitz on bounding the modulus of the characteristic function of clique counts in random graphs, we study the maximum number $\tau_t(n)$ of rainbow $t$-cliques in an almost $t$-Gallai colouring of $E(K_n)$. For every $t \ge 4$, we show that $n^{2-o(1)} \leq \tau_t(n) = o(n^2)$. For $t=3$, surprisingly, the behaviour is substantially different. Our main result establishes that $$\left ( \frac{1}{2}-o(1) \right ) n\log n \le \tau_3(n) \le O\big (n^{\sqrt{2}}\log n \big ),$$ which gives the first non-trivial improvements over the simple lower and upper bounds. Our proof combines various applications of the probabilistic method and a generalisation of the edge-isoperimetric inequality for the hypercube.

papers.title: A Riemannian approach for PDE-constrained shape optimization over the diffeomorphism group using outer metrics
papers.authors: Estefania Loayza-Romero, Lidiya Pryymak, Kathrin Welker
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the use of outer metrics, in particular Sobolev-type metrics on the diffeomorphism group in the context of PDE-constrained shape optimization. Leveraging the structure of the diffeomorphism group we analyze the connection between the push-forward of a smooth function defined on the diffeomorphism group and the classical shape derivative as an Eulerian semi-derivative. We consider in particular, two predominant examples on PDE-constrained shape optimization. An electric impedance tomography inspired problem, and the optimization of a two-dimensional bridge. These problems are numerically solved using the Riemannian steepest descent method where the descent directions are taken to be the Riemannian gradients associated to various outer metrics. For comparison reasons, we also solve the problem using other previously proposed Riemannian metrics in particular the Steklov-Poincar\'e metric.

papers.title: Co-evolving vertex and edge dynamics in dense graphs
papers.authors: Siva Athreya, Frank den Hollander, Adrian R\"ollin
papers.abstract: We consider a random graph in which vertices can have one of two possible colours. Each vertex switches its colour at a rate that is proportional to the number of vertices of the other colour to which it is connected by an edge. Each edge turns on or off according to a rate that depends on whether the vertices at its two endpoints have the same colour or not. We prove that, in the limit as the graph size tends to infinity and the graph becomes dense, the graph process converges, in a suitable path topology, to a limiting Markov process that lives on a certain subset of the space of coloured graphons. In the limit, the density of each vertex colour evolves according to a Fisher-Wright diffusion driven by the density of the edges, while the underlying edge connectivity structure evolves according to a stochastic flow whose drift depends on the densities of the two vertex colours.

papers.title: Period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions for $\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$
papers.authors: Yubo Jin, Jian-Shu Li, Dongwen Liu, Binyong Sun
papers.abstract: Using the modular symbol approach, we prove the rationality and period relations for certain critical values of Rankin-Selberg L-functions for $\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$ over any number field that contains a CM field.

papers.title: Interpolation in Polynomial Spaces of p-Degree
papers.authors: Phil-Alexander Hofmann, Damar Wicaksono, Michael Hecht
papers.abstract: We recently introduced the Fast Newton Transform (FNT), an hierarchical algorithm for performing multivariate Newton interpolation in arbitrary downward closed polynomial spaces of spatial dimension $m$. Here, we analyze the FNT in the context of a specific family of downward closed sets $A_{m,n,p}$, defined as all multi-indices with $\ell^p$ norm less than $n$ with $p \in [0,\infty]$. The FNT performs with time complexity $\mathcal{O}(|A_{m,n,p}|mn)$ on the induced downward closed polynomial spaces $\Pi_{m,n,p}$. We show that the $\Pi_{m,n,p}$ choice compared to the tensor product spaces $\Pi_{m,n,\infty}$, reduces time complexity by a factor of $\rho_{m,n,p}$, decaying super exponentially with spatial dimension when $m \lesssim n^p$. We showcase the efficiency of the FNT by computing activity scores in sensitivity analysis.

papers.title: Coherent configurations and Frobenius structures
papers.authors: Dominik Lachman, Gejza Jen\v{c}a, Anna Jen\v{c}ov\'a
papers.abstract: We prove that coherent configurations can be represented as modules over Frobenius structures in the category of real nonnegative matrices. We generalize the notion of admissible morphism from association schemes to coherent configurations. We show that the Frobenius structure associated to a coherent configuration can be modified to become a dagger Frobenius structure, and use this to connect the coherent configurations to groupoids and $H^*$-algebras. We examine the properties of the dagger Frobenius structure with respect to admissible morphisms. We introduce the matrix $O$ obtained as the composition of comultiplication and multiplication of the dagger Frobenius structure and prove that we may obtain the valencies of colors, and thus recover the original coherent configuration, as an eigenvector of $O$. In the last part of the paper, we examine the spectrum of $O$ and apply it to generalize the Lagrange theorem from groups to association schemes.

papers.title: Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs: resilience and approximate decompositions
papers.authors: Nemanja Dragani\'c, Jaehoon Kim, Hyunwoo Lee, David Munh\'a Correia, Mat\'ias Pavez-Sign\'e, Benny Sudakov
papers.abstract: Dirac's classical theorem asserts that, for $n\ge 3$, any $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $\frac{n}{2}$ is Hamiltonian. Furthermore, if we additionally assume that such graphs are regular and sufficiently large, then, by the breakthrough work of Csaba, K\"uhn, Lo, Osthus, and Treglown, they admit a decomposition into Hamilton cycles and at most one perfect matching, solving the well-known Nash-Williams conjecture. In the pseudorandom setting, it has long been conjectured that similar results hold in much sparser graphs. We prove two overarching theorems for graphs that exclude excessively dense subgraphs, which yield asymptotically optimal resilience and Hamilton-decomposition results in sparse pseudorandom graphs. Firstly, our results imply that for every fixed $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that if $G$ is a spanning subgraph of an $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph satisfying $\delta(G)\ge\bigl(\tfrac12+\gamma\bigr)d$ and $d/\lambda\ge C$, then $G$ must contain a Hamilton cycle. Secondly, we show that for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $C>0$ so that any $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph $G$ with $d/\lambda\ge C$ contains at least $\bigl(1-\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, and, finally, we prove that the entire edge set of $G$ can be covered by no more than $\bigl(1+\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ such cycles. All bounds are asymptotically optimal and significantly improve earlier results on Hamiltonian resilience, packing, and covering in sparse pseudorandom graphs.

papers.title: Exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s with Compactly Supported Diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We show that for diffeomorphisms of closed simply-connected $4$-manifolds dissolving under a single stabilization, there is a natural induced diffeomorphism on an exotic copy of $\RR^4$. We thereby construct uncountably many exotic copies of $\RR^4$ with nontrivial compactly supported mapping class groups of arbitrarily large rank. This follows from a modification of the construction of the diffeomorphism corks of arXiv:2407.04696 that makes their exteriors simply-connected.

papers.title: Irreducible representations of tree automorphism groups into Pontryagin spaces
papers.abstract: Let G = Aut(T) be the automorphism group of a regular tree T. We study continuous irreducible representations of G that preserve a continuous strongly nondegenerate sesquilinear form of finite index on a Hilbert space. These are already classified for index 0 (unitary case) and for index 1. We show that there are no more representations for index > 1, which completes the classification.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and asymptotic behavior of large strong solutions to the 3D full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients
papers.authors: Yachun Li, Peng Lu, Zhaoyang Shang
papers.abstract: It is well known that the global well-posedness of the Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients is a challenging problem, especially in multi-dimensional space. In this paper, we study the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients in the whole space. When the initial density and the initial temperature are linearly equivalent to some large constant states, we establish the first result on the global existence of large strong solution. Moreover, the optimal decay rates of the solution to its associated equilibrium are established when the initial data belong to $L^{p_0}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for some $p_0\in[1,2]$.

papers.title: Constructing and transforming standard resolutions of local modules
papers.abstract: We construct standard resolutions for analytic local modules on complex hypersurfaces using standard basis methods, with extensions to complete intersections. The algebraic version over arbitrary infinite fields is also suggested. Applications include derived category formula of local hypersurface blow-ups, revealing new connections between standard bases and categorical geometry.

papers.title: A Markovian Approach for Cross-Category Complementarity in Choice Modeling
papers.authors: Omar El Housni, Shuo Sun, Rajan Udwani
papers.abstract: In modern retail and e-commerce, customers often purchase multiple items across distinct product categories, exhibiting both substitution and complementarity. We consider the cross-category assortment optimization problem where retailers jointly determine assortments across categories to maximize expected revenue. Most prior work on the topic either overlooks complementarity or proposes models that lead to intractable optimization problems, despite being based on the multinomial logit (MNL) choice model. We propose a sequential multi-purchase choice model for cross-category choice that incorporates complementarity through a Markovian transition structure across categories, while allowing general Random Utility Maximization (RUM)-based choice models to capture the within-category substitution. We develop an Expectation-Maximization algorithm for estimation, and a polynomial-time algorithm for unconstrained assortment optimization that yields the optimal solution when the within-category substitution follows a Markov chain choice model. Furthermore, we introduce an empirical metric to quantify the strength of complementarity across product categories and conduct extensive numerical experiments using both synthetic data and a large-scale transaction-level dataset from a major U.S. grocery store. Our model improves predictive accuracy and model fit in both synthetic and real-data experiments and improves expected revenue in synthetic settings with complementarity. It also reveals intuitive market structures such as brand-loyal cross-category purchasing. Overall, we believe that our model provides a theoretically grounded and practical framework for modeling complementarity and making better cross-category assortment decisions.

papers.title: Simple and Sharp Generalization Bounds via Lifting
papers.abstract: We bound the supremum of stochastic processes using a rate-distortion functional analogous to classical entropy integrals. A lifting argument embeds the process into a higher-dimensional space with permutation symmetry, reducing the analysis to a stationary process. This gives a two-sided characterization of the supremum of Gaussian processes, including cases where Dudley's entropy integral is not sharp. Combining the sharpness of Dudley's integral for stationary processes with information-theoretic arguments gives a proof of the majorizing measure theorem. The method also yields localized generalization bounds without a slicing argument. As an application, we derive risk bounds for empirical risk minimization over Lipschitz images of Sobolev ellipsoids. Our proof does not use the majorizing measure theorem.

papers.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, remixed
papers.abstract: For each endotrivial complex for a $p$-group arising from Bredon homology of a representation sphere, we construct $p$-local quasi-isomorphisms, called forerunners. These enable us to extend Balmer--Gallauer's results concerning the tensor-triangular geometry of permutation modules for elementary abelian $p$-groups to all $p$-groups. We construct an open cover of the Balmer spectrum under which all endotrivials are tt-line bundles, that is, every endotrivial is locally isomorphic to a shift of the tensor unit. We define a remixed permutation twisted cohomology ring for which the canonical comparison map from the Balmer spectrum to the homogeneous spectrum of the twisted cohomology ring is injective. If the twisted cohomology ring is Noetherian, the comparison map is an open immersion, and the open cover endows the Balmer spectrum with Dirac scheme structure. We prove Noetherianity holds for Dedekind groups and the dihedral group of order 8, and conjecture it holds for all $p$-groups.

papers.title: Distributed Information Bottleneck Theory for Multi-Modal Task-Aware Semantic Communication
papers.authors: Yujie Zhou, Cheng Peng, Rulong Wang, Yong Xiao, Yingyu Li, Guangming Shi, Ping Zhang
papers.abstract: Semantic communication shifts the focus from bit-level accuracy to task-relevant semantic delivery, enabling efficient and intelligent communication for next-generation networks. However, existing multi-modal solutions often process all available data modalities indiscriminately, ignoring that their contributions to downstream tasks are often unequal. This not only leads to severe resource inefficiency but also degrades task inference performance due to irrelevant or redundant information. To tackle this issue, we propose a novel task-aware distributed information bottleneck (TADIB) framework, which quantifies the contribution of any set of modalities to given tasks. Based on this theoretical framework, we design a practical coding scheme that intelligently selects and compresses only the most task-relevant modalities at the transmitter. To find the optimal selection and the codecs in the network, we adopt the probabilistic relaxation of discrete selection, enabling distributed encoders to make coordinated decisions with score function estimation and common randomness. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrate that our solution matches or surpasses the inference quality of full-modal baselines while significantly reducing communication and computational costs.

papers.title: Matrix-valued regular functions of a quaternionic variable - a decomposition and some approximation results
papers.abstract: A quaternionic matrix-valued regular function is a map $F: \Omega \rightarrow M_n(\mathbb{H})$ whose entries are (left) regular functions of a quaternionic variable, where $\Omega$ is a domain in $\mathbb{H}$. Given any $n \times n$ matrix-valued regular function $F(q)$ over $\mathbb{H}$ having norm at most $1$, we derive a decomposition of $F(q)$ in the form $U \star \begin{bmatrix} ||F(q_0)|| & 0\\0 & G(q)\end{bmatrix} V$ for some constant unitary matrices $U, V$, some vector $q_0$ and an $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ matrix-valued regular function $G(q)$, where $\star$ denotes the star product over $\mathbb{H}$. We use this to prove a Fisher-type approximation result for matrix-valued regular functions $F(q)$ on the quaternionic unit ball $\mathbb{B}$: if $F(q)$ has norm at most $1$ and is continuous on the boundary of the ball, then $F(q)$ can be uniformly approximated by a convex combination of matrix-valued rational unitary functions on $\overline{\mathbb{B}}$.

papers.title: Achiral Lefschetz fibrations and the moduli space of curves
papers.abstract: Symplectic Lefschetz fibrations can be described via classifying maps with values in the Deligne-Mumford compactification of the moduli space of curves, by means of constructions relying on symplectic geometry. In this note we prove the existence of classifying maps for achiral Lefschetz fibrations using Riemannian geometry. We further extend Smith's signature formula to the achiral case, providing a more elementary proof of this statement.

papers.title: Degeneration of Derived Quot schemes, Lagrangian Foliations, and categorical Donaldson-Thomas invariants
papers.abstract:
We develop a derived-geometric framework for Donaldson--Thomas invariants in semistable Calabi--Yau threefold degenerations. Derived restriction from the two smooth components of the central fiber to their common anticanonical divisor is Lagrangian. We give explicit universal-family diagrams for this structure, compare the deformation complexes with perfect complexes on the singular union, and construct the fourfold duality using a canonical bundle pulled back from the base. On specified Quot presentations we describe the real Lagrangian foliation and its shifted potential.
  We formulate proper-completion and cohomological-comparison conjectures for sheaves arising from sections of an extending line bundle. Their specialization is described by oriented two-sided bar complexes and a finite Gauss--Manin system.

papers.title: Circular law for non-Hermitian block band matrices with slowly growing bandwidth
papers.abstract: We consider the empirical eigenvalue distribution for a class of non-Hermitian random block tridiagonal matrices $T$ with independent entries. The matrix has $n$ blocks on the diagonal and each block has size $\ell_n$, so the whole matrix has size $n\ell_n$. We assume that the nonzero entries are i.i.d. with mean 0, variance $(3\ell_n)^{-1}$ and having finite moments of all orders. We prove that when the entries have a bounded density, then whenever $\lim_{n\to\infty}\ell_n=\infty$ and $\ell_n=O(\operatorname{Poly}(n))$, the normalized empirical spectral distribution of $T$ converges almost surely to the circular law. The growing bandwidth condition $\lim _{n\to\infty}\ell_n=\infty$ is the optimal condition for the circular law with small bandwidth. This confirms the folklore conjecture that the circular law holds whenever the bandwidth increases with the dimension; earlier circular-law proofs required the delocalized regime $\ell_n\gg n$.

papers.title: On the tensor-triangular geometry of isotropic motives
papers.abstract: We investigate the tensor-triangular geometry of the categories of isotropic Tate motives, isotropic Artin motives and isotropic Artin--Tate motives. In particular, we study the categories $DTM_{gm}(k/k;\mathbb{F}_2)$, $DAM_{gm}(k/k;\mathbb{F}_2)$ and $DATM_{gm}(k/k;\mathbb{F}_2)$ where $k$ is a flexible field and we fix $\mathbb{F}_2$-coefficients. In this case, we prove their Balmer spectra are singletons. The proof of this relies on the fact that the categories in question are generated by objects whose morphisms are `nilpotent enough.' Furthermore, we investigate their homological spectra, and verify Balmer's Nerves of Steel conjecture in these cases by showing these spaces are also singletons, and we give an explicit description of the homological primes. We also investigate stratification, and we conclude by studying generation properties of these categories -- the latter results we see also apply to global (i.e. non-isotropic) motives.

papers.title: Spectral decomposition and entropy for open set-valued maps
papers.authors: C\'assio H. Vieira Morais, T\'ulio Vales, Rafael Da C. Pereira
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the dynamics of set-valued maps whose graphs are open and such that the image of each point is an open and connected set. Building upon the work of P. Duarte and M. Torres, who introduced and analyzed the combinatorial structure of the final recurrent set, we incorporate the notions of transitivity and mixing, thereby bringing their framework into the spirit of Smale's spectral decomposition theorem. We also demonstrate that such maps exhibit infinite topological entropy, and we establish a connection between transitive open set-valued maps and transitive Anosov diffeomorphisms.

papers.title: Distributional properties of first jump times of CBI processes with jump sizes in given Borel sets
papers.authors: Matyas Barczy, Sandra Palau, Yao Xue
papers.abstract: We derive an expression for the joint distribution function of the first jump times of a continuous state and continuous time branching process with immigration (CBI process) with jump sizes in given Borel sets having finite total L\'evy measures, where by total L\'evy measure, we mean the sum of the measures appearing in the branching and immigration mechanisms of the CBI process in question. Our result generalizes a corresponding result of He and Li (2016), who considered this problem in case of a single Borel set having finite total L\'evy measure.

papers.title: Closed Colored Models and Demazure Crystals
papers.abstract:
We construct and study solvable lattice models whose partition functions are Demazure characters. Two types of colored generalizations of the five-vertex model can be defined that are called the open and closed models. States of both models are associated with Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns, or equivalently, semistandard Young tableaux. We characterize the tableaux arising from states of the closed model and prove that they form a Demazure crystal. This is stronger than identifying the partition function as a Demazure character: it requires constructing Kashiwara crystal operators on the states through lattice moves and recoloring. For the open model, Brubaker, Bump, Buciumas, and Gustafsson showed that the states realize (crystal) Demazure atoms. We also give a new, independent proof of their result.
  Bump and Naprienko considered bosonic models involving a parameter t. In these models, the edges and vertices are constructed by fusion of simpler edge and vertex types. Taking t=0 produces bosonic analogs of the open model. By reversing the fusion order, we construct closed bosonic models and establish their Yang-Baxter equations, yielding a Demazure-Lusztig recursion for the partition functions. At t=0, these models specialize to bosonic analogues of the closed five-vertex model, and we prove that their states form Demazure crystals.

papers.title: Interpretation of a Discrete de Rham method as a Finite Element System
papers.abstract: Within the framework of Finite Element Systems (FES) we define a numerical method for computing differential forms, inspired by the Discrete de Rham (DDR) method. The discrete $L^2$ product of DDR is given a new interpretation, as a computable approximation of the true $L^2$ product on local spaces of forms defined by partial differential equations. Without significantly modifying the numerical method itself, this point of view provides an alternative approach to the analysis. The conformity and consistency properties we obtain are stronger than those previously shown, even in low dimensions. We can also recover some of the other results that have been proved about DDR, from those that have already been proved, in principle, in the general context of FES. Parts of the analysis involve a conjectural hypothesis of stability of constants, with respect to small mesh perturbations, that we detail. We also bring VEM, the Virtual Element Method, into the discussion. For convenience, background material on the FES framework is reviewed.

papers.title: A polynomial dimension-dependence analysis of Bramble--Pasciak--Xu preconditioners
papers.authors: Boou Jiang, Jongho Park, Jinchao Xu
papers.abstract: We investigate the dimension dependence of Bramble--Pasciak--Xu~(BPX) preconditioners for simplicial $\mathbb{P}_1$ finite element discretizations of high-dimensional partial differential equations and establish that the condition numbers of BPX-preconditioned systems grow only polynomially with the spatial dimension. Our analysis requires a careful derivation of the dimension dependence of several fundamental tools in the theory of finite element methods, including elliptic regularity, the Bramble--Hilbert lemma, trace inequalities, and inverse inequalities. We further analyze an averaged Scott--Zhang-type quasi-interpolation operator, and show that its associated constants scale polynomially with the dimension. Building on these ingredients, we prove a multilevel norm equivalence theorem and derive a BPX preconditioner with explicit polynomial bounds on its dimensional dependence. The analysis is motivated in part by recent tensor and quantum finite element methods, where dimension-explicit conditioning estimates for BPX preconditioners play an important role.

papers.title: On classifications of third- and fourth-order symmetric tensors by eigenvalues
papers.abstract: This paper addresses two fundamental problems posed by Qi regarding the sufficiency of eigenvalues for the classification of symmetric tensors in the two-dimensional setting. For $2\times2\times2$ and $2\times2\times2\times2$ complex symmetric tensors, we classify their equivalence classes using canonical forms of their associated binary cubics and quartics. We then determine the number of eigenpair classes and the multiplicities of zero eigenvalues for the canonical forms over the complex domain. We demonstrate that these spectral counts do not distinguish all real equivalence classes. Finally, we extend this approach to derive canonical forms and classification for real third- and fourth-order linear partial differential equations in two variables using their bijective relationship to binary forms.

papers.title: Critical metrics for the quadratic curvature functional on complete four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We study complete four-dimensional Riemannian metrics on connected manifolds that are critical for the curvature functional $\A(g)=\int_M|\Rm|^2\,\vol$ and have finite curvature energy. If $\langle\Ract\E,\E\rangle\ge0$, where $\E=\Ric-\frac14\Scal\,g$ and $\Ract$ is the curvature action on symmetric two-tensors, then the metric is either Einstein or locally isometric to a product of surfaces of constant Gaussian curvatures $c$ and $-c$, with $c\ne0$. This extends the corresponding compact classification to the complete setting with finite curvature energy.

papers.title: The variety of orthogonal frames
papers.abstract: An orthogonal n-frame is an ordered set of n pairwise orthogonal vectors. The set of all orthogonal n-frames in a d-dimensional quadratic vector space is an algebraic variety V(d,n). In this paper, we investigate the singularities and components of the variety V(d,n), as well as the algebraic properties of the quadratic ideal I(d,n) generated by the orthogonality relations, which cuts out V(d,n) set-theoretically. By a general result of Ananyan and Hochster, these objects satisfy increasingly strong regularity conditions when d becomes large compared to n; we establish optimal effective bounds to quantify this behavior. We give criteria for the ideal I(d,n) to be prime or a complete intersection, thereby resolving open problems proposed by Conca and Welker. We give criteria for the variety V(d,n) to be normal or factorial. We provide strong evidence in support of the conjecture that I(d,n) defines V(d,n) scheme-theoretically. As applications, we improve the existing bounds for when the Lov\'asz-Saks-Schrijver ideals of simple graphs satisfy these four properties.

papers.title: Tight paths in fully directed hypergraphs
papers.authors: Richard C. Devine, Kevin G. Milans
papers.abstract:
It is well-known that every tournament has a spanning path. We consider hypergraph analogues. In an \emph{$r$-uniform fully directed hypergraph}, or \emph{$r$-digraph}, every edge is a list or $r$ distinct vertices. An $(r,k)$-tournament is an $r$-digraph $G$ such that for every $r$-set $S$ of vertices in $G$, exactly $k$ of the orderings of $S$ are edges in $G$. A \emph{directed tight path} is an $r$-digraph $G$ whose vertices can be ordered so that the intervals of size $r$ are the edges in $G$. Let $f(n,r,k)$ be the maximum $s$ such that every $n$-vertex $(r,k)$-tournament contains a tight path on $s$ vertices. Since every tournament has a spanning path, we have $f(n,2,1)=n$.
  In this paper, we show that the minimum $k$ such that $f(n,r,k)$ tends to infinity with $n$ is in the interval $\left[\left(1-\frac{1}{r}-O(\frac{\log r}{r^2\log\log r})\right)r!, ~\left(1-\frac{1}{r} - \frac{\varphi(r)-1}{r!}\right)r!\right]$ where $\varphi(r)$ is the Euler Totient Function, and we find the exact value when $r\le 5$. We also show that $\Omega(\sqrt{\log n/\log \log n}) \le f(n,3,3) \le O(\log n)$ and $f(n,3,4)\ge \Omega(n^{1/5})$.

papers.title: On cohomological dimensions of totally disconnected locally compact groups
papers.authors: Ilaria Castellano, Nadia Mazza, Brita Nucinkis
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce Mackey functors for a t.d.l.c. group and define the cohomological dimension of this group over the Mackey category. We then compare this dimension to the rational discrete cohomological dimension defined by Castellano and Weigel, as well as to the Bredon cohomological dimension of that t.d.l.c. group with respect to the family of compact open subgroups. We also extend results about the geometric dimension of a t.d.l.c. group.

papers.title: Schopieray's Galois-modular extension conjecture
papers.abstract: Plavnik, Schopieray, Yu, and Zhang have drawn attention to those (automatically premodular) fusion subcategories of modular fusion categories which are submodules for the Galois action on the ambient category. In particular, they showed that a subcategory is a Galois submodule if and only if its centralizer is integral. In the other direction, Schopieray has conjectured that every premodular fusion category can be embedded as a Galois-closed subcategory of a modular category; Schopieray calls such an embedding a \emph{Galois-modular extension}. We prove Schopieray's conjecture for pseudounitary categories; in the nonpseudounitary case, we prove that every braided fusion category admits a "Galois nondegenerate extension" but we do not know it to be modular. Along the way we record some general comments about the minimal nondegenerate extension problem for braided fusion categories.

papers.title: Decomposable shuffles
papers.authors: Jo\~ao Dias, Bruno Dinis, Carlos Correia Ramos
papers.abstract: We develop a combinatorial and order-theoretic framework for shuffles, understood as ordered partitions of the natural numbers. We introduce decomposable shuffles as generalised sums of finite ordinals, copies of $\omega$, and copies of its dual $\omega^*$, indexed by countable scattered linear orders. These building blocks are called benches, ladders and snakes, respectively. We introduce a subclass, layered shuffles, and for this subclass we construct an explicit finite-address representation which reduces comparison in the induced order on $\mathbb N$ to lexicographic comparison of integer tuples. We determine the order types of represented layered shuffles, establish that all represented orders are scattered, and define an involution that realises order duality. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical composition on bench-free injective uniform shuffles of fixed sign. For each sign, this operation yields a monoid graded by reduced degree. Its degree-one component is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb N)$ and consists precisely of the invertible elements.

papers.title: Traveling waves near shear flows for the inhomogeneous Euler equations with non-constant density
papers.abstract: We investigate the existence and nonexistence of traveling wave solutions near monotonic shear flows with non-constant background density for the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Euler equations in a finite channel. For any small $\tau>0$, first, we construct nontrivial traveling waves with velocity and density in $H^{5/2-\tau}$ and $H^{3/2-\tau}$, respectively, showing that inviscid damping fails at these regularities. Second, when the distorted Rayleigh operator has no eigenvalues, we prove that such traveling wave solutions cannot exist in higher regularity spaces ($H^{5/2+\tau}$ for velocity and $H^{3/2+\tau}$ for density).

papers.title: Sharp Sobolev inequalities on noncompact Riemannian manifolds with bounded Ricci curvature
papers.authors: Carlo Morpurgo, Stefano Nardulli, Liuyu Qin
papers.abstract: Given a smooth, complete Riemannian manifold $M$ with bounded Ricci curvature and positive injectivity radius, we derive a sharp Sobolev inequality for the embedding of $W^{1,p}(M)$ into $L^{\frac{np}{n-p}}(M)$, when $1\le p< n$. We will first reduce the inequality to functions having support with small enough volume. In turn, we will show that the inequality for small volumes is implied by a first order uniform asymptotic expansion of the isoperimetric profile for $M$, for small volumes. We will then show that such an expansion follows from a local, uniform Sobolev inequality for functions in $W^{1,1}$, having support with small enough diameter.

papers.title: Scott spectral gaps for trees are bounded
papers.abstract: Given a Borel class of trees, we show that there is a tree in that class whose Scott sentence is not too much more complicated than the definition of the class. In particular, if the class is definable by a $\Pi_\alpha$ sentence, then there is a model of Scott rank at most $\alpha + 2$. This gives another proof-and one that does not require first proving Vaught's conjecture for trees-of the fact that trees are not faithfully Borel complete.

papers.title: Sharp Sobolev and Moser-Trudinger inequalities on noncompact Riemannian manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below
papers.abstract: We establish Sobolev and Moser-Trudinger inequalities with best constants on noncompact Riemannan manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below, and positive injectivity radius.

papers.title: Remarks on modules of finite projective dimension
papers.abstract:
We investigate homological and depth-theoretic properties of finitely generated modules of finite projective dimension over Noetherian local rings. A central theme is the study of criteria for freeness and reflexivity derived from the torsion-freeness or reflexivity of tensor products of the form \( M \otimes_R M \) and \( M \otimes_R M^* \). Under mild homological assumptions, we prove that such properties of these tensor products impose strong structural constraints on \( M \), often forcing it to be free. These results generalize classical theorems of Auslander beyond the regular case.
  The second part of the paper is devoted to the dimension and support of Ext-modules, particularly \( \operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M, R) \) for critical values of \( i \), when \( M \) has finite projective dimension. We establish sharp bounds on their Krull dimensions, analyze their behavior for prime and equidimensional modules, and relate these findings to the grade conjecture and other homological conjectures, i.e., whenever $\operatorname{grade}(M) = \operatorname{ht}(\operatorname{Ann}(M))$ where Gdim$(M)<\infty$. We consider the problem that asks whenever is \( \pd_R(M \otimes_R N) = 1 \)? Applications include new cases of a question of Jorgensen, which asks whether \( \operatorname{pd}(M) < i \) whenever \( \operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M, M) = 0 \) and \( M \) has finite projective dimension over a complete intersection ring. Finally, we examine the projective dimension of prime ideals in rings that fail chain conditions.

papers.title: Online Coordinated Scheduling of EV Battery Charging and Heating in Cold Environments
papers.authors: Xiaowei Wang, Yize Chen, Yue Chen
papers.abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) adoption in cold regions is hindered by degraded EV charging performance at low temperatures, which necessitates effective battery thermal management during charging. Given the coupling of battery charging and heating dynamics, this paper explores the benefits of online coordinated charging and heating control, rather than performing them separately. Specifically, we first build queue models for both battery charging and thermal dynamics. Then, we formulate an optimization problem to minimize the system cost of a charging station, which allows us to coordinate charging and heating through maintaining queue stability. To solve the problem, we develop an online coordinated charging and heating control algorithm using Lyapunov optimization techniques. The proposed algorithm is prediction-free and has provable feasibility and optimality guarantees. Numerical experiments based on real-world data demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed method compared to existing benchmarks.

papers.title: General-purpose post-sampling reweighting method for multimodal target measures
papers.abstract: When sampling multi-modal probability distributions, correctly estimating the relative probability of each mode, even when the modes have been discovered and locally sampled, remains challenging. We test a simple reweighting scheme designed for this situation, which consists in minimizing (in terms of weights) the Kullback-Leibler divergence of a weighted (regularized) empirical distribution of the samples with respect to the target measure. We show in a theoretical toy model that the convergence in terms of the number of samples follows the Monte Carlo rate. Numerical experiments on a variety of simple benchmarks are provided, exploring the effect of the ambient dimension, number of modes, number of samples and definition of the modes. We find that, particularly in the situation of interest with well-identified separated modes, the method is able to correct the error in the estimation from the initial sampling of the relative probabilities of the modes.

papers.title: A general equivalence relation on the global class of morphisms of a category
papers.abstract: We introduce a general equivalence relation on the global class of morphisms of a category that subsumes several classical notions of equivalence in mathematics. We show that group-action equivalence relations, pullback equivalence relations, and coarse analysis-operator-based equivalence relations on continuous Bessel families are special cases of this general definition.

papers.title: Approximation classes for adaptive anisotropic space-time finite element methods. An almost characterization
papers.authors: Pedro Morin, Cornelia Schneider, Nick Schneider
papers.abstract: We study the approximation of $L_p$-functions, $p\in (0,\infty]$, on cylindrical space-time domains $\Omega_T:=[0,T]\times \Omega$, $0<T<\infty$, $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ Lipschitz, $d\in \mathbb{N}$, with respect to continuous anisotropic space-time finite elements on prismatic meshes. In particular, we propose a suitable refinement technique which creates (locally refined) prismatic meshes with sufficient smoothness and the desired anisotropy, and prove complexity estimates. Furthermore, we define a (quasi-)interpolation operator on this type of meshes and use it to characterize the corresponding approximation classes by showing direct and inverse estimates in terms of anisotropic Besov norms.

papers.title: A Closed-loop Framework to Discriminate Models Using Optimal Control
papers.authors: Laurent Pagnier, Melvyn Tyloo, Akshita Jindal, Pragati Thakur, Kyle C. A. Wedgwood
papers.abstract: Predicting the response of an observed system to a known input is a fruitful first step to accurately control the system's dynamics. Despite the recent advances in fully data-driven algorithms, the most interpretable way to reach this goal is through mechanistic mathematical modeling. Here, we leverage optimal control and propose a closed-loop iterative method to choose among a set of candidate models the one that most accurately predicts an observed system. We assume that one has control over an input of the observed system and access to measurements of its response. Our approach is to identify the input control that maximally discriminates the response of the candidate models, allowing us to determine which model is best by comparing such responses with the observed data. We demonstrate our proposed framework in numerical simulations before applying it during an electrophysiology experiment, successfully discriminating between different models for photocurrents produced via opsin dynamics.

papers.title: Importance sampling and active subspace in quasi-Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) is widely used in computational finance, and its efficiency strongly depends on the smoothness and effective dimension of the integrand. In this work, we propose a three-step approach, referred to as the IS\_AS\_PI method, which sequentially applies importance sampling (IS), the active subspace (AS) method and preintegration (PI). The proposed method overcomes the problem of empirical failure in constructing active subspaces when nonzero payoff gradients are rarely sampled. Here, empirical failure means that the estimated gradient information matrix is zero and thus provides no useful directions. We establish the orthogonal invariance of active subspaces and IS-active subspaces under suitable conditions. The method is applied to pricing Asian and basket options and estimating the Delta of Asian options under the Black--Scholes model. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method avoids this empirical failure in the deep out-of-the-money cases. Moreover, in all experiments, the proposed method with Laplace IS achieves the largest variance reduction factors, indicating the best performance, among the methods compared.

papers.title: Estimation of the entropy of normal populations under prior information
papers.abstract: In many practical applications, prior knowledge about unknown parameters is available in the form of ordering constraints, and incorporating such information into the inferential procedure can improve the efficiency of the resulting estimators. In this paper, we consider the problem of estimating Shannon's entropy of two normal populations with ordered location parameters under a general location-invariant loss function. We derive the maximum likelihood estimator, the restricted maximum likelihood estimator, and the uniformly minimum variance unbiased estimator. Furthermore, we obtain an estimator that dominates the best affine equivariant estimator. In addition, we propose a smooth estimator that improves upon the best affine equivariant estimator. Moreover, we obtain improved estimators with respect to the Pitman closeness criterion. We consider interval estimation and construct several confidence intervals, such as asymptotic confidence intervals, bootstrap confidence intervals, highest posterior density credible intervals, and the intervals based on generalized pivotal quantities. A Monte Carlo simulation study is conducted to assess the performance of the proposed point and interval estimators. Finally, the proposed methods are illustrated by using two real data sets.

papers.title: Characterizing the optimum bases of a convex geometry using quasi-closed hypergraphs
papers.authors: Anthony Meunier, Lhouari Nourine, Simon Vilmin
papers.abstract: Optimizing an implicational base of a closure system consists in turning this implicational base into an equivalent one with premises and conclusions as small as possible. This task is known to be hard in general but tractable for a number of classes of closure systems. In particular, several classes of convex geometries are known to have tractable optimization, while the problem was recently claimed to remain hard in general convex geometries. Continuing this line of research, we give a characterization of the optimum bases of a convex geometry in terms of what we call quasi-closed hypergraphs. We then use this characterization to show that when each quasi-closed hypergraph has disjoint edges, any implicational base of the convex geometry can be optimized in polynomial time with existing minimization and reduction algorithms. Finally, we prove that this property applies to double-shelling convex geometries, $D$-geometries, convex geometries with the $n$-Carousel property and $q$-acceptant convex geometries, thus unifying and extending the existing results regarding the tractability of optimization.

papers.title: Lower and Upper Expected Hitting Times for Weighted Imprecise Markov Chains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend hitting times for imprecise Markov chains to the framework of weighted imprecise Markov chains (WIMCs), in which each transition is associated with a strictly positive weight encoded by a matrix $W$. Given a convex set $\mathcal{T}$ of admissible transition matrices, we define lower and upper expected hitting times for WIMCs as the infimum and supremum of the (weighted) expected hitting times over $\mathcal{T}$, and we characterise these quantities as the unique solutions of nonlinear fixed-point equations. We show that any weighted hitting time problem can be transformed into an unweighted hitting time problem on an augmented state space, enabling the reuse of existing IMC theory and algorithms. In particular, we are able to adapt known iterative methods for the numerical computation of lower and upper hitting times for WIMCs.

papers.title: Relation between Hitting Times and Probabilities for Imprecise Markov Chains
papers.authors: Marco Sangalli, Erik Quaeghebeur, Thomas Krak
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the relation between hitting times and hitting probabilities in discrete-time imprecise Markov chains (IMCs). We define lower and upper hitting times and probabilities for IMCs whose set of transition matrices $\T$ is compact, convex, and has separately specified rows. Building on reachability-based partitions of the state space, we prove two key implications: (i) finiteness of the upper expected hitting time entails the lower hitting probability equals one, and (ii) finiteness of the lower expected hitting time entails the upper hitting probability equals one. We further show an equivalence: the upper expected hitting time is finite if and only if the lower hitting probability is one. Finally, by presenting a counterexample, we show that the converse of the second implication can fail.

papers.title: On the classifying space of a Morse flow category
papers.abstract: We show that the classifying space of the flow category of a \emph{tame} Morse function on a smooth, closed manifold $M$ recovers the homotopy type of $M$, thereby addressing a claim in a preprint of Cohen--Jones--Segal. The tameness assumption is that the compactified moduli spaces of broken gradient trajectories are locally contractible, ensuring the flow category is topologically well-behaved. We construct a Morse function and Riemannian metric on $S^2\times S^1$ for which the associated flow category fails to recover the correct homotopy type, showing that the tameness hypothesis is crucial.
