Together, these results clarify the extent to which transversality assumptions can be relaxed so that the flow category models the homotopy type of the underlying manifold.

papers.title: Optimal Multi-bit Generative Watermarking Schemes Under Worst-Case False-Alarm Constraints
papers.authors: Yu-Shin Huang, Chao Tian, Krishna Narayanan
papers.abstract: This paper considers the problem of multi-bit generative watermarking for large language models under a worst-case false-alarm constraint. Prior work established a lower bound on the achievable miss-detection probability in the finite-token regime and proposed a scheme claimed to achieve this bound. We show, however, that the proposed scheme is in fact suboptimal. We then develop two new encoding-decoding constructions that attain the previously established lower bound, thereby completely characterizing the optimal multi-bit watermarking performance. Our approach formulates the watermark design problem as a linear program and derives the structural conditions under which optimality can be achieved. In addition, we identify the failure mechanism of the previous construction and compare the tradeoffs between the two proposed schemes.

papers.title: Non-Gaussian Uncertainty Estimation via Semi-nonparametric Density
papers.authors: Aaron R. Liao, Kenshiro Oguri, Michele D. Carpenter
papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient representation of non-Gaussian state distributions is critical for estimation, control, and decision-making, especially when the system is highly nonlinear. This paper develops a mathematical framework for estimating non-Gaussian uncertainty via semi-nonparametric (SNP), or Gallant-Nychka, densities. SNP densities use squared probabilists' Hermite polynomials to guarantee nonnegative probability densities while representing non-Gaussian behavior. For uncertainty propagation, once fitted to propagated state samples, SNP densities enable direct analytical density and probability evaluations without needing to tune additional hyperparameters besides the polynomial order. To enable their application to nonlinear dynamical systems, we derive analytic marginal and cumulative distribution functions and develop a lossless convex formulation of the coefficient estimation problem along a given sign branch. The approach is demonstrated on the chaotic Lorenz system and compared against Gaussian mixture models and Edgeworth approximations. Results demonstrate that SNP densities can accurately represent non-Gaussian state distributions while enabling direct probability and quantile evaluation, making them a promising tool for density estimation and uncertainty quantification in nonlinear estimation and control.

papers.title: Finite-Step Bounds for Iterated Correlation Matrices
papers.abstract:
We establish finite-step probabilistic upper bounds on the contraction ratios $\rho_k = \Delta_{k+1}/\Delta_k$ for iterated Pearson correlation dynamics. Let $(P_k)_{k\ge 0}$ be the sequence generated by the Pearson update. Define $\Delta_k := \|P_{k+1}-P_k\|_F$, $\rho_k := \Delta_{k+1}/\Delta_k$ for $\Delta_k > 0$, and $\delta_k := \Delta_k/n$. Although $\Delta_k \to 0$ along convergent trajectories, the ratios $\rho_k$ may exceed unity in finitely many steps. This behavior is invisible to local linearization. Our main contribution is a probabilistic bounding framework that captures these finite-step expansions.
  We initialize $P_0$ with i.i.d. $\mathcal{U}[-1,1]$ entries and let $\mathbb{P}$ be the induced measure. For $k \ge 2$, we construct state-dependent bounds $B_p : \mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}_+$ satisfying $\mathbb{P}(\rho_k \le B_p(\delta_k)) \ge p$. The functions $B^{\mathrm{q}}_p(\delta)$ are empirical conditional $p$-quantiles of $\log \rho_k$ given $\delta_k$ under logarithmic binning. Larger families $B^{\mathrm{TC}}_{p,\tau}(\delta)$ and $B^{\mathrm{tol}}_{p,\tau}(\delta)$ are obtained via multiplicative adjustments, yielding pointwise larger bounds that preserve the $\delta$-dependence.
  Validation on held-out trajectories confirms the bounds hold with empirical coverage matching nominal levels for all $n \in [3,2000]$. The baseline $0.95$-quantile bound $B^{\mathrm{q}}_{0.95}(\delta)$ yields two concrete results: $\mathbb{P}(\rho \le 1 \mid \delta \le 0.03) \ge 0.95$ uniformly in $n$, and $\mathbb{P}(\rho \le 1.7) \ge 0.95$ for 21 of 22 dimensions. The exception $n = 69$ attains $2.35$, revealing a rare extreme upper tail discontinuity not captured by asymptotic analysis. These are the first finite-step probabilistic bounds for Pearson correlation dynamics. The framework is fully reproducible with provided code and data.

papers.title: Open WDVV equations and $\bigvee$-systems
papers.authors: Alessandro Proserpio, Ian A. B. Strachan
papers.abstract: The idea of a $\bigvee$-system was introduced by Veselov in the study of rational solutions of the WDVV equations of associativity. These are algebraic/geometric conditions on the set of covectors that appear in rational solutions to the WDVV equations. Here, this idea is generalized to open WDVV equations, which are an additional set of PDEs originating from open Gromow-Witten Theory. We develop -- for rank-one extensions -- algebraic/geometric conditions on the covectors that supplement the $\bigvee$-system to give rational solutions to the open WDVV equations. Examples, and the relation to superpotentials and to Dubrovin almost-duality, are given.

papers.title: Joint Exclusivity
papers.abstract: We introduce \emph{joint exclusivity} (JE), a relaxation of mutual exclusivity (ME) for non-negative random vectors that forbids only the simultaneous positivity of all $n$ components. Whereas ME requires the probabilities of positive outcomes to sum to at most one, a JE random vector with prescribed marginals $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ exists if and only if $$ \sum_{i=1}^n \overline{F}_i(0)\le n-1. $$ An inclusion--exclusion identity shows that JE laws are determined by their $(n-1)$-dimensional margins and decomposes aggregate stop-loss premiums into those of sub-portfolios. A single wrap-around construction attains the existence bound, minimises the number of claims in convex order and, in frequency--severity models with exchangeable severities, the aggregate loss, extending the safest-dependence property of ME beyond its admissible range. We develop canonical and distortion-based constructions, an $m$-exclusivity hierarchy between ME and JE, and admissibility criteria for general families of claim patterns, explicit for hierarchical caps. Finally, we identify the most dangerous exclusive structure in convex order for lines sharing a severity law, which yields sharp stop-loss and Tail Value-at-Risk bounds.

papers.title: Mismatch Capacity under Stochastic Decoding
papers.authors: Francesc Molina, Albert Guillen i Fabregas
papers.abstract: This article investigates channel capacity under mismatched stochastic decoding. Feinstein- and Verd\'u-Han-type bounds on the error probability of coded communication are derived for sequences of $n$-letter channels and decoding metrics. These are used to obtain an information-spectrum formula for the corresponding channel capacity: the supremum, over all input distribution sequences, of the limit inferior in probability of the sequence of normalized mismatched information densities. This formula yields the mismatched analog of the Verd\'u-Han channel capacity formula. For discrete-memoryless channels and product metrics, uniform integrability allows to show that the limit product-space improvements of the generalized mutual information and the LM rate give the mismatch capacity under stochastic decoding. This establishes the stochastic decoding counterpart of the Csisz\'ar-Narayan conjecture. Relationships among the capacity formulas of related decoders are investigated. A number of examples are discussed including the case of binary-input binary-output channels and decoding metrics, where capacity is characterized in single-letter form.

papers.title: On the Jacobian algebras of Ziegler pairs of plane arrangements
papers.abstract: We consider a Ziegler pair of plane arrangements, that is two plane arrangements $\mathcal{A}:f=0$ and $\mathcal{A}':f'=0$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^3$, such that the intersection lattices $L(\mathcal{A})$ and $L(\mathcal{A}')$ are isomorphic, but the Betti numbers of the minimal resolutions of their Jacobian algebras are not the same. We introduce several properties for such pairs and relate them to cones over Ziegler pairs of line arrangements in $\mathbb{P}^2$.

papers.title: Hamiltonian Interface Dynamics for Reduced-Order Optimization of Incompressible Mixing
papers.abstract: We develop a reduced-order framework for optimizing mixing in two-dimensional incompressible flows. Instead of optimizing the full transport PDE, the method maximizes the length of advected material interfaces, leading to a Hamiltonian control problem with a finite spatial basis based on parametrized stream functions. We derive the continuous adjoint equations and reduced gradients, and discretize the forward and adjoint dynamics with the implicit midpoint rule. The resulting discrete adjoint is algebraically consistent with the derivative of the fully discrete objective when the implicit equations are solved exactly. The approach applies to bounded two-dimensional domains with sufficiently regular finite-dimensional stream-function parametrizations. Numerical experiments on cellular-flow and Doswell frontogenesis benchmarks show interface stretching and mix-norm decay over the simulated horizons. In four comparisons, the interface runs have lower recorded optimization times, whereas the Sobolev controls attain smaller terminal mix-norms. The different constraints, stopping rules and timing scopes preclude an equal-accuracy speedup claim.

papers.title: The Quasi-linearity problem for Jordan-Banach algebras: a topological characterization
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{J}$ be a JB$^*$-algebra with no quotients isomorphic to any spin factor. Let $\mu$ be a local quasi-linear Jordan functional on $\mathfrak{J}_{sa}$. We show that $\mu$ is a linear functional on $\mathfrak{J}_{sa}$ if and only if the restriction of $\mu$ to the closed unit ball of $\mathfrak{J}_{sa}$ is uniformly weakly continuous.

papers.title: Canonical parameters on marginally trapped surfaces in the Minkowski 4-space
papers.abstract: Marginally trapped surfaces are spacelike surfaces in the Minkowski space whose mean curvature vector is lightlike at each point. In general, the marginally trapped surfaces are determined by seven functions satisfying several conditions (differential equations). In the present paper, we introduce special principal parameters, called canonical, and prove that every marginally trapped surface of general type admits (at least locally) canonical principal parameters which allow us to reduce the number of functions. We prove a Fundamental existence and uniqueness theorem formulated in terms of canonical parameters, which states that every marginally trapped surface of general type is determined up to a motion by three smooth functions satisfying a system of partial differential equations. The special subclass of marginally trapped surfaces with parallel mean curvature vector field is described in terms of only one differential equation. Finally, the theory is enriched with examples of marginally trapped surfaces for which canonical parameters are determined.

papers.title: Quantifying Concentration Phenomena of Mean-Field Transformers in the Low-Temperature Regime
papers.authors: Albert Alcalde, Leon Bungert, Konstantin Riedl, Tim Roith
papers.abstract: Transformers with self-attention modules as their core components have become an integral architecture in modern large language and foundation models. In this paper, we study the evolution of tokens in deep encoder-only transformers at inference time which is described in the large-token limit by a mean-field continuity equation. Leveraging ideas from the convergence analysis of interacting multi-particle systems, with particles corresponding to tokens, we prove that the token distribution rapidly concentrates onto the push-forward of the initial distribution under a projection map induced by the key, query, and value matrices, and remains metastable for moderate times. Specifically, we show that the Wasserstein distance of the two distributions scales like $\sqrt{{\log(\beta+1)}/{\beta}}\exp(Ct)+\exp(-ct)$ in terms of the temperature parameter $\beta^{-1}\to 0$ and inference time $t\geq 0$. For the proof, we establish Lyapunov-type estimates for the zero-temperature equation, identify its limit as $t\to\infty$, and employ a stability estimate in Wasserstein space together with a quantitative Laplace principle to couple the two equations. Our result implies that for time scales of order $\log\beta$, which correspond to the early-phase behavior most relevant for practical finite-depth models, the token distribution concentrates at the identified limiting distribution. Numerical experiments confirm this and, beyond that, complement our theory by showing that for finite $\beta$ and large $t$ the dynamics enter a different terminal phase, dominated by the spectrum of the value matrix.

papers.title: Convergence of Singular Dynamics Driven by Mixed Logarithmic Heat Gradients
papers.abstract: We study the terminal behavior of singular deterministic and stochastic dynamics driven by convex or extrapolative combinations of logarithmic heat gradients. These equations arise in exact-score guided diffusion sampling, including classifier-free guidance. The rescaled potentials converge to weighted sums of squared support distances, but extrapolative mixing can produce limiting directions that depend on probability masses and lie outside the Clarke subdifferential of the limiting potential. A componentwise chain rule gives dissipation for the limiting differential inclusion. Posterior relative entropy yields finite deterministic kinetic action in logarithmic time, while a conditional free-energy estimate bounds expected energy increments uniformly in the restart time. For compactly supported laws, these estimates give energy convergence and equilibrium localization, almost surely for each fixed stochastic initialization; extrapolation requires a lower small-ball mass bound on the reference law. For finite atomic measures, we prove that the equilibrium set is finite for arbitrary site configurations. Every deterministic trajectory therefore converges to an equilibrium, and stochastic convergence holds almost surely for each fixed initialization, including endpoints at projection interfaces. At empirical endpoints with a unique nearest atom in each active support, deterministic trajectories admit a square-root heat-time expansion with an exponentially small remainder. The exponent 1/2 is sharp when the leading coefficient is nonzero. These results provide a geometric and dynamical framework for understanding terminal convergence in guided diffusion models.

papers.title: Intrinsic uniform structure on median algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce the median uniformity $\mathcal U_{\mathrm m}$, an intrinsic precompact convex uniform structure on a median algebra. It is Hausdorff under natural assumptions, for instance for finite-rank median algebras. In the Hausdorff case, its uniform completion yields the Minimal Median Compactification (MMC). The induced topology $\tau_{\mathrm m}$ provides a natural higher-rank analogue of the interval topology on linearly ordered sets and of the shadow topology on rank-one median algebras. When the intrinsic topology $\tau_{\mathrm m}$ is Hausdorff and all intervals are compact, the MMC is the unique proper median compactification and is canonically isomorphic to the Roller--Fioravanti compactification. We apply this uniform framework to continuous actions of a topological group $G$ by median automorphisms. We show that the MMC is a median $G$-compactification. In the finite-rank case, the resulting compact $G$-system is Rosenthal representable and dynamically tame.

papers.title: Pseudo-Euclidean Novikov Superalgebras: Structure and Properties
papers.authors: Said Benayadi, Sofiane Bouarroudj, Hamza El Ouali
papers.abstract:
A pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebra $A$ is a Novikov superalgebra endowed with a non-degenerate symmetric bilinear form $\langle, \rangle$ such that all left multiplication operators are $\langle, \rangle$-antisymmetric. In this case, the associated Lie superalgebra $(A^{-},\langle, \rangle)$ is a flat pseudo-Euclidean Lie superalgebra. In this paper, we investigate the structure of pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebras. In particular, we introduce a distinguished subclass, called \emph{Milnor superalgebras}, and prove that any pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebra whose two-sided ideal is non-degenerate belongs to this class. We provide a method for constructing pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebras.
  We also introduce a double extension procedure for pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebras and show that every such superalgebra with a degenerate two-sided ideal can be obtained via this method. Furthermore, we establish that any pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebra is either a Milnor superalgebra or can be obtained by a sequence of double extensions starting from a Milnor superalgebra. As an application, we provide a complete classification of pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebras of total dimension at most four over the field of real numbers.

papers.title: Integrals of general geometric random variables on the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article we provide an integration formula enabling us to integrate random variables defined on the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces which involve the lengths of closed geodesics of any prescribed topological type, at fixed genus and number of boundaries. We then compute the general form of length functions of closed loops in Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates. Using this expression together with our integration formula, we express the expectations of geometric random variables as integrals over R with almost polynomial density. As a consequence, given an arbitrary closed loop $\gamma$, we obtain an improvement of Mirzakhani's asymptotic equivalent of the Weil-Petersson expectation E[N$\gamma$(a)], when a $\rightarrow$ $\infty$, of the number of geodesics with same topological type as $\gamma$ of length at most a. We finally provide, for a loop $\gamma$ filling a one-holed torus or a four-holed sphere, an interpretation of the density function associated with $\gamma$ as the period of the Hamiltonian flow of the length function of $\gamma$.

papers.title: The Floquet-Magnus expansion of unbounded operators
papers.authors: Daniel Burgarth, Robin Hillier, Davide Lonigro, Leonhard Richter
papers.abstract: The Floquet-Magnus expansion is a widely used tool to derive effective descriptions of time-periodic quantum systems by approximating their dynamics with a time-independent Hamiltonian. However, its standard formulation is, strictly speaking, restricted to bounded Hamiltonians. In this work, we extend its definition and analysis to a broad class of time-periodic unbounded Hamiltonians. Our approach is based on an a priori distinct nonperturbative framework for the construction of effective Hamiltonians, which we show to reproduce the Floquet-Magnus expansion. A particular strength of our framework is that it allows us to prove that the resulting effective dynamics approximates the original time evolution propagators to arbitrary order in the high-frequency limit without requiring convergence of the Floquet-Magnus expansion, a condition that is already highly restrictive even in the bounded setting. We illustrate the scope of the method on representative models: the quantum Rabi Hamiltonian in the interaction picture, and the periodically driven quantum harmonic oscillator.

papers.title: Eigenvalue bounds for quantum dot Dirac operators
papers.abstract: We exploit the connection between quantum dot Dirac operators and $\overline\partial$-Robin Laplacians. First, we find a graphical relation between their smallest positive eigenvalues, which allows us to deduce a recipe for translating bounds (from above and below) from one to the other. As an application, we provide new upper and lower bounds for the eigenvalues of the quantum dot Dirac operators, which depend only on geometric quantities of the underlying domain. In particular, we obtain some Faber-Krahn type inequalities for convex thin domains.

papers.title: Strong log-concavity in probit regression
papers.authors: Martin Chak, Zoraida F. Rico, Giacomo Zanella
papers.abstract: We show that strong log-concavity emerges in probit regression likelihoods without ridge penalization (i.e. Gaussian priors), unlike for the logistic case. Specifically, we provide: (a) a non-asymptotic characterization of strong log-concavity for fixed designs, similar to that for the existence of the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) and (b) an asymptotic analysis for random designs, in the proportional regime when the sample size $n$ and the number of covariates $d$ grow proportionally $d/n\rightarrow r\in[0,1)$. In the latter case we show that, provided $r$ is small enough, the resulting condition number is finite and bounded independently of $n,d,r$ with high-probability. Numerically tractable estimates are given in case $r=0$. Thus, probit regression provides a non-trivial example of a high-dimensional, well-conditioned log-concave objective.

papers.title: On Star operation and some ideals on the Baire space
papers.abstract: We investigate several $\sigma$-ideals on the Baire space $\omega^\omega$ $(\mathbb{Z}^\omega)$, introducing and studying the ideals $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{SMZ}^+$, alongside the classical ideals of meager sets, strong measure zero sets, the eventually different ideal and infinitely equal ideal We establish structural relationships and proper inclusions among these ideals. Also we compute the cardinal invariants of $\mathcal{M}_-$, proving that they are same as invariants of $\sigma$-ideal of meager sets. We further analyze the operation $^*$ on families of sets, establishing dual relationships such as $\mathcal{ED}^* = \mathcal{IE}$, $\mathcal{IE}^*=\mathcal{ED}$, $\mathcal{M}_-^*=\mathcal{SMZ}^+$ and $\mathcal{H}^* = \mathcal{G}$, and derive separations between ideals under additional set-theoretic assumptions. Finally, we prove a tree dichotomy theorem for the ideal $\mathcal{M}_-$ and we study the associated forcing notion.

papers.title: Accelerating Min-Max Optimization via Power-Law Stepsizes
papers.authors: Yue Wu, Weiqiang Zheng, Yang Cai, Haipeng Luo
papers.abstract:
We revisit the convergence guarantees of the Extragradient (EG) method for unconstrained biaffine min-max optimization. It is known that EG with a fixed stepsize achieves a $\Theta(T^{-1/2})$ last-iterate convergence rate, which is slower than the optimal $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$ rate attainable by incorporating additional mechanisms such as anchoring. Motivated by recent advances showing that dynamic stepsizes alone can significantly accelerate gradient descent, we ask whether dynamic stepsizes can similarly accelerate the last-iterate convergence of EG.
  We present the first positive result in this direction. Specifically, we provide a deterministic dynamic stepsize schedule that accelerates the convergence rate of EG to $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2/3+\varepsilon})$ for any $\varepsilon > 0$. We also show that this rate is nearly tight when the extrapolation and update steps of EG use the same stepsize. We then show that allowing different stepsizes for the extrapolation and update steps further improves the convergence rate to the near-optimal $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1+\varepsilon})$. Our analysis reduces stepsize scheduling to an optimization problem, whose solution leads to a stepsize schedule that follows (a discretization of) a power-law distribution. Our proposed stepsize schedules and analysis extend to other methods, such as Optimistic Gradient (OG), and suggest broader applicability to general min-max optimization problems.

papers.title: On Local Finiteness of Modal K4 Algebras
papers.abstract: We study local finiteness for modal $K4$ algebras via the tunability of their dual general frames. In particular, we provide a sufficient condition for modal $K4$ algebras to be locally finite by identifying a structure which must be present in non-locally finite modal $K4$ algebras. We then show that this condition becomes both necessary and sufficient for $\sigma$-complete modal $K4$ algebras. Next, we translate this condition into a pair of order-theoretic conditions on transitive Kripke frames, providing a classification of local finiteness on their dual modal algebras. We further show that the logic of any class of well-founded transitive relations with no infinite antichains has the finite model property, and conclude that the logic of the class of well-quasi orderings has the finite model property.

papers.title: A stacky resolution of singularities for orders by Azumaya algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a stacky resolution of singularities for certain noncommutative spaces which can be viewed as 'finite noncommutative extensions' of schemes. More precisely, we show that any order over a reduced separated finite type scheme over a field of characteristic zero can be resolved by an Azumaya algebra over a smooth Deligne--Mumford stack by a sequence of stacky blow-ups.

papers.title: No-Harm Physics-Informed Inverse Learning with Residual-Calibrated Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Physics-informed learning is increasingly used for partial differential equation (PDE)-governed inverse problems, but its reliability remains difficult to certify. This paper develops a no-harm certification-and-selection framework for physics-informed inverse learning. A learned reconstruction is accepted only when its residual-calibrated radius is no worse than the baseline radius, namely when $$R_{\mathrm{learn}}\le R_{\mathrm{base}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{safe}};$$otherwise, the method returns the baseline. The certificate combines data, physics, boundary or initial-condition, and optimization residuals. Under a conditional stability estimate, these residuals yield an a posteriori reconstruction-error bound and a deterministic uncertainty radius. A high-probability certificate is also derived for physics residuals estimated from independent random collocation points. Numerical tests on Poisson source recovery, inverse heat reconstruction, limited-angle tomography, elliptic coefficient identification, and stochastic residual validation show that the selector accepts certified improvements, rejects shifted, hallucinated, or unfinished candidates, and becomes conservative in strongly ill-posed regimes. The framework is therefore a certification-and-selection layer, not another reconstruction architecture.

papers.title: Substitution groups of formal power series
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be the group of power series $x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3+\cdots\in R[[x]]$ under substitution, where $R$ is a commutative ring with $1\neq 0$ of prime characteristic $p$. Given any $n\geq 1$, the subgroup $K_n=\{x+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+a_{n+2}x^{n+2}+\cdots\,|\, a_i\in R\}$ is normal in $G$, and the quotient $G_n=G/K_n$ is the group of truncated polynomials over $R$ of degree $\leq n$ under substitution. In this paper, we compute the exponent of the image of $K_r$ in $G_n$, for all $r,n\geq 1$, indicating in every case a family of elements realizing this exponent.

papers.title: Topology of isometric classes and flows of geometric structures
papers.abstract:
We study the topology of isometric classes of tensorial $H$-structures for closed and connected subgroups $H\leqslant\mathrm{SO}(n)$. The map assigning an $H$-structure its induced metric admits a global trivialization; consequently, the space of $H$-structures is homotopy equivalent to any fixed isometric class. On flat tori, these classes are mapping spaces into $\mathrm{SO}(n)/H$. We give examples with infinitely many connected components for $\mathrm{G}_2$, $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$, and almost Hermitian structures, determine the number of components for $\mathrm{SU}(m)$-structures on flat tori, and study the corresponding moduli spaces.
  For closed manifolds of dimension $n>2$, the intrinsic torsion energy on the full space of $H$-structures has infimum zero on every nonempty path component, and its critical points are precisely the torsion-free structures. In fixed isometric classes, we contrast the concentration phenomena underlying finite-time singularities with cohomological classes admitting positive energy lower bounds and harmonic representatives.
  Finally, we establish a lifting principle for metric-dependent flows, derive an evolution identity for isometric flows, and extend harmonic-flow estimates to general $H$-structures.

papers.title: Bounded Bruhat intervals and affine Coxeter groups
papers.abstract: Dyer (1991) proved that, for each fixed length $k$, only finitely many isomorphism types of Bruhat intervals occur in finite Coxeter groups. In this short paper, we prove that this result holds also for affine Coxeter groups, and moreover that this characterizes the affine groups among all infinite Coxeter groups. We also show that the coefficients of $q$ in the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of a Coxeter group are bounded if and only if the group is finite or affine.

papers.title: Finite difference methods for a continuous-time heterogeneous agent model with recursive utility
papers.abstract: We propose, analyze and test computational methods for solving a continuous-time heterogenous agent model with Epstein-Zin utility. Such recursive utilities allow the model to disentangle between risk aversion and intertemporal substitution. Having discretized the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation arising in the model, we propose a Howard-Newton algorithm for the late resolution preference case, and a Howard-Tarski-Kantorovich algorithm for the early resolution preference case. We prove the convergence of the iterative algorithms. We obtain as a consequence the existence of solutions to the discretized HJB equations. In the late resolution case, we supply a priori estimates between the unique solutions of the continuous and discretized HJB equations.

papers.title: A characterization of edge-chromatic 3-critical graphs
papers.abstract: A graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ is \emph{$\Delta$-critical} if it is connected, has chromatic index $\Delta+1$, and the deletion of any edge reduces its chromatic index to $\Delta$; it is \emph{nontrivial} if it has no subgraph $H$ with $|E(H)|>\Delta\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$. We prove a characterization of all nontrivial $3$-critical graphs: every such graph is obtained either from smaller $3$-critical graphs by replacing a vertex with a triangle, by a Haj\'os-join, or by replacing a vertex with a suitable class~$1$ graph, or from a snark by deleting at most one vertex and some independent edges. The third operation, which we call a Meredith-type extension, generalizes the Meredith extension by allowing other class~$1$ graphs in place of $K_{2,3}$, and we give a sufficient condition under which it produces new nontrivial $3$-critical graphs from smaller ones. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first characterization of this kind for edge-chromatic $3$-critical graphs, and the Meredith-type extension has not previously been considered in this generality. The characterization was found by analyzing the output of an exhaustive computer search for nontrivial $3$-critical graphs of orders $13$ to $24$, and we make the resulting data publicly available. Based on these data, we also propose two conjectures that are closely related to the case $\Delta=3$ of Seymour's exact conjecture and to Gr\"otzsch's conjecture on the $3$-edge-colorability of planar graphs.

papers.title: Strongly Primitive Salem Growth Polynomials for Right-Angled Coxeter Groups
papers.abstract: We study standard spherical growth rates of right-angled Coxeter groups through the clique polynomial of the defining graph. We prove that every even degree at least four occurs as the degree of a strongly primitive Salem growth rate: for each $d\geq2$, there are infinitely many connected $K_{2d+1}$-free defining graphs whose full reciprocal-radius polynomial is an irreducible Salem polynomial of degree $2d$. We also establish independence-polynomial obstructions for prescribed Salem polynomials, including a sharp first-coefficient bound $a_1\leq-5$. Finally, an elementary golden-ratio growth gap excludes Lehmer's number from the standard spherical growth rates of right-angled Coxeter groups.

papers.title: Diffeological Riemannian orbifolds
papers.abstract: We show that the data of a Riemannian metric on a differentiable stack presented by an orbifold groupoid is equivalent to the data of a Riemannian metric on its diffeological orbit space. As a consequence, we conclude that the classical notion of Riemannian orbifold is equivalent to that of a Riemannian diffeological orbifold. We use the framework for Riemannian diffeology introduced by Kuribayashi, Sakai, and Shiobara, and our result answers a problem they posed in the affirmative. More generally, we show that a Riemannian metric on a Lie groupoid, namely a 2-metric in the sense of del Hoyo and Fernandes, induces a Riemannian metric on its diffeological orbit space only if the Lie groupoid is regular, and that properness is a sufficient but not necessary condition.

papers.title: Combinatorial identities derived from explicit formulas of Gauss hypergeometric functions
papers.abstract: In the present paper, with the help of the Fa\`a di Bruno formula and several identities of partial Bell polynomials, the author establishes explicit formulas of the Gauss hypergeometric functions \begin{gather*} {\,}_2F_1\biggl(\frac{1-n}{2},\frac{2-n}{2};\frac{3}{2}-m;z^2\biggr), \quad {\,}_2F_1\biggl(-\frac{n}{2},\frac{1-n}{2};\frac{1}{2}-m;z^2\biggr),\\ {\,}_2F_1\biggl(a,a+\frac{1}{2};\frac{3}{2}-m;z^2\biggr), \quad {\,}_2F_1\biggl(a,a+\frac{1}{2};\frac{1}{2}-m;z^2\biggr) \end{gather*} for $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $a\in\mathbb{C}$, and then derives two combinatorial identities \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=0}^{m}\frac{2^k}{k!} \binom{2m-2k}{m-k} \sum_{\ell=0}^{k} \frac{(-1)^\ell}{2^\ell} \frac{(2k-2\ell-1)!!}{(n-\ell)!} \binom{2k-\ell-1}{\ell-1} =\frac{1}{n!}\binom{2m-n}{m} \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=1}^{m}\frac{1}{(k!)^2}\binom{2m-2k}{m-k} \sum_{\ell=1}^{k} \binom{k}{\ell}\ell(2k-\ell-1)! (2a)_\ell =\binom{2m+2a}{m}-\binom{2m}{m}, \end{equation*} where $m\in\mathbb{N}_0$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $a\in\mathbb{C}$. These newly-established identities extend and generalize the beautiful combinatorial identity \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{2^{k}}{k!}\binom{2n-2k}{n-k} \sum_{j=0}^{k}\frac{(-1)^{j}}{2^j} \frac{(2k-2j-1)!!}{(n-j)!} \binom{2k-j-1}{j-1} =\frac{1}{n!}, \quad n\in\mathbb{N}_0, \end{equation*} which was obtained in Theorem 4 of the paper "F. Qi, C.-Y. He, and D. Lim, Explicit formulas of two Gauss hypergeometric functions and several combinatorial identities, Discrete Appl. Math. Vol. 393 (2026), 215--229. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dam.2026.06.023."

papers.title: A Twin gradient method for unconstrained optimization
papers.authors: Anna De Magistris, Michiel E. Hochstenbach, Gerardo Toraldo
papers.abstract: We propose a new strategy for gradient-based unconstrained optimization, involving two parallel sequences of iterates that cooperate to determine their stepsizes via a \textit{Twin-Step} principle. Rather than minimizing the objective function individually, the algorithm selects steplengths that minimize the Euclidean distance between the two gradient based processes occurring simultaneously at each iteration. The theoretical analysis shows that the convergence of the mutual distance is governed by the angle between the search directions. In particular the effectiveness of the overall process degrades as the directions approach parallelism. To ensure robustness against collinearity, we introduce a hybrid framework, Twin-ABB$_{\min}$, which switches to the Adaptive Barzilai--Borwein method when the geometric cooperation becomes ineffective. Extensive and very promising numerical results evidence that the Twin phase creates favorable initial conditions for subsequent BB-type iterations.

papers.title: Heilbronn's Problem in the Unit Triangle: Computational Optimality Certificates for $n \le 8$
papers.abstract: We study Heilbronn's triangle problem in the unit right triangle, where $n$ points are placed to maximize the smallest of the $\binom{n}{3}$ triangle areas they span. We prove a boundary-structure result: unless all three vertices are occupied, some optimal configuration with $n \ge 5$ has at least four points on the boundary, one edge containing two of them. With the affine $S_3$ symmetry this fixes four boundary points and $n$ orientation variables in a mixed-integer model that certifies global optimality for all $n \le 8$ up to a relative gap of $10^{-4}$. For $n \le 7$ this independently confirms the known exact optima, the case $n = 7$ having been proved by Zeng and Chen with symbolic computation. For $n = 8$, where only bounds were known, it narrows the gap to Cantrell's configuration fourfold in 39 minutes on one machine. The optimum there is conjectured to be the real root of a septic obtained by Chen, Zeng and Zhou, which our reconstruction confirms to 250 digits. We show its Galois group is $S_7$, so on that conjecture no expression in radicals exists.

papers.title: Asymptotic Resurgence of Facet and Stanley-Reisner ideals of Matroids
papers.authors: Michael DiPasquale, Louiza Fouli, Arvind Kumar
papers.abstract:
Matroid configurations -- introduced by Geramita, Harbourne, Migliore, and Nagel -- are projective varieties which generalize so-called \textit{star configurations} and whose defining ideals are obtained by appropriately specializing the Stanley-Reisner ideal of a matroid. Motivated by this connection, we study the asymptotic resurgence of the Stanley-Reisner ideals of matroids. A result of Villareal shows that it is equivalent to study the asymptotic resurgence of facet ideals. We prove a formula for the asymptotic resurgence of the facet ideal of a matroid in terms of the Waldschmidt constant of facet ideals of the contractions of the matroid. As a consequence, we show that asymptotic resurgence respects the weak order on matroids of the same rank. Therefore, the asymptotic resurgence of the facet ideal of a given matroid is bounded above by the asymptotic resurgence of the facet ideal of a so-called \textit{almost-uniform} matroid of the same rank, which we compute explicitly.
  Guardo, Harbourne, and Van Tuyl showed that the asymptotic resurgence of an ideal is bounded below by the ratio of the initial degree of the ideal by its Waldschmidt constant. We prove that this lower bound is an equality for facet ideals of many classes of matroids, including matroids of rank $k$ on a ground set of size $n\ge 2k$ whose dual is paving, perfect matroid designs, and sparse paving matroids arising from Steiner systems. For the latter two classes, we explicitly compute the asymptotic resurgence.

papers.title: Derived Azumaya Algebras on Compact Derived Smooth Manifolds
papers.abstract: We extend To\"en's derived Brauer theory to the open site of Spivak's derived smooth manifolds. For a compact derived smooth manifold $X$, we define a spectralized structure sheaf $\mathbb{O}_{X}$ and prove that every Picard twist can be represented by a derived Azumaya algebra, whose Morita equivalence class is uniquely determined by the twist. In the open locally Morita trivial setting, this gives a natural bijection \begin{align*} \Phi_{X}:\mathbf{dBr}^{\mathrm{open}}(X) \xrightarrow{\cong} H^{1}(|X|;\underline{\mathbb {Z}}) \times \pi_0\Gamma(|X|,\mathrm B^2GL_1(\mathbb O_X)). \end{align*} If we consider $C^\infty_X(\mathbb C)$ on ordinary smooth manifolds, the second factor is $H^3(|X|;\underline{\mathbb Z})$, which recovers the Dixmier-Douady invariant. If we consider $C^\infty_X(\mathbb R)$, the second factor is $H^2(|X|;\underline{\mathbb Z/2})$, which recovers the corresponding invariant of Donovan and Karoubi.

papers.title: A cube complex for virtual Artin groups
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a Coxeter graph, and let $S$ be its vertex set. An elemental complex over $\Gamma$ is an abstract simplicial complex $\mathcal D$ on $S$ that contains every pair $\{s, t\}$ with $s \neq t$ and $m_{s,t} \neq \infty$. To each elemental complex $\mathcal D$, we associate a cube complex $\Xi_{\mathcal D}$ on which the virtual Artin group ${\rm VA} [\Gamma]$ acts. We prove that $\Xi_{\mathcal D}$ is connected, simply connected, and locally regular; that the action of ${\rm VA}[\Gamma]$ on $\Xi_{\mathcal D}$ is regular, cocompact, and by isometries; and that the stabilizers of cells are parabolic subgroups. We finally prove that $\Xi_{\mathcal D}$ is CAT(0) if and only if ${\mathcal D}$ is a flag complex.

papers.title: Disconnected Stab(X) and infinitely many braid group orbits
papers.abstract: We show that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions Stab(Y) on a very general quintic threefold Y has infinitely many connected components. Using similar methods, we also prove that for a particular smooth projective (weak Fano) threefold X the braid group action on the set of full exceptional collections in Dscr^b(X) has infinitely many orbits, in particular, it is not transitive. This provides a counterexample to a conjecture of Bondal and Polishchuk from 1993. The conjecture was first disproved by Chang, Haiden, and Schroll, who constructed a family of partially wrapped Fukaya categories for which the transitivity fails. However, no counterexample of the form Dscr^b(X) for X a smooth projective variety was previously known. In addition, we show that Stab(X) also has infinitely many connected components. These are the first known examples of a smooth projective varieties whose spaces of Bridgeland stability conditions are disconnected.

papers.title: On the Column Number of Delta-Modular Matrices: an $O(m^2 \Delta)$ Bound via the Shifted Heller Constant
papers.authors: Elizaveta Pribytkova, Dmitrii Gribanov, Dmitrii Taletskii, Stanislav Moiseev
papers.abstract: In this paper, we build on the analysis initiated by Averkov and Schymura (2022) and prove that the shifted Heller constant for matrices with $m$ rows is at most $m^2 + m$ for all sufficiently large $m$. Consequently, the number of distinct columns of a $\Delta$-modular matrix $A \in Z^{m \times n}$ of rank $m$ is at most $O(m^2 \Delta)$. This improves upon the earlier bounds of $O(m^4 \Delta)$ and $O(m^2 \Delta^2)$.

papers.title: Critical $p$-Laplace equations with monotone coefficients: Liouville classification and a Schoen-type Harnack inequality
papers.abstract:
We investigate positive weak solutions of the critical $p$-Laplace equation $$
  -\Delta_p u = u^{p^*-1} h(u), \qquad 1 < p < n, $$ where $h$ is a positive, bounded, continuous, and nonincreasing function. Our first main result is a complete classification of normalized, bounded, positive entire solutions for every equation in a compact family determined by $h$: Any such solution must coincide with an Aubin--Talenti profile. Moreover, the existence of an Aubin--Talenti profile as a solution implies that $h$ is constant on the entire interval of values attained by that profile.
  Subsequently, applying this classification result, we establish the following scale-invariant Schoen-type estimate $$
  \left(\sup_{B_R} u\right)\left(\inf_{B_{2R}} u\right)^{p-1}
  \le C R^{p-n} $$ for nonnegative weak solutions defined in $B_{3R}$. As a direct corollary, we apply the profound result of Ciraolo--Gatti \cite{CG2026} to obtain a fully unrestricted Liouville theorem: Every positive entire solution must coincide with an Aubin--Talenti profile. For the purely critical equation, we also show that the corresponding Liouville classification is equivalent to a Schoen-type Harnack inequality.
  The arguments in this work give quasilinear versions of the Kelvin transform and the method of moving spheres, which was previously available only in the semilinear setting, and also yield alternative proofs of the classical results. The technique developed here can likely be extended to a wider class of Liouville-type problems for critical equations.

papers.title: Pure dimension and counterexamples to the maximality of purely-primes
papers.abstract: In analogy with the notion of Krull dimension, for every commutative ring $R$, we introduce the notion of pure dimension $\pdim(R)$ by considering chains of purely-prime ideals. Then we see that the inequality $\pdim(R)\leqslant\dim(R)$ holds for a very broad class of rings $R$, including pseudo-Noetherian rings (e.g., Noetherian rings), Gelfand rings (e.g., local rings), mp-rings (e.g., integral domains), and rings with finitely many maximal ideals or finitely many minimal primes. In fact, for all of these rings $R$, we always have $\pdim(R)=0$, i.e., every purely-prime ideal of $R$ is purely-maximal. \\ However, we prove a classification theorem which states for each ordinal number $\Omega$ the proper pure ideals of the commutative ring $$R_{\Omega}=k[X_{\alpha} : \alpha <\Omega]/\big(X_{\alpha}(1-X_{\beta}) : \alpha<\beta<\Omega\big)$$ are exactly of the form $I_{\lambda}=(x_{\alpha}: \alpha<\lambda)$ with $\lambda=0$ or $\lambda\leqslant\Omega$ a limit ordinal (we write $x_{\alpha}$ for the image of $X_{\alpha}$ in $R_{\Omega}$). In addition, all of them are purely-prime ideals and form the following unique strictly ascending chain: $$I_{0}=0\subset I_{\omega}\subset I_{\omega\cdot2}\subset I_{\omega\cdot 3}\subset\ldots\subset I_{\omega\cdot\alpha}$$ where $\alpha$ is a unique ordinal with $\Omega=\omega\cdot\alpha+n$ and $n\in\omega$. To prove this theorem, we use the full strength of ...

papers.title: Brauer graph algebras are closed under stable equivalence of Morita type
papers.authors: Pengyun Chen, Nengqun Li, Yuming Liu, Bohan Xing
papers.abstract: We study stable equivalences of Brauer graph algebras. We prove that a basic symmetric algebra without semisimple summands which is stably equivalent to a Brauer graph algebra is again a Brauer graph algebra. In particular, Brauer graph algebras are closed up to semisimple summands under stable equivalence of Morita type. As consequences, we reprove the closure under derived equivalence established by Antipov and Zvonareva and obtain a solution of the reconstruction problem posed by Rickard and Rouquier for algebras stably equivalent of Morita type to Brauer graph algebras.

papers.title: Generalized Hitchin-Kobayashi correspondence and Weil-Petersson current
papers.abstract: In this paper we extend Hitchin-Kobayashi correspondence along holomorphic fibre space and we show that there exists a generalized Hermitian-Einstein metric which is twisted with Weil-Petersson current.In fact we generalise Song-Tian program for vector bundles

papers.title: A new strong rigidity phenomenon for the Bergman metric
papers.authors: Peter Ebenfelt, John N. Treuer, Ming Xiao
papers.abstract: We establish a new local-to-global rigidity phenomenon for the Bergman metric. Namely, under natural geometric hypotheses, a local conformal identification of Bergman metrics determines the underlying complex manifold globally, up to the unavoidable ambiguity of removing Bergman-negligible subsets. More precisely, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain with a complete Bergman metric, and suppose that the Bergman metric of a complex manifold $M$ is locally conformal, via a holomorphic map $f$, to that of $\Omega$, with a constant conformal factor when $n=1$. We prove that the given local map $f$ extends to a biholomorphism $F\colon M\to D$ onto a subdomain $D\subseteq\Omega$ in two complementary settings. If $M$ is Stein, then $\Omega\setminus D$ is a closed pluripolar set. If $M$ is a bounded domain and $\Omega$ satisfies a natural symmetry condition expressed in terms of its automorphism orbits, then $\Omega\setminus D$ is Bergman-negligible. In particular, this applies when $\Omega$ is a bounded homogeneous domain and yields a characterization, up to Bergman-negligible sets, of a class of bounded domains with locally symmetric Bergman metrics, addressing a question raised by Loi--Palmieri and Zimmer. A key ingredient in the proofs is a new Calabi-type extension theorem tailored to Bergman metrics.

papers.title: The minimum of the graph likelihood
papers.abstract: The likelihood of a finite simple undirected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is the probability that the uniform sequential attachment process, which at each step joins a new vertex to a uniformly random subset of uniformly random size of the vertices already present, outputs a graph isomorphic to $G$. Dervovic, Mocherla and Severini conjectured that the likelihood is minimised by the balanced complete bipartite graph. We prove that, among complete bipartite graphs of a given order, the balanced one uniquely minimises the likelihood. Exact computation shows that it also minimises over all graphs for every order from $6$ through $14$. At $n=15$, the exact global minimisers are $C_5[\bar K_3]$ and its complement, giving the first counterexample. Completed exact searches show that the global minimisers at order $16$ are $K_{8,8}$ and its complement. At order $17$, the unique minimiser is a self-complementary mixed blow-up of $C_5$. At order $18$, the minimisers are $K_{9,9}$ and its complement. We show that the failure is not sporadic by proving that the likelihood of the balanced complete bipartite graph is $2^{-(1/2-1/(8\ln 2)+o(1))n^2}$, whereas the minimum over all graphs of order $n$ is $2^{-(1/2+o(1))n^2}$, so the conjectured minimiser exceeds the minimum by a factor exponential in $n^2$. We also determine the Shannon entropy of the process to leading order, namely $n^2/(4\ln 2)$ bits, which shows that the conjectured minimiser is in fact more likely than a typical output of the process. The proofs rest on a vertex deletion recurrence which evaluates the likelihood in time $O(2^n n)$ and which closes on the blow-ups of any fixed base graph.

papers.title: A Sharp Refinement of Samuels' Inequality via Cap Moves
papers.abstract:
Let $0\le \mu_1\le \mu_2 \le \cdots \le \mu_n$ and $\delta > 0$. Samuels' conjecture states that if $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are independent non-negative random variables with $\mathbb{E}[X_i] = \mu_i$, then $$
  \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^n X_i < \delta + \sum_{i=1}^n \mu_i \right) \ge \min_{1\le i\le n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left(1-\frac{\mu_j}{\delta + \sum_{k=i}^n \mu_k}\right).$$ This conjecture was recently proved by Ling. In this note, we prove a refinement of Samuels' inequality via an operation called the \emph{cap move}. Our refined inequality is sharp, with equality attained for a strictly larger class of distributions than in the original inequality.

papers.title: Wave Selection at an $O(2)$-Hopf Bifurcation in Conservative Two-Component PDE Systems
papers.abstract: At an $O(2)$-equivariant Hopf bifurcation a spatially periodic system selects between traveling waves and standing waves, and which branch appears and whether it is stable is decided by two cubic normal form coefficients. Obtaining these coefficients for a given PDE has required a derivation carried out afresh for each model. We remove that step for two-component systems with conservative polynomial differential nonlinearities on a one-dimensional periodic domain, deriving closed form formulas for both coefficients. They are expressed directly in terms of the array of nonlinear PDE coefficients and the spectral data of the linearization, its critical eigenvectors, adjoint eigenvectors, and non-critical resolvents. We give verifiable conditions under which the underlying center manifold reduction is valid. A structural condition on the principal part of the linearization, together with sign conditions on the trace and determinant of its Fourier symbol, yields the resolvent estimate and the spectral gap that the reduction requires. A companion implementation evaluates the two normal form coefficients from the coefficient array and verifies the assumptions for a given system. We specialize the formulas to two applications: a strain-gradient regularization of the nonlinear $p$-system, whose quadratic case contains a previously studied model as a special case, and a first order conservative bilinear family, not previously analyzed, in which every bifurcation scenario allowed by the general classification is realized.

papers.title: Waveguiding in systems of high contrast resonators: Theory and fast computations
papers.authors: Habib Ammari, Bowen Li, Borui Miao, Jiayu Qiu, Lara Vrabac
papers.abstract: In this work, we study guided modes in systems of high-contrast resonators near nonzero interior Neumann frequencies, beyond the subwavelength regime. In the regular exterior regime, where the exterior Dirichlet problem is well-posed at the reference wavenumber, we introduce an infinite-dimensional frequency-dependent capacitance operator obtained by compressing the exterior Helmholtz Dirichlet-to-Neumann map to the traces of the interior resonant Neumann eigenspaces. We prove the norm-resolvent convergence of the continuous problem to this discrete effective operator as the contrast $\delta\to0$, and derive first-order asymptotic formulas for compact-defect frequencies and line-defect band functions. We then establish exponential off-diagonal decay of the capacitance coefficients by a Combes--Thomas argument, yielding an exponentially accurate truncation of the discrete operator, and show that its retained coefficients can be computed from local Helmholtz problems. At the physical frequency, this local approximation converges exponentially under a uniform stability assumption for the growing finite-cluster problems. The stability assumption can be removed by introducing a vanishing complex absorption together with a Hermitian symmetrization. In particular, an absorption parameter of order $\sqrt\delta$, together with interaction truncation and patch radii of order $|\log\delta|$, suffices to preserve the $O(\delta^2)$ accuracy of the first-order high-contrast expansion of the defect eigenfrequencies, yielding a fast computational method. Numerical experiments for dipole and quadrupole resonances illustrate the accuracy, exponential locality, and applicability of the discrete model to straight and bent waveguides generated by material or geometric detuning.

papers.title: Ramanujan Transforms and Maximum Energy of Odd-Total-Exponent Integral Circulants
papers.abstract: For a finite graph, its energy is the sum of the absolute values of its adjacency eigenvalues. Let n be the product of powers of distinct odd primes, where all exponents are positive integers, the sum of the exponents is odd, and every prime whose exponent is odd is at least five. Among all nonempty sets of proper divisors of n, the energy of the corresponding integral circulant graph is uniquely maximised by the checkerboard divisor set consisting of those divisors for which the sum of the prime-power exponents is even. The maximum energy is one half of the sum of n and the product, over all prime factors, of explicit polynomial quantities. For exponent k and parameter x, the corresponding polynomial is given by two k plus one times x to the k-th power, together with four times the sum from zero to k minus one of j plus one times x to the j-th power with alternating sign determined by the parity of k minus j. For the proof, we use weighted prime-power Ramanujan transforms, which give an exact energy model in tensor form and extend to a polynomial matrix family for real parameters greater than one. A semidefinite parity theorem shows that the matrix obtained from this polynomial family by an explicit positive diagonal normalisation is a real symmetric contraction whose unique eigenvalue of modulus one is the simple eigenvalue determined by the parity of the exponent; this holds for even exponents at least two and parameters at least three, and for odd exponents at least one and parameters at least five. Tensorising this spectral structure and centring the binary divisor tensor yield a sharp one-norm bound for the corresponding tensor operator on sign vectors. In particular, for n equal to p squared times q cubed, with distinct odd primes p and q and with q at least five, this proves Roldan's conjectured maximality in this range.

papers.title: On Decay of the Local Mean Oscillations of the Vorticity Direction in Critical Navier-Stokes Flows
papers.abstract: We isolate and analyze the geometric PDE governing the evolution of the vorticity direction in the 3D incompressible (unforced) Navier-Stokes equations (NSE), restricted to the case of a critical spatial point singularity where the vorticity magnitude concentrates as $O(|x|^{-2})$, inhabiting the critical Lorentz space $L^{3/2, \infty}$. The PDE consists of the Harmonic Map Heat Flow (HMHF) into the sphere supplemented with the fluid transport, cross-diffusion and tangential strain. The question is whether the NSE mechanics can propagate logarithmic decay of the local mean oscillations of the direction -- the condition $\xi \in \mathrm{bmo}_{1/|\log r|}$ -- which (in this setting) was shown in the companion paper to prevent finite time blow-up. A key observation is that the $O(|x|^{-2})$ concentration, factored out of the viscous cross-diffusion, generates an outward radial drift $4\nu\, x/|x|^2$ at the core. Under a suitable condition we prove a barrier lemma for the total drift-diffusion operator and show that the HMHF nonlinearity is harmless for the quantity $\frac12|\xi - e|^2$ which is a subsolution on any hemisphere. This yields a transfer theorem: the $\mathrm{bmo}_{1/|\log r|}$ regularity of the direction at the core, uniformly up to the singular time, is controlled by a logarithmic modulus in time of the direction at the inner scale, together with the physical strain. Crucially, the strain enters the direction equation only through its tangential component which vanishes precisely when the direction is an eigenvector of the strain tensor. Since this includes the eigenvector carrying the maximal stretching, the result is in contrast to the classical geometric regularity theory which is built on depleting the full vortex-stretching term and thus confined to configurations of weak stretching.

papers.title: Local Well-Posedness of the Unsteady Boundary Layer System for Dilatant Power-Law Fluids
papers.abstract: We establish local-in-time existence and uniqueness of monotone classical solutions to the two-dimensional nonstationary boundary layer equations for dilatant power-law fluids in a periodic half-space, for every fixed exponent $n>1$. The result holds under Oleinik's monotonicity condition and suitable weighted Sobolev, algebraic decay, and compatibility assumptions. The main difficulties are the tangential derivative loss caused by the normal velocity and the degeneracy at infinity of the principal coefficient $n\omega^{n-1}$ in the nonlinear vorticity diffusion $\partial_y^2(\omega^n)$, where $\omega=\partial_y u$. We adapt the Masmoudi-Wong energy method and use a good unknown to control the tangential derivative loss. For the nonlinear diffusion, we separate the estimates near the boundary from the treatment of degeneracy in the far field. Nonlinear boundary reduction and localized trace estimates control the boundary terms, while weighted estimates exploit the compensating decay of vorticity derivatives to control the diffusion commutators. Together with tangential regularization and weighted maximum and minimum principles, these estimates yield bounds uniform in the regularization parameter and preserve weighted monotonicity. Under these assumptions, the result provides an affirmative local-in-time answer to the existence and uniqueness question in Open Problem~11 of Oleinik and Samokhin.

papers.title: A Sharp Sobolev Inequality on Compact CR Manifolds
papers.abstract:
For any \(n\geq 1\), let \((M,\theta)\) be a compact strictly pseudoconvex hypersurface type CR manifold with dimension \(2n+1\), \(Q=2n+2\) be its homogeneous dimension. We prove the sharp Folland--Stein Sobolev inequality on \(M\): if \(Q^*=2Q/(Q-2)\), then there exists a constant \(A>0\), depending only on \((M,\theta)\), such that
  \[
  \|u\|_{L^{Q^*}(M)}^2 \le K(n)^2\|\nabla_b u\|_{L^2(M)}^2 + A\|u\|_{L^2(M)}^2, \qquad u\in S^{1,2}(M).
  \]
  Here \(K(n)\) is the sharp constant in the Folland--Stein Sobolev inequality on the Heisenberg group \(\mathbb H^n\).

papers.title: Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers I. Analytic Rigidity
papers.abstract: Let $\mathscr L$ denote the set of Liouville numbers. We prove a local arithmetic rigidity theorem for real-analytic functions. If $U\subset\mathbb R$ is an open interval and $f:U\to\mathbb R$ is real-analytic with $f(\mathscr L\cap U)\subseteq\mathscr L$, then $f$ is the restriction to $U$ of a rational function in $\mathbb R(x)$. Quantitatively, there exists an absolute constant $\tau>2$ such that, for every nonrational real-analytic function $f$ and every nonempty open subinterval $V\subset U$, the set of $\xi\in V\cap\mathscr L$ satisfying $\mu(f(\xi))\leq\tau$ contains a Cantor set. As a consequence, every entire function $F:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ satisfying $F(\mathscr L)\subseteq \mathscr L$ is a polynomial with real coefficients. This gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Mahler in 1984. The proof develops a two-height counting estimate for rational approximation to analytic graphs, treating source and target denominators separately, and combines it with a nested construction producing Liouville inputs whose images have uniformly bounded irrationality exponent.

papers.title: Jordan-H\"older theory for complementary polyhedra and moduli of parahoric Higgs torsors
papers.abstract: We extend Behrend's theory of complementary polyhedra to include Jordan-H\"older theory by introducing the notion of Jordan-H\"older facets. As a consequence, we can construct Jordan-H\"older parabolic subgroup schemes for reductive group schemes over a smooth projective curve. We use these results to provide a uniform approach to describing Jordan-H\"older filtrations and S-equivalence of moduli stacks of semistable bundles, including vector bundles, principal bundles, parabolic bundles, parahoric torsors, and parahoric Higgs torsors, following Zhang. We explicitly give a description of Jordan-H\"older filtrations and S-equivalence in the semistable locus of parahoric torsors and parahoric Higgs torsors, coming from their good moduli spaces, as constructed by Alper-Halpern-Leistner-Heinloth and R\'ega. This application uses the Rees construction, as given by Heinloth, to identify filtrations of moduli stacks of parahoric torsors with reductions of parahoric torsors to parabolic subgroups, inducing Jordan-H\"older stratifications of the moduli stacks.

papers.title: Evaluations of Series Using the Beta Function
papers.abstract: This article presents proofs of seven conjectural series identities for $\pi$ proposed by Z.-W. Sun. Our proofs rely mainly on transformations involving the Beta function. We also use symbolic integration with the software \texttt{Mathematica} to reduce the amount of computational work.

papers.title: Bounds on non-hermite Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information
papers.abstract: We obtain the relation between non-hermite skew information $NI_{\rho,\alpha}(A)$, $NU_{\rho,\alpha}(A)$, variance $NV_{\rho}(A)$ and $NJ_{\rho,\alpha}(A)$ by using the maximal eigenvalue and the minimal eigenvalue of density $\rho$. And also we obtain their refinements.

papers.title: Affine reflection transforms of convex polygons with parallel opposite sides
papers.authors: Peter Giblin, Stanis\l{}aw Janeczko, Micha\l{} Zwierzy\'nski
papers.abstract: We study affine reflection transforms of convex polygons with parallel opposite sides. An opposite-side involution sends a pencil through an interior point to a piecewise smooth family of lines. Its completed envelope consists of conic arcs and transition segments. The completed transform has non-positive oriented area. Maximising the negative oriented area and dividing by the polygonal area gives an affine invariant that vanishes precisely for centrally symmetric polygons. Combining an identity for reflected chord vectors with the Rogers--Shephard inequality shows that this invariant is strictly less than $1$, with optimal universal constant $1$. The energy extends continuously to the boundary and vanishes there. We also compare chord counts under compatible smoothing and prove Hausdorff convergence to the smooth transform.

papers.title: No infinite spin in the $n$-body problem in all dimensions
papers.abstract:
In the planar $n$-body problem, Moeckel and Montgomery \cite{MM25} showed that there is no infinite spin for total collision solutions, when the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Following their approach, generalizations have been obtained for partial collision solutions and parabolic solutions in the planar case, and for total collision solutions in the spatial cases by various authors, all under the same assumption that the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration.
  Here we prove there is no infinite spin for any collision or parabolic solution in all dimensions without such an assumption.

papers.title: Integrating Learning and Optimization for Open Transport Capacity Pooling under Disruption
papers.authors: Yujia Xu, Walid Klibi, Benoit Montreuil
papers.abstract: Disruptions can leave logistics networks short of capacity, yet outside capacity is hard to use: incumbent models are private, provider records are incomplete, and offers stay hidden until a costly request for quotation (RFQ). We introduce open capacity pooling as a budgeted provider-discovery problem that links which capacity need to pursue, whom to contact, and which verified offer to admit. The alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) coordinates incumbents without sharing models, and the resulting capacity gaps direct discovery. A machine-learning layer fitted before search ranks providers by predicted capability and a fleet-size proxy from directory records and large language model (LLM) readings of self-descriptions. Verification reveals offers, reduced-cost screening admits them, and re-optimization updates the gaps and prices. Under fixed offers and exact coordination, a full-revelation reference reaches the finite-universe optimum, while budgeted discovery remains heuristic. We evaluate the mechanism on 4,509 real firms in three US regions excluded from predictor training, using scenarios calibrated to seven historical disruptions and simulated availability, offered quantities, and prices. With 80 RFQs, about 1% of exhaustive search, the mechanism recovers 19-43% of the full-information value of outside transport, against 2-6% for random search, and saves USD 73,000-104,000 per event before search and contracting costs. At tight RFQ budgets, gap-guided need selection and learned ranking are complements in these testbeds. LLM reading helps rank capabilities that records omit, such as refrigerated service, but its operating value varies by region. The results support combining record-based learning with coordination-derived gaps under limited search budgets.

papers.title: The edge case of the Hilbert matrix operator between weighted Bergman spaces
papers.abstract:
The Hilbert matrix operator $H$ is bounded on the standard weighted Bergman spaces $A^p_\alpha,\, p>\alpha+2>1$. We examine the limiting case when $\alpha=p-2$, and for $p\leq 2$, we characterize the logarithmic modification of the standard weight needed for the domain $A^p_{v_{\gamma,p}}$ and codomain $A^p_{v_{\beta,p}}$ to ensure boundedness. In particular, we prove that $H:A^2_{\log^\gamma} \to A^2_{\log^\beta}$ is bounded if and only if $\gamma-\beta\geq 2$ and $\gamma>1$, solving an open problem posed by B. Karapetrovi\'c and M. Jevti\'c. We also settle the situation for $p>2$ in all cases, except when the logarithmic exponents $\gamma$ and $\beta$ satisfy $\gamma-\beta=p$.
  Moreover, we completely solve the same problem when the domain and codomain are certain weighted reflexive $\ell^p$ spaces. All results are extended to the generalized Hilbert operator $H_g$.

papers.title: A power-commutator presentation for the group of truncated polynomials under substitution
papers.abstract: Given a prime $p$, the Nottingham group $G(p)$ is the group of formal power series $x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3+\cdots$, $a_i\in{\bf Z}/p{\bf Z}$, under substitution. For $n\geq 1$, we write $G_n(p)$ for the quotient of $G(p)$ by its normal subgroup $K_n=\{x+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+a_{n+2}x^{n+2}+\cdots\,|\, a_i\in {\bf Z}/p{\bf Z}\}$, namely the group of truncated polynomials $x+a_2x^2+\cdots+a_nx^n$, $a_i\in {\bf Z}/p{\bf Z}$, under substitution, which is a $p$-group of order $p^{n-1}$ generated by $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^n$. In this paper, we determine the power-commutator presentation of $G_{15}(p)$ relative to $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^{15}$. This, in turn, automatically gives the power-commutator presentation of $G_{n}(p)$ relative to $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^{n}$ for any $1\leq n<15$, as well as the initial segments of the power and commutator relations in $G_{n}(p)$ corresponding to $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^{15}$ for any $n>15$.

papers.title: A natural Chow lemma for smooth threefolds and fourfolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth proper integral variety of dimension at most four over a field of characteristic zero. We construct a finite sequence of blowups along smooth centers with projective endpoint, preserving the intersection of all maximal quasi-projective opens of $X$. The construction depends only on a fixed functorial principalization procedure and is natural under isomorphisms, including those over different ground fields. The proof has two parts. A colength argument on regular local surfaces gives, in every dimension, a finite preparation after which some maximal quasi-projective open has complement mapping into codimension at least three in $X$. In dimensions at most four these images are points or curves. Ample numerical classes on the normalized components of that complement give finite bounds for summing base ideals of linear systems. The resulting ideal descends to the original field; geometric integrality is not required.

papers.title: Local Fan-type obstructions and Ore-type conditions for rainbow Hamiltonicity in graph systems
papers.abstract:
Let $G=(G_1,...,G_n)$ be a graph system on a common $n$-vertex set $V$. For $v\in V$, set \[
  \delta(v)=\min_{i\in[n]}d_{G_i}(v),
  \qquad
  E_{\cap}=\bigcap_{i=1}^n E(G_i), \] and let $d^c(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest rainbow $u$--$v$ path. We study Hamiltonicity conditions imposed only on pairs at small rainbow distance. Suppose that every $G_i$ is $2$-connected and that \[
  \delta(u),\delta(v)<\frac n2,
  \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  uv\in E_{\cap}. \] Our main result shows that any system satisfying this local Fan-type condition but containing no rainbow Hamilton cycle must satisfy \[
  E_{\cap}=\varnothing,
  \qquad
  \sum_{v\in V}\delta(v)\le\frac{n^2-1}{2}. \] Consequently, either $E_{\cap}\ne\varnothing$ or $\sum_{v\in V}\delta(v)\ge\lceil n^2/2\rceil$ guarantees a rainbow Hamilton cycle. We further prove that the local Ore-type condition \[
  \delta(u)+\delta(v)<n,
  \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  uv\in E_{\cap} \] already forces a rainbow Hamilton cycle. Along the way, the Fan-type hypothesis yields a rainbow Hamilton path and a rainbow $(n-1)$-cycle. For diagonal systems, our conditions reduce to the classical Fan and local Ore conditions. The proofs combine rainbow rotation--extension with a double-counting argument in an auxiliary digraph.
  Keywords: graph system; rainbow Hamilton cycle; rainbow distance; Fan-type condition; Ore-type condition; rotation--extension.

papers.title: H\"older regularity for metric Anosov flows
papers.abstract: We define a class of flows on compact metric spaces that we call $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows, $0 < \alpha < 1$ or $\alpha = \mathrm{Lip}$. We give verifiable criteria for a metric Anosov flow to be $C^\alpha$. We show that $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows have H\"older continuous local product structure, and in particular H\"older continuous holonomies. We deduce that topological conjugacies between $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows are automatically H\"older continuous. We show that any $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flow admits a strong (i.e. H\"older continuous) Markov coding. This yields strong ergodic properties for equilibrium states for H\"older potentials for transitive $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows. The regularity of the local product structure is proved in a non-compact setting which applies for the geodesic flow on the universal cover of a locally CAT(-1) space. This allows us to obtain H\"older regularity results for the holonomy maps for pinched negative curvature manifolds with respect to the Sasaki metric. This contrasts with the result of Ballmann, Brin and Burns that there are examples in this class for which the dynamical distributions are not H\"older.

papers.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
papers.abstract: We study Galois coinvariants of the geometric \'etale fundamental group and \'etale cohomology of varieties over a finitely generated field $k$. We establish finiteness properties of these coinvariants for (possibly infinite) Galois extensions $L/k$ such that $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As applications, we obtain finiteness results for $L$-rational torsion points on abelian varieties and \'etale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over number fields.

papers.title: Ray class groups in the cyclotomic tower
papers.abstract:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty finite set of rational primes different from $p$. In the cyclotomic tower $\mathbb{Q}(\mu_{p^{n+1}})$, we determine the kernels of the natural maps from the minus $p$-primary ray class groups, with modulus the product of the primes above $\Sigma$, to the corresponding ordinary minus $p$-primary class groups. We give their character components and elementary divisors at every finite layer, including the layers before splitting stabilizes. In the norm inverse limit, we obtain an explicit integral cyclic decomposition of the local module modulo the single diagonal global Tate module. Its coinvariants recover the finite local kernels. Together with ordinary class-group control, this gives exact control for the minus ray class groups.
  We identify the local Frobenius factors with Bernoulli regularization factors. For nonexceptional characters, the classical main conjecture then yields regularized measure generators of the ray class characteristic ideals. The exceptional Teichm\"uller component is treated without the main conjecture: the single Tate correction corresponds to the single pole of the $p$-adic zeta function. At the bottom layer, the local calculation and Herbrand--Ribet yield characterwise nonvanishing criteria involving regularized Bernoulli values. For a single auxiliary prime, the exceptional component detects the Wieferich condition. We also deduce Eisenstein congruence consequences from existing modular-form theorems.

papers.title: Strong Invariance Principle for Random Dirichlet Series
papers.abstract: It is shown that the random prime Dirichlet series $ X(s)=\sum_{p\in \mathcal{P}}\frac{\xi_p}{p^{s+1/2}} $ can be almost surely approximated by a Brownian motion, where $ \{\xi_p\}_{p\ge 1} $ are independent and identically distributed random variables with zero mean and finite variance, and $ \mathcal{P} $ is the set of prime numbers. As a consequence, the functional law of the iterated logarithm, limit laws of the iterated logarithm, and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for $ X(s) $ are obtained. It is also shown that the random Dirichlet series $ Y(s)=\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} \frac{(\log k)^{\alpha}}{k^{s+1/2}} $ with $ \alpha=-1/2 $ admits the same approximation as $ X(s) $, and a direct relationship between $ X(s) $ and $ Y(s) $ with $ \alpha=-1/2 $ is established. The strong invariance principle for $ Y(s) $ with $ \alpha>-1/2 $ is also obtained.

papers.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,\Phi)$ with $(E,\Phi)\cong(E,-\Phi)$. For a complex reductive group $G$ realized as a self-adjoint subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, we show that if $(E,\Phi)$ corresponds to a representation $\rho$ of $\pi_1(\Sigma)$, then $(E,-\Phi)$ corresponds to $(\overline{\rho}^{\,t})^{-1}$. As a consequence, the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles is the fixed locus of an involution of the character variety and carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. For a connected semisimple group and every topological type, we prove that the reversible locus in the smooth moduli space is a $(B,A,A)$-brane. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $\eta\mapsto-\eta$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.

papers.title: The Big Match under translation-invariant charges
papers.abstract: We study finite two-player zero-sum stochastic games in which the stream of expected stage payoffs is evaluated by a translation-invariant charge on the set of stages. Every patient valuation, that is, every diffuse charge that obeys the time value of money principle, is translation-invariant. By Mertens and Neyman (1981), every finite two-player zero-sum stochastic game has a value; in particular, each player has, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a strategy that is $\varepsilon$-optimal for all patient valuations simultaneously. We show that this robustness breaks down for translation-invariant charges, even when the charge is fixed in advance. In the Big Match with $0$--$1$ payoffs, for every charge, Player~2 can guarantee that Player~1's payoff is at most $1/2$, but cannot guarantee any smaller bound. Nevertheless, we construct a fixed translation-invariant charge such that, for every strategy of Player~1 and every $\delta>0$, Player~2 has a pure reply yielding payoff less than $\delta$. Consequently, the Big Match has no value under this charge. More generally, the supremum of the payoffs that Player~1 can guarantee ranges over $[0,1/2]$ as the translation-invariant charge varies.
